title.zh: 卷19 志第14 天文上
title.raw: 卷19 志第14 天文上 Volume 19 Treatises 14: Astronomy 1

sentences.zh: 若夫法紫微以居中，擬明堂而布政，依分野而命國，體眾星而效官，動必順時，教不違物，故能成變化之道，合陰陽之妙。

translations.literal: As for modeling the Purple Palace to stand at the center, taking the Bright Hall as a pattern for dispensing government, assigning states according to territorial divisions, and taking the multitude of stars as the model for offices—acting always in accord with the seasons and teaching without violating the nature of things—thus one can accomplish the Way of transformation and harmonize with the subtlety of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's order mirrors earthly rule: the Purple Palace stands at the center as the emperor's seat, the Bright Hall models the distribution of government, territorial divisions assign each state its place, and the stars map the hierarchy of offices. When action follows the seasons and instruction respects the nature of things, the Way of transformation is fulfilled and yin and yang work in harmony.

sentences.zh: 爰在庖犧，仰觀俯察，謂以天之七曜、二十八星，周於穹圓之度，以麗十二位也。

translations.literal: Already in the time of Fuxi, looking up and looking down, it was said that the seven luminaries of Heaven and the twenty-eight asterisms circle the degrees of the vaulted dome to adorn the twelve positions.
translations.idiomatic: As early as Fuxi, through observation above and inquiry below, it was held that Heaven's seven luminaries and twenty-eight asterisms traverse the arc of the celestial vault to mark the twelve terrestrial positions.

sentences.zh: 在天成象，示見吉凶。

translations.literal: In Heaven forms take shape, revealing fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven forms images that portend good and ill.

sentences.zh: 五緯入房，啓姬王之肇跡，長星孛斗，鑒宋人之首亂，天意人事，同乎影響。

translations.literal: When the five planets entered the Chamber, they opened the first traces of the Zhou kings; when a long comet bristled at the Dipper, it mirrored the Song people's first rebellion—Heaven's intent and human affairs respond like shadow to form.
translations.idiomatic: The five planets entering the Chamber heralded the Zhou dynasty's rise; a long-tailed comet at the Dipper foreshadowed the Song's first revolt. Heaven's will and human affairs mirror each other as closely as shadow and substance.

sentences.zh: 自夷王下堂而見諸侯，赧王登臺而避責，《記》曰：「天子微，諸侯僭。

translations.literal: From King Yi descending the hall to receive the feudal lords, to King Nan ascending the tower to evade blame, the Record says: "The Son of Heaven grows weak, the feudal lords grow arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: From King Yi of Zhou descending the hall to meet the feudal lords, to King Nan mounting the tower to shirk responsibility, the Record says: "The Son of Heaven wanes and the feudal lords usurp their prerogatives.

sentences.zh: 」於是師兵吞滅，僵僕原野。

translations.literal: " Then armies swallowed one another and corpses littered the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Armies then devoured one another, and the dead lay strewn across the fields.

sentences.zh: 秦氏以戰國之餘，怙茲凶暴，小星交鬭，長彗橫天。

translations.literal: The House of Qin, relying on the residue of the Warring States, trusted in this brutal violence; lesser stars crossed in battle, and a long comet stretched across the sky.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin, inheritors of the Warring States' violence, leaned on brutal force; lesser stars clashed in the heavens and a long comet swept the sky.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖驅駕英雄，墾除災害，五精從歲，七重暈畢，含樞曾緬，道不虛行。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han drove forth heroes and cleared away calamity; the five bright planets followed Jupiter, a sevenfold halo ringed the Net, the Pivot held fast at the center—Heaven's Way does not move in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu rallied heroes and swept away disaster; the five planets marched with Jupiter, a sevenfold halo encircled the Net, and the celestial Pivot held its place—the Way of Heaven does not act without purpose.

sentences.zh: 自西京創制，多歷年載。

translations.literal: From the founding of the Western Capital, many years passed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Western Capital was established, many years elapsed.

sentences.zh: 世祖中興，當塗馭物，金行水德，祗奉靈命，玄兆著明，天人不遠。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor restored the dynasty, he took the reins at the right moment; the Metal phase and Water virtue received the numinous mandate—dark omens shone clear, and Heaven and man were not far apart.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu restored the Han, he seized the moment to rule; Metal and Water received the sacred mandate, dark portents appeared plainly, and Heaven and humanity stood in close accord.

sentences.zh: 昔者榮河獻籙，溫洛呈圖，六爻摛範，三光宛備，則星官之書，自黃帝始。

translations.literal: Formerly at the Glory of the River a chart was presented, at the Warmth of the Luo a diagram appeared, the six lines unfolded their pattern, and the three luminaries were fully arrayed—then the book of star officials began with the Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the chart was offered at the Glory of the River and the diagram at the Warmth of the Luo, the six lines revealed their pattern and sun, moon, and stars stood complete—the annals of star officials thus begin with the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 高陽氏使南正重司天，北正黎司地，帝堯乃命羲、和，欽若昊天。

translations.literal: Gaoyang Shi made the Southern Regulator Chong oversee Heaven and the Northern Regulator Li oversee Earth; Emperor Yao then commanded Xi and He to reverently conform to the vast Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuanxu appointed the Southern Regulator Chong to govern Heaven and the Northern Regulator Li to govern Earth; Emperor Yao then charged Xi and He to reverently align themselves with the great Heaven.

sentences.zh: 夏有昆吾，殷有巫咸，周之史佚，宋之子韋，魯之梓慎，鄭之裨灶，魏有石氏，齊有甘公，皆能言天文、察微變者也。

translations.literal: Xia had Kunwu, Yin had Wu Xian, Zhou had the historiographer Yi, Song had Zi Wei, Lu had Zi Shen, Zheng had Pi Zao, Wei had the Shi clan, and Qi had Duke Gan—all were able to speak of astronomy and discern subtle changes.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia had Kunwu, the Yin had Wu Xian, the Zhou historiographer Yi, Song's Zi Wei, Lu's Zi Shen, Zheng's Pi Zao, Wei's Shi clan, and Qi's Duke Gan—all masters of astronomy who could read subtle celestial changes.

sentences.zh: 漢之傳天數者，則有唐都、李尋之倫。

translations.literal: Those who transmitted Heaven's numbers in Han included Tang Du, Li Xun, and their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han transmitters of celestial reckoning were Tang Du, Li Xun, and others of their company.

sentences.zh: 光武時，則有蘇伯况、郎雅光，並能參伍天文，發揚善道，補益當時，監垂來世。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Guangwu there were Su Bo Kuang and Lang Ya Guang, both able to compare and coordinate astronomical matters, expound the good Way, benefit their age, and set a standard for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangwu, Su Bo Kuang and Lang Ya Guang could cross-check astronomical data, advance the proper doctrine, serve their own age, and leave a model for posterity.

sentences.zh: 而河、洛圖緯，雖有星占星官之名，未能盡列。

translations.literal: Yet though the charts and weft-texts of the River and Luo had the names of star diviners and star officials, they could not list them all completely.
translations.idiomatic: Even the River and Luo charts and apocryphal texts named star diviners and star officials, yet could not enumerate them fully.

sentences.zh: 後漢張衡為太史令，鑄渾天儀，總序經星，謂之《靈憲》。

translations.literal: Later, in the Eastern Han, Zhang Heng served as Grand Astrologer, cast the armillary sphere, and arranged the fixed stars in order, calling it the Ling Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Han, Zhang Heng as Grand Astrologer cast an armillary sphere, catalogued the fixed stars, and titled the work Ling Xian.

sentences.zh: 其大略曰：「星也者，體生於地，精發於天。

translations.literal: Its general outline says: "Stars—their bodies arise from Earth, their essence issues in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Its summary runs: "Stars have bodies born from Earth and essence radiating in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 紫宮為帝皇之居，太微為五帝之坐，在野象物，在朝象官。

translations.literal: The Purple Palace is the dwelling of the emperor, the Supreme Palace the seat of the Five Emperors; in the wilds they image things, at court they image offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Purple Palace is the emperor's residence, the Supreme Palace the seat of the Five Emperors; beyond the court they mirror things, within the court they mirror offices.

sentences.zh: 居其中央，謂之北斗，動系於占，實司王命。

translations.literal: Occupying the center among them is what is called the Northern Dipper; its movements are tied to divination and it truly governs the royal mandate.
translations.idiomatic: At their center stands the Northern Dipper; its motion governs divination and truly holds the royal mandate in charge.

sentences.zh: 四布于方，為二十八星，日月運行，曆示休咎。

translations.literal: Spread in four directions are the twenty-eight asterisms; sun and moon travel their courses and mark out blessing and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-eight asterisms spread across the four quarters; as sun and moon run their paths they reveal fortune and disaster.

sentences.zh: 五緯經次，用彰禍福，則上天之心，於是見矣。

translations.literal: The five planets pass in sequence, making misfortune and blessing manifest—then the heart of High Heaven is seen.
translations.idiomatic: The five planets move in their ordained sequence, displaying calamity and blessing—and thus the mind of Heaven is revealed.

sentences.zh: 中外之官，常明者百有二十，可名者三百二十，為星二千五百；

translations.literal: Of the inner and outer officials, those constantly bright number one hundred and twenty; those that can be named, three hundred and twenty; as stars, two thousand five hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Among the inner and outer star-offices, one hundred and twenty shine constantly, three hundred and twenty bear names, and as individual stars they number two thousand five hundred;

sentences.zh: 微星之數萬一千五百二十，庶物蠢動，咸得繫命。

translations.literal: faint stars number slightly more than eleven thousand five hundred and twenty—all moving creatures receive their allotted fates thereby.
translations.idiomatic: faint stars slightly exceed eleven thousand five hundred and twenty—in this way every living thing has its fate bound.

sentences.zh: 」而衡所鑄之圖，遇亂堙滅，星官名數，今亦不存。

translations.literal: " But the chart Heng cast was lost in the turmoil, and the names and numbers of the star officials are not preserved today.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the chart Heng cast was buried in the chaos of war, and the names and counts of the star officials no longer survive.

sentences.zh: 三國時，吳太史令陳卓，始列甘氏、石氏、巫咸三家星官，著於圖錄。

translations.literal: In the Three Kingdoms period, Chen Zhuo, Grand Astrologer of Wu, first arranged the star officials of the Gan, Shi, and Wu Xian traditions and recorded them in charts and registers.
translations.idiomatic: During the Three Kingdoms, Wu's Grand Astrologer Chen Zhuo first compiled the star officials of the Gan, Shi, and Wu Xian schools into charts and catalogues.

sentences.zh: 并注占贊，總有二百五十四官，一千二百八十三星，並二十八宿及輔官附坐一百八十二星，總二百八十三官，一千五百六十五星。

translations.literal: He also appended divinatory commentary, totaling two hundred fifty-four offices, one thousand two hundred eighty-three stars, together with the twenty-eight lodges and attendant offices with one hundred eighty-two seated stars—in all two hundred eighty-three offices and one thousand five hundred sixty-five stars.
translations.idiomatic: Adding divinatory notes, he recorded two hundred fifty-four offices and one thousand two hundred eighty-three stars, plus the twenty-eight lodges and their attendant seats with one hundred eighty-two stars—two hundred eighty-three offices and one thousand five hundred sixty-five stars in all.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，太史令錢樂之所鑄渾天銅儀，以硃黑白三色，用殊三家，而合陳卓之數。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Liu Song, Grand Astrologer Qian Lezhi cast a bronze armillary sphere, using cinnabar, black, and white to distinguish the three schools while matching Chen Zhuo's totals.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Song's Yuanjia reign, Grand Astrologer Qian Lezhi cast a bronze armillary sphere, marking the three schools in red, black, and white while conforming to Chen Zhuo's counts.

sentences.zh: 高祖平陳，得善天官者周墳，並得宋氏渾儀之器。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu pacified Chen, he obtained the skilled celestial officer Zhou Fen, and also acquired the armillary instruments of the Song house.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu conquered Chen, he gained the adept celestial officer Zhou Fen and recovered the Song dynasty's armillary instruments.

sentences.zh: 乃命庾季才等，參校周、齊、梁、陳及祖暅、孫僧化官私舊圖，刊其大小，正彼疏密，依准三家星位，以為蓋圖。

translations.literal: He then ordered Yu Ji Cai and others to collate the official and private old charts of Zhou, Qi, Liang, Chen, Zu Geng, and Sun Seng Hua, adjust their large and small scales, correct their sparse and dense placements, and take the star positions of the three schools as the standard for a canopy chart.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yu Ji Cai and others to collate old charts from Zhou, Qi, Liang, Chen, Zu Geng, and Sun Seng Hua—public and private—adjusting scale, correcting density, and using the three schools' star positions as the basis for a canopy chart.

sentences.zh: 旁摛始分，甄表常度，並具赤黃二道，內外兩規。

translations.literal: Along the sides the initial divisions were set out, tables marked the regular degrees, and both the red and yellow paths and the inner and outer circles were fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: Initial divisions were laid out at the margins, standard degrees tabulated, and both the red and yellow paths with inner and outer circles were included.

sentences.zh: 懸象著明，纏離攸次，星之隱顯，天漢昭回，宛若穹蒼，將為正範。

translations.literal: The suspended images shone clear, the entwined separations took their order, stars' hiding and appearing and the Milky Way's winding return—all like the vaulted azure, to serve as the correct model.
translations.idiomatic: Suspended stars stood plain, lodge boundaries fell in order, stars waxed and waned, and the Milky Way wound back like the vault of sky itself—a standard for correct reckoning.

sentences.zh: 以墳為太史令。

translations.literal: Fen was appointed Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fen was made Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 墳博考經書，勤於教習，自此太史觀生，始能識天官。

translations.literal: Fen broadly examined the classics and diligently instructed; from this the students of the Astrological Bureau began to recognize the celestial offices.
translations.idiomatic: Fen studied the classics exhaustively and taught with diligence; from then on the Astrological Bureau's trainees could identify the celestial offices.

sentences.zh: 煬帝又遣宮人四十人，就太史局，別詔袁充，教以星氣，業成者進內，以參占驗云。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang also sent forty palace women to the Astrological Bureau and separately commanded Yuan Chong to teach them star qi; those who completed the training entered the inner palace to assist in divination and verification.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang dispatched forty palace women to the Astrological Bureau and separately ordered Yuan Chong to instruct them in star qi; graduates entered the inner palace to aid in divination.

sentences.zh: 史臣於觀臺訪渾儀，見元魏太史令晁崇所造者，以鐵為之，其規有六。

translations.literal: The historiographer, visiting the observatory platform to inspect the armillary sphere, saw the one cast by Chao Chong, Grand Astrologer of Northern Wei, made of iron with six circles.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer, examining the armillary sphere at the observatory, found the instrument cast by Northern Wei Grand Astrologer Chao Chong—iron, with six rings.

sentences.zh: 其外四規常定，一象地形，二象赤道，其餘象二極。

translations.literal: Of the outer four circles, four were fixed—one imaging the terrain, one the equator, and the rest the two poles.
translations.idiomatic: Four of the outer six rings were fixed: one representing terrain, one the equator, and the remainder the two celestial poles.

sentences.zh: 其內二規，可以運轉，用合八尺之管，以窺星度。

translations.literal: The inner two circles could rotate, used together with an eight-foot tube to sight star degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The inner two rings rotated, paired with an eight-foot sighting tube to measure stellar degrees.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊所得。

translations.literal: It was obtained when Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou conquered Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Emperor Wu acquired it when he conquered Qi.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇三年，新都初成，以置諸觀臺之上。

translations.literal: In the third year of Sui Kaihuang, when the new capital was first completed, it was placed atop the observatory platform.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui Kaihuang year 3, when the new capital was finished, the instrument was installed on the observatory platform.

sentences.zh: 大唐因而用焉。

translations.literal: The Great Tang continued to use it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang dynasty continued to employ it.

sentences.zh: 馬遷《天官書》及班氏所載，妖星暈珥，雲氣虹霓，存其大綱，未能備舉。

translations.literal: Ma Qian's Treatise on the Celestial Offices and Ban's record preserve the broad outline of strange stars, halos and spurs, cloud vapors, rainbows, and secondary rainbows, but cannot list them all.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian's Treatise on the Celestial Offices and Ban Gu's account give the broad categories of prodigious stars, halos, spurs, cloud vapors, and rainbows, but do not enumerate every form.

sentences.zh: 自後史官，更無紀錄。

translations.literal: Afterward the historiographers made no further records.
translations.idiomatic: Later historiographers kept no further records.

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：「公既視朔，遂登觀臺，凡分至啓閉，必書雲物。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "After the duke had performed the new-moon sacrifice, he then ascended the observatory platform—for every solstice, equinox, and seasonal gate, cloud phenomena were always recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: "After performing the new-moon sacrifice, the duke ascended the observatory—for each solstice, equinox, and seasonal commencement, cloud signs were duly written down.

sentences.zh: 」神道司存，安可誣也！

translations.literal: " The numinous Way has its keeper—how could it be falsely reported!
translations.idiomatic: The numinous Way has its officers—how could such things be fabricated!

sentences.zh: 今略舉其形名占驗，次之經星之末云。

translations.literal: Now I briefly set forth their forms, names, and divinatory verification, placing them after the fixed stars.
translations.idiomatic: Here I briefly list their forms, names, and divinatory tests, appending them after the section on fixed stars.

sentences.zh: ○天體

translations.literal: The Body of Heaven
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Body

sentences.zh: 古之言天者有三家，一曰蓋天，二曰宣夜，三曰渾天。

translations.literal: Those who spoke of Heaven in antiquity had three schools: first, Canopy Heaven; second, Overnight Heaven; third, Spherical Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient cosmologists recognized three schools: Canopy Heaven, Overnight Heaven, and Spherical Heaven.

sentences.zh: 蓋天之說，即《周髀》是也。

translations.literal: The theory of Canopy Heaven is that of the Zhou Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Canopy Heaven theory is set forth in the Zhou Bi.

sentences.zh: 其本庖犧氏立周天曆度，其所傳則周公受于殷商，周人志之，故曰《周髀》。

translations.literal: Its origin lies in Fuxi's establishment of the degrees of the circuit of Heaven; what was transmitted passed from the Shang to the Duke of Zhou, and the Zhou people recorded it—hence it is called the Zhou Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi first established the degrees of Heaven's circuit; the tradition passed from Shang to the Duke of Zhou, and the Zhou recorded it—hence Zhou Bi, "Zhou Gnomon."

sentences.zh: 髀，股也；

translations.literal: Bi means thigh;
translations.idiomatic: Bi means thigh—

sentences.zh: 股者，表也。

translations.literal: the thigh is the gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: the thigh serves as the measuring post.

sentences.zh: 其言天似蓋笠，地法覆槃，天地各中高外下。

translations.literal: It says Heaven is like an inverted bowl and Earth like an overturned dish—Heaven and Earth each high in the center and low at the edges.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven resembles an inverted bowl, Earth an upturned dish—each highest at the center and sloping downward at the rim.

sentences.zh: 北極之下，為天地之中，其地最高，而滂沲四蕆，三光隱映，以為晝夜。

translations.literal: Below the North Pole is the center of Heaven and Earth; that land is highest, and waters pour out in four directions; the three luminaries hide and shine, making day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the North Pole lies the center of Heaven and Earth, where the land stands highest; waters spill outward on all sides, and the three luminaries alternately hide and shine to create day and night.

sentences.zh: 天中高於外衡冬至日之所在六萬里，北極下地高於外衡下地亦六萬里，外衡高於北極下地二萬里。

translations.literal: Heaven at the center is sixty thousand li higher than the outer circle at the winter solstice sun's position; the North Pole's land is sixty thousand li higher than the land beneath the outer circle, and the outer circle is twenty thousand li higher than the land beneath the North Pole.
translations.idiomatic: At the center Heaven rises sixty thousand li above the outer ring where the winter solstice sun stands; land under the North Pole stands sixty thousand li above land under the outer ring, while the outer ring itself stands twenty thousand li above the land beneath the North Pole.

sentences.zh: 天地隆高相從，日去地恆八萬里。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth rise high in parallel, and the sun is constantly eighty thousand li from Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth rise together in parallel, and the sun always stands eighty thousand li from Earth.

sentences.zh: 日麗天而平轉，分冬夏之間日所行道為七衡六間。

translations.literal: The sun clings to Heaven and turns level; between winter and summer the path the sun travels forms seven circles and six intervals.
translations.idiomatic: The sun rides Heaven and revolves evenly; between winter and summer its path forms seven rings and six intervals.

sentences.zh: 每衡周徑裡數，各依算術，用句股重差，推晷影極遊，以為遠近之數，皆得於表股也，故曰《周髀》。

translations.literal: The circuit diameter of each ring follows arithmetic reckoning; using right triangles and double differences, one infers gnomon shadows and polar motion to determine distances—all obtained from the gnomon post—hence Zhou Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Each ring's circumference and diameter follow arithmetical calculation; by gnomon shadows and double-difference triangulation one derives distances of extreme motion—all from the measuring post—hence the name Zhou Bi.

sentences.zh: 又《周髀》家云：「天圓如張蓋，地方如棋局。

translations.literal: The Zhou Bi school also says: "Heaven is round like an spread canopy, Earth square like a chessboard.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Bi school also holds: "Heaven is round like an opened canopy; Earth is square like a chessboard.

sentences.zh: 天旁轉如推磨而左行，日月右行，天左轉，故日月實東行，而天牽之以西沒。

translations.literal: Heaven turns at the side like a millstone grinding to the left; sun and moon move to the right—Heaven turns left, so though sun and moon truly move eastward, Heaven drags them to set in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven rotates sideways like a millstone turning left; sun and moon move rightward. Heaven turns left, so though sun and moon truly travel east, Heaven pulls them westward to set.

sentences.zh: 譬之於蟻行磨石之上，磨左旋而蟻右去，磨疾而蟻遲，故不得不隨磨以左回焉。

translations.literal: It is like an ant crawling on a millstone— the stone turns left while the ant goes right; the stone is fast and the ant slow, so the ant cannot but wheel left with the stone.
translations.idiomatic: Like an ant on a turning millstone: the stone spins left while the ant crawls right; the stone outpaces the ant, so the ant is carried leftward with it.

sentences.zh: 天形南高而北下，日出高故見，日入下故不見。

translations.literal: Heaven's form is high in the south and low in the north; the sun rises from the high and so is seen, and sets in the low and so is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven slopes high in the south and low in the north; the sun rises from the heights and becomes visible, and sets in the depths and disappears.

sentences.zh: 天之居如倚蓋，故極在人北，是其證也。

translations.literal: Heaven's position is like a leaning canopy, so the pole is north of man—this is the proof.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven rests like a tilted canopy, placing the pole north of the observer—this is the evidence.

sentences.zh: 極在天之中，而今在人北，所以知天之形如倚蓋也。

translations.literal: The pole is at Heaven's center, yet now it is north of man—by this one knows Heaven's form is like a leaning canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The pole stands at Heaven's center, yet appears north of us—whence we know Heaven's shape resembles a tilted canopy.

sentences.zh: 日朝出陰中，暮入陰中，陰氣暗冥，故從沒不見也。

translations.literal: The sun emerges from yin at dawn and enters yin at dusk; yin qi is dark and obscure, so from setting it is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the sun rises from yin; at dusk it enters yin again. Yin qi is dark, so once it sets the sun vanishes from sight.

sentences.zh: 夏時陽氣多，陰氣少，陽氣光明，與日同暉，故日出即見，無蔽之者，故夏日長也。

translations.literal: In summer yang qi is abundant and yin qi scarce; yang qi is bright and shares radiance with the sun, so at rising it is seen with nothing to hide it—thus summer days are long.
translations.idiomatic: In summer yang prevails and yin is sparse; yang shines bright and shares the sun's light, so at sunrise nothing obscures it—hence long summer days.

sentences.zh: 冬時陰氣多，陽氣少，陰氣暗冥，掩日之光，雖出猶隱不見，故冬日短也。

translations.literal: In winter yin qi is abundant and yang qi scarce; yin qi is dark and obscure and masks the sun's light—even when risen it remains hidden—thus winter days are short.
translations.idiomatic: In winter yin prevails and yang is sparse; dark yin shrouds the sun's light, so even after rising it stays concealed—hence short winter days.

sentences.zh: 漢末，揚子雲難蓋天八事，以通渾天。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Yang Xiong raised eight objections to Canopy Heaven to reconcile it with Spherical Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Han, Yang Xiong posed eight objections to Canopy Heaven theory in favor of Spherical Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其一云：「日之東行，循黃道。

translations.literal: The first says: "The sun travels east along the Yellow Path.
translations.idiomatic: The first objection: "The sun moves east along the Yellow Path.

sentences.zh: 晝夜中規，牽牛距北極南百一十度，東井距北極南七十度，並百八十度。

translations.literal: At midday it fits the compass; Oxherd is one hundred ten degrees south of the North Pole, Well one hundred ten degrees south of the North Pole—together one hundred eighty degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At noon it bisects the horizon; Oxherd lies one hundred ten degrees south of the North Pole, Well seventy degrees south—one hundred eighty degrees together.

sentences.zh: 週三徑一，二十八宿周天當五百四十度，今三百六十度，何也？

translations.literal: Circumference three, diameter one—the twenty-eight lodges should circuit five hundred forty degrees, yet now it is three hundred sixty degrees—why?
translations.idiomatic: With circumference thrice the diameter, the twenty-eight lodges should span five hundred forty degrees, yet they span only three hundred sixty—why?

sentences.zh: 」其二曰：「春秋分之日正出在卯，入在酉，而晝漏五十刻。

translations.literal: " The second says: "On the days of the spring and autumn equinoxes the sun rises due east at mao and sets due west at you, and the daylight clepsydra reads fifty marks.
translations.idiomatic: The second: "At the equinoxes the sun rises at mao due east and sets at you due west, with fifty marks of daylight.

sentences.zh: 即天蓋轉，夜當倍晝。

translations.literal: If the canopy of Heaven turns, night should be twice day.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven's canopy rotates, night should be twice as long as day.

sentences.zh: 今夜亦五十刻，何也？

translations.literal: Yet tonight is also fifty marks—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet tonight too runs fifty marks—why?

sentences.zh: 」其三曰：「日入而星見，日出而不見，即斗下見日六月，不見日六月。

translations.literal: " The third says: "When the sun sets stars appear; when the sun rises they are not seen—thus below the Dipper the sun is seen six months and not seen six months.
translations.idiomatic: The third: "Stars appear at sunset and vanish at sunrise—below the Dipper the sun is visible six months and hidden six months.

sentences.zh: 北斗亦當見六月，不見六月。

translations.literal: The Northern Dipper too should be seen six months and not seen six months.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Dipper should likewise be visible six months and hidden six months.

sentences.zh: 今夜常見，何也？

translations.literal: Yet tonight it is always seen—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet it is always visible at night—why?

sentences.zh: 」其四曰：「以蓋圖視天河，起斗而東入狼弧間，曲如輪。

translations.literal: " The fourth says: "Viewing the Milky Way on the canopy chart, it rises from the Dipper and enters eastward between Wolf and Arc—curved like a wheel.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth: "On the canopy chart the Milky Way rises from the Dipper and runs east between Wolf and Arc, curved like a wheel.

sentences.zh: 今視天河直如繩，何也？

translations.literal: Yet now viewing the Milky Way it is straight as a cord—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet viewed directly it runs straight as a cord—why?

sentences.zh: 」其五曰：「周天二十八宿，以蓋圖視天，星見者當少，不見者當多。

translations.literal: " The fifth says: "The twenty-eight lodges circuit Heaven—on the canopy chart, stars seen should be fewer and stars unseen should be more.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth: "The twenty-eight lodges circle Heaven—on the canopy chart, visible stars should be fewer and invisible stars more numerous.

sentences.zh: 今見與不見等，何出入無冬夏，而兩宿十四星當見，不以日長短故見有多少，何也？

translations.literal: Yet now seen and unseen are equal—why, with no winter or summer in rising and setting, are two lodges' fourteen stars always visible, not varying in number because days are long or short—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet seen and unseen are equal—why, with no seasonal change in rising and setting, are fourteen stars of two lodges always visible, unaffected by day length—why?

sentences.zh: 」其六曰：「天至高也，地至卑也。

translations.literal: " The sixth says: "Heaven is highest and Earth is lowest.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth: "Heaven is supremely high and Earth supremely low.

sentences.zh: 日托天而旋，可謂至高矣。

translations.literal: The sun rests on Heaven and revolves—this may be called supremely high.
translations.idiomatic: The sun rides Heaven and revolves—surely this is the highest reach.

sentences.zh: 縱人目可奪，水與影不可奪也。

translations.literal: Though the human eye may be deceived, water and shadow cannot be deceived.
translations.idiomatic: The eye may err, but water and shadow cannot.

sentences.zh: 今從高山上，以水望日，日出水下，影上行，何也？

translations.literal: Yet now from atop a high mountain, viewing the sun in water, when the sun rises it is below the water and the shadow rises above—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet from a high mountain, sighting the sun in water, at sunrise the sun appears below the water while the shadow rises above—why?

sentences.zh: 」其七曰：「視物近則大，遠則小。

translations.literal: " The seventh says: "View objects near and they appear large; far and they appear small.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh: "Near objects look large; distant ones look small.

sentences.zh: 今日與北斗，近我而小，遠我而大，何也？

translations.literal: Yet now the sun and the Northern Dipper—near us they are small, far from us they are large—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sun and Northern Dipper look small when near and large when far—why?

sentences.zh: 」其八曰：「視蓋橑與車輻間，近杠轂即密，益遠益疏。

translations.literal: " The eighth says: "Viewing the canopy rafters and the spaces between chariot spokes, near the axle hub they are dense and farther away increasingly sparse.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth: "Between canopy ribs and chariot spokes, spacing is tight near the hub and grows wider with distance.

sentences.zh: 今北極為天杠轂，二十八宿為天橑輻。

translations.literal: Now the North Pole is Heaven's axle hub and the twenty-eight lodges are Heaven's rafters and spokes.
translations.idiomatic: The North Pole is Heaven's hub; the twenty-eight lodges are its rafters and spokes.

sentences.zh: 以星度度天，南方次地星間當數倍。

translations.literal: Measuring Heaven by star degrees, the intervals between stars in the south next to Earth should be several times greater.
translations.idiomatic: By stellar degrees, star intervals in the south near Earth should be several times wider.

sentences.zh: 今交密，何也？

translations.literal: Yet now they cross densely—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet they crowd together—why?

sentences.zh: 」其後桓譚、鄭玄、蔡邕、陸績，各陳《周髀》考驗天狀，多有所違。

translations.literal: " Afterward Huan Tan, Zheng Xuan, Cai Yong, and Lu Ji each set forth the Zhou Bi and tested the state of Heaven, finding much that did not accord.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huan Tan, Zheng Xuan, Cai Yong, and Lu Ji each examined the Zhou Bi against Heaven's actual state and found much amiss.

sentences.zh: 逮梁武帝于長春殿講義，另擬天體，全同《周髀》之文，蓋立新意，以排渾天之論而已。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang lectured in the Everlasting Spring Hall, he proposed another model of the celestial body identical to the Zhou Bi text—essentially advancing a new idea merely to refute Spherical Heaven theory.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Wudi lectured in the Everlasting Spring Hall, he proposed a celestial model identical to the Zhou Bi—chiefly a new formulation meant to overturn Spherical Heaven.

sentences.zh: 宣夜之書，絕無師法。

translations.literal: Books of the Overnight school have absolutely no transmitted teaching lineage.
translations.idiomatic: No master lineage survives for Overnight Heaven texts.

sentences.zh: 唯漢秘書郎郗萌記先師相傳云：「天了無質，仰而瞻之，高遠無極，眼瞀精絕，故蒼蒼然也。

translations.literal: Only Xi Meng, Secretary of the Han Secretariat, recorded what earlier masters transmitted, saying: "Heaven has no solid substance; looking up at it, it is boundlessly high and far, the eyes dazzled and the spirit exhausted, hence the blue expanse.
translations.idiomatic: Only Han Secretariat officer Xi Meng recorded the oral tradition: "Heaven has no solid body; gazing upward it extends without limit, the eyes dazzled and spirit spent—hence the blue expanse.

sentences.zh: 譬之旁望遠道之黃山而皆青，俯察千仞之深谷而窈黑，夫青非真色，而黑非有體也。

translations.literal: It is like looking sideways at distant Yellow Mountains and seeing all blue, or peering down a thousand-ren chasm and finding deep black—blue is not a true color, and black is not a solid body.
translations.idiomatic: Like seeing distant Yellow Mountains all blue from the side, or a thousand-ren gorge black from above—blue is not true color, black is not solid form.

sentences.zh: 日月眾星，自然浮生虛空之中，其行其止，皆須氣焉。

translations.literal: Sun, moon, and the multitude of stars naturally float in empty space; their going and stopping all depend on qi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and stars naturally float in the void; their motion and rest depend entirely on qi.

sentences.zh: 是以七曜或逝或住，或順或逆，伏見無常，進退不同，由乎無所根系，故各異也。

translations.literal: Thus the seven luminaries sometimes speed and sometimes halt, sometimes advance directly and sometimes retreat; their hiding and appearing are not fixed, their advance and retreat not the same—because they have nothing to which they are tethered, each differs.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the seven luminaries now hurry, now pause, now advance, now retreat; their visibility shifts without rule because nothing anchors them—each moves on its own.

sentences.zh: 故辰極常居其所，而北斗不與眾星西沒也。

translations.literal: Therefore the pole star constantly keeps its place, and the Northern Dipper does not set westward with the other stars.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the pole star holds its station, and the Northern Dipper does not sink westward with the other stars.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康中，會稽虞喜因宣夜之說，作《安天論》，以為「天高窮於無窮，地深測於不測。

translations.literal: In the Xian Kang era of Emperor Cheng of Jin, Yu Xi of Kuaiji, following the Overnight theory, composed the An Tian Lun, holding that "Heaven's height extends to the boundless and Earth's depth measures the immeasurable.
translations.idiomatic: During Jin Chengdi's Xian Kang reign, Yu Xi of Kuaiji, drawing on Overnight Heaven theory, wrote the An Tian Lun, arguing that Heaven stretches endlessly upward and Earth measures immeasurably downward.

sentences.zh: 天確乎在上，有常安之形，地魄焉在下，有居靜之體，當相覆冒，方則俱方，圓則俱圓，無方圓不同之義也。

translations.literal: Heaven firmly stands above with a form of constant rest; Earth's soul rests below with a body of settled dwelling—they should cover and enclose each other, square together if square, round together if round, with no meaning of square and round being different.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven stands firmly above in fixed form; Earth's essence rests below in settled body—they mutually cover and enclose, alike in shape whether square or round, with no asymmetry between them.

sentences.zh: 其光曜布列，各自運行，猶江海之有潮汐，萬品之有行藏也。

translations.literal: Their radiance is spread in array and each runs its own course, like the tides of rivers and seas and the going and hiding of the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Their lights are arrayed and each runs its own path, like ocean tides and the appearing and hiding of all creatures.

sentences.zh: 」葛洪聞而譏之曰：「苟辰宿不麗於天，天為無用，便可言無。

translations.literal: " Ge Hong, hearing this, mocked it, saying: "If the lodges do not cling to Heaven, Heaven is useless and one might as well say it does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong scoffed: "If the lodges do not attach to Heaven, Heaven is useless—one might as well deny it exists.

sentences.zh: 何必復云有之而不動乎？

translations.literal: Why must one again say it exists yet does not move?"
translations.idiomatic: Why insist it exists yet never moves?"

sentences.zh: 」由此而談，葛洪可謂知言之選也。

translations.literal: From this discussion, Ge Hong may be called a master of discerning speech.
translations.idiomatic: On this point Ge Hong showed himself a master of critical judgment.

sentences.zh: 喜族祖河間相聳，又立《穹天論》云：「天形穹隆如雞子幕，其際周接四海之表，浮乎元氣之上。

translations.literal: Xi's clansman, the Chancellor of Hejian, Song, also established the Qiong Tian Lun, saying: "Heaven's form is vaulted like a hen's-egg canopy; its edge circles and joins the outer rim of the four seas, floating upon primordial qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi's kinsman Song, Chancellor of Hejian, proposed the Qiong Tian Lun: "Heaven arches like an egg-shell canopy, its rim joining the outer edge of the four seas, floating on primordial qi.

sentences.zh: 譬如覆奩以抑水而不沒者，氣充其中故也。

translations.literal: It is like covering a casket to press down on water without submerging it—qi fills the interior, hence this.
translations.idiomatic: Like a lid pressed on water that does not sink—because qi fills the space within.

sentences.zh: 日繞辰極，沒西還東，而不出入地中。

translations.literal: The sun circles the pole star, sets in the west and returns east, and does not pass in and out beneath Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The sun orbits the pole, sets west and returns east, never passing beneath Earth.

sentences.zh: 天之有極，猶蓋之有斗也。

translations.literal: Heaven having a pole is like a canopy having a pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's pole is like the hub of a canopy.

sentences.zh: 天北下於地三十度，極之傾在地卯酉之北亦三十度。

translations.literal: Heaven slopes northward below Earth by thirty degrees; the pole's tilt north of Earth at mao and you is also thirty degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven dips thirty degrees below Earth to the north; the pole tilts thirty degrees north of the mao-you line.

sentences.zh: 人在卯酉之南十餘萬里，故斗極之下，不為地中，當對天地卯酉之位耳。

translations.literal: Man stands more than one hundred thousand li south of mao and you, so below the Dipper's pole is not Earth's center but faces the mao-you position between Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Humanity stands over one hundred thousand li south of mao-you, so beneath the Dipper's pole is not Earth's center but the mao-you axis between Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 日行黃道繞極。

translations.literal: The sun travels the Yellow Path circling the pole.
translations.idiomatic: The sun follows the Yellow Path around the pole.

sentences.zh: 極北去黃道百一十五度，南去黃道六十七度，二至之所舍，以為長短也。

translations.literal: The pole is one hundred fifteen degrees north of the Yellow Path and sixty-seven degrees south of it; the solstices mark where it lodges, determining long and short days.
translations.idiomatic: The pole stands one hundred fifteen degrees north of the Yellow Path and sixty-seven south; the solstices mark its lodging and fix day length.

sentences.zh: 」吳太常姚信，造《昕天論》云：「人為靈蟲，形最似天。

translations.literal: " Wu Grand Steward Yao Xin composed the Xin Tian Lun, saying: "Man is the numinous creature whose form most resembles Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Grand Steward Yao Xin wrote the Xin Tian Lun: "Humanity is the numinous creature whose form most resembles Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今人頤前侈臨胸，而項不能覆背。

translations.literal: Now man's chin projects forward over the chest, yet the nape cannot cover the back.
translations.idiomatic: The human chin juts forward over the chest, yet the neck cannot cover the back.

sentences.zh: 近取諸身，故知天之體，南低入地，北則偏高也。

translations.literal: Taking what is near from the body, one thus knows Heaven's body slopes low entering Earth in the south and is relatively high in the north.
translations.idiomatic: From our own bodies we infer Heaven's form: low where it enters Earth in the south, higher in the north.

sentences.zh: 又冬至極低，而天運近南，故日去人遠，而斗去人近，北天氣至，故水寒也。

translations.literal: Also at the winter solstice the pole is lowest and Heaven's motion nears the south, so the sun is far from man and the Dipper near—northern Heaven's qi arrives, hence cold water.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice the pole stands lowest and Heaven's motion nears the south; the sun recedes and the Dipper draws near—northern qi arrives and water turns cold.

sentences.zh: 夏至極起，而天運近北，而斗去人遠，日去人近，南天氣至，故蒸熱也。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice the pole rises highest and Heaven's motion nears the north; the Dipper recedes and the sun draws near—southern Heaven's qi arrives, hence steaming heat.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice the pole rises and Heaven nears the north; the Dipper recedes and the sun draws near—southern qi arrives and heat steams upward.

sentences.zh: 極之高時，日行地中淺，故夜短；

translations.literal: When the pole is high, the sun travels shallowly through Earth's center, hence short nights;
translations.idiomatic: When the pole stands high, the sun's path through Earth's center is shallow, so nights are short;

sentences.zh: 天去地高，故晝長也。

translations.literal: Heaven is far from Earth, hence long days.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven stands far above Earth, so days are long.

sentences.zh: 極之低時，日行地中深，故夜長；

translations.literal: When the pole is low, the sun travels deeply through Earth's center, hence long nights;
translations.idiomatic: When the pole is low, the sun's path through Earth's center runs deep, so nights are long;

sentences.zh: 天去地下，故晝短也。

translations.literal: Heaven is near below Earth, hence short days.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sits lower above Earth, so days are short.

sentences.zh: 」自虞喜、虞聳、姚信，皆好奇徇異之說，非極數談天者也。

translations.literal: " From Yu Xi, Yu Song, and Yao Xin onward—all curious, eccentric theories, not the ultimate reckoning for discussing Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi, Yu Song, and Yao Xin all offered curious, eccentric theories—not the definitive reckoning of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 前儒舊說，天地之體，狀如鳥卵，天包地外，猶殼之裹黃，周旋無端，其形渾渾然，故曰渾天。

translations.literal: The old doctrine of earlier scholars holds that the bodies of Heaven and Earth are shaped like a bird's egg—Heaven wraps outside Earth as a shell enfolds the yolk, turning without end, its form perfectly round—hence Spherical Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars taught that Heaven and Earth resemble a bird's egg—Heaven wraps Earth as a shell enfolds the yolk, revolving endlessly in perfect roundness—hence Spherical Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「天表裡有水，兩儀轉運，各乘氣而浮，載水而行。

translations.literal: It also says: "Inside and outside Heaven is water; the two principles turn and move, each riding qi to float, bearing water as they go.
translations.idiomatic: It also holds: "Water lies inside and outside Heaven; the two principles rotate, each borne on qi, carrying water as they move.

sentences.zh: 」漢王仲任，據蓋天之說以駁渾儀，云：「舊說，天轉從地下過。

translations.literal: " Wang Chong of Han, relying on Canopy Heaven theory to refute the armillary sphere, said: "The old doctrine says Heaven turns passing beneath Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Wang Chong, using Canopy Heaven to refute the armillary sphere, argued: "Old doctrine says Heaven rotates beneath Earth.

sentences.zh: 今掘地一丈輒有水，天何得從水中行乎？

translations.literal: Now dig one zhang and there is always water—how can Heaven pass through water?
translations.idiomatic: Dig one zhang down and water appears—how can Heaven travel through water?

sentences.zh: 甚不然也。

translations.literal: This is quite wrong.
translations.idiomatic: This cannot be right.

sentences.zh: 日隨天而轉，非入地。

translations.literal: The sun follows Heaven in turning—it does not enter Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The sun turns with Heaven—it does not plunge into Earth.

sentences.zh: 夫人目所望，不過十裡，天地合矣。

translations.literal: What the human eye sees extends no more than ten li—then Heaven and Earth meet.
translations.idiomatic: Human sight reaches only ten li—then Heaven and Earth seem to meet.

sentences.zh: 實非合也，遠使然耳。

translations.literal: In fact they do not meet—distance makes it seem so.
translations.idiomatic: They do not truly meet; distance creates the illusion.

sentences.zh: 今視日入，非入也，亦遠耳。

translations.literal: Now when we see the sun set, it does not enter—it is also distance.
translations.idiomatic: When we see the sun set, it does not enter Earth—it merely recedes.

sentences.zh: 當日入西方之時，其下之人亦將謂之為中也。

translations.literal: When the sun enters the west, people below also take that for the center.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun sets in the west, observers there likewise call it the center.

sentences.zh: 四方之人，各以其近者為出，遠者為入矣。

translations.literal: People in the four directions each take what is near as rising and what is far as setting.
translations.idiomatic: Each quarter of the world takes the near as sunrise and the far as sunset.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How is this made clear?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be demonstrated?

sentences.zh: 今試使一人把大炬火，夜行於平地，去人十裡，火光滅矣。

translations.literal: Now suppose one person carries a great torch and walks at night on level ground—ten li from others, the firelight vanishes.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose a man carries a great torch across level ground at night—ten li away, its light disappears.

sentences.zh: 非火滅也，遠使然耳。

translations.literal: The fire is not extinguished—distance makes it seem so.
translations.idiomatic: The fire is not out; distance only makes it seem so.

sentences.zh: 今日西轉不復見，是火滅之類也。

translations.literal: Now when the sun turns west and is seen no more, it is of the same kind as fire going out.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun wheels west and vanishes, the principle is the same.

sentences.zh: 日月不圓也，望視之所以圓者，去人遠也。

translations.literal: Sun and moon are not round—what makes them appear round in distant viewing is their distance from man.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon are not inherently round; distance makes them appear so.

sentences.zh: 夫日，火之精也；

translations.literal: The sun is the essence of fire;
translations.idiomatic: The sun is fire's essence;

sentences.zh: 月，水之精也。

translations.literal: the moon is the essence of water.
translations.idiomatic: the moon is water's essence.

sentences.zh: 水火在地不圓，在天何故圓？

translations.literal: Fire and water on Earth are not round—why should they be round in Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Fire and water on Earth are not round—why round in Heaven?

sentences.zh: 」丹陽葛洪釋之曰：

translations.literal: " Ge Hong of Danyang explained:
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong of Danyang replied:

sentences.zh: 《渾天儀注》云：「天如雞子，地如中黃，孤居於天內，天大而地小。

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Armillary Sphere says: "Heaven is like a hen's egg, Earth like the yolk within, solitary inside Heaven—Heaven large and Earth small.
translations.idiomatic: The Armillary Sphere Commentary says: "Heaven is like an egg, Earth like the yolk within, alone inside Heaven—Heaven vast, Earth small.

sentences.zh: 天表裡有水，天地各乘氣而立，載水而行。

translations.literal: Inside and outside Heaven is water; Heaven and Earth each stand on qi, bearing water as they move.
translations.idiomatic: Water surrounds Heaven within and without; Heaven and Earth ride qi, carrying water as they turn.

sentences.zh: 周天三百六十五度四分度之一，又中分之，則半覆地上，半繞地下，故二十八宿半見半隱。

translations.literal: The circuit of Heaven is three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter degrees; halve this and half covers above Earth, half circles beneath—hence half the twenty-eight lodges are seen and half hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's circuit is three hundred sixty-five and a quarter degrees; halved, half covers Earth above and half runs beneath—so half the twenty-eight lodges appear and half hide.

sentences.zh: 天轉如車轂之運也。

translations.literal: Heaven turns like the motion of a chariot hub."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven rotates like a chariot hub."

sentences.zh: 」諸論天者雖多，然精於陰陽者少。

translations.literal: Though many have theorized about Heaven, few are skilled in yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Many have theorized about Heaven, yet few master yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 張平子、陸公紀之徒，咸以為推步七曜之道，以度曆象昏明之證候，校以四八之氣，考以漏刻之分，占咎影之往來，求形驗于事情，莫密於渾象也。

translations.literal: Zhang Pingzi, Lu Gongji, and their kind all held that tracing the paths of the seven luminaries, using degrees to verify the calendar's signs of dusk and dawn, comparing with the four-eight qi, examining clepsydra divisions, reading the shadow's comings and goings, and seeking shape-verification in affairs—nothing is more precise than the spherical model.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng, Lu Tongji, and others held that tracking the seven luminaries, calibrating dusk and dawn by degrees, comparing the four-eight qi, testing clepsydra marks, reading shadow motion, and verifying by observation—nothing matches the spherical model.

sentences.zh: 張平子既作銅渾天儀，於密室中，以漏水轉之，與天皆合如符契也。

translations.literal: After Zhang Pingzi made the bronze armillary sphere in a sealed chamber, turned by flowing water, it accorded with Heaven like a tally.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's bronze armillary sphere, water-driven in a sealed chamber, matched Heaven like a tally.

sentences.zh: 崔子玉為其碑銘曰：「數術窮天地，製作侔造化。

translations.literal: Cui Ziyu composed its stele inscription: "Calculation exhausts Heaven and Earth, craftsmanship rivals creation.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ziyu wrote its inscription: "Calculation exhausts Heaven and Earth; craftsmanship rivals creation itself.

sentences.zh: 高才偉藝，與神合契。

translations.literal: Lofty talent and great art unite with the numinous in accord."
translations.idiomatic: Supreme talent and art accord with the divine."

sentences.zh: 」蓋由於平子渾儀及地動儀之有驗故也。

translations.literal: This was because Pingzi's armillary sphere and seismoscope had verification.
translations.idiomatic: This praise rested on the verified performance of Heng's armillary sphere and seismoscope.

sentences.zh: 若天果如渾者，則天之出入，行于水中，為必然矣。

translations.literal: If Heaven is truly as the sphere holds, then Heaven's passing in and out, traveling in water, is necessarily so.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven is truly spherical, its passage through water is necessarily so.

sentences.zh: 故《黃帝書》曰：「天在地外，水在天外。

translations.literal: Thus the Yellow Emperor's Book says: "Heaven is outside Earth, water is outside Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor's Book says: "Heaven lies outside Earth; water lies outside Heaven.

sentences.zh: 水浮天而載地者也。

translations.literal: Water floats Heaven and bears Earth."
translations.idiomatic: Water floats Heaven and carries Earth."

sentences.zh: 」又《易》曰：「時乘六龍。

translations.literal: The Changes also says: "Timely riding the six dragons."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Timely riding the six dragons."

sentences.zh: 」夫陽爻稱龍，龍者居水之物，以喻天。

translations.literal: Yang lines are called dragons—dragons are creatures dwelling in water, used to image Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yang lines are called dragons; dragons dwell in water, imaging Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天陽物也，又出入水中，與龍相似，故比以龍也。

translations.literal: Heaven is a yang thing, and since it also passes in and out of water like a dragon, it is thus compared to a dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is yang, and passing through water like a dragon, it is likened to one.

sentences.zh: 聖人仰觀俯察，審其如此。

translations.literal: The sage looked up and looked down and examined that it is so.
translations.idiomatic: The sage observed above and below and confirmed this.

sentences.zh: 故《晉》卦坤下離上，以證日出於地也。

translations.literal: Thus the Jin hexagram has Kun below and Li above, to verify the sun rising from Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin hexagram—Kun below, Li above—shows the sun rising from Earth.

sentences.zh: 又《明夷》之卦離下坤上，以證日入於地也。

translations.literal: The Ming Yi hexagram has Li below and Kun above, to verify the sun entering Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Yi hexagram—Li below, Kun above—shows the sun entering Earth.

sentences.zh: 又《需》卦乾下坎上，此亦天入水中之象也。

translations.literal: The Xu hexagram has Qian below and Kan above—this too is the image of Heaven entering water.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu hexagram—Qian below, Kan above—likewise images Heaven entering water.

sentences.zh: 天為金，金水相生之物也。

translations.literal: Heaven is metal; metal and water are mutually generating things.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is metal; metal and water mutually generate.

sentences.zh: 天出入水中，當有何損，而謂為不可乎？

translations.literal: Heaven passing in and out of water—what harm should there be, that one calls it impossible?
translations.idiomatic: What harm if Heaven passes through water—why call it impossible?

sentences.zh: 然則天之出入水中，無複疑矣。

translations.literal: Then Heaven's passing in and out of water need no longer be doubted.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's passage through water need no longer be doubted.

sentences.zh: 又今視諸星出於東者，初但去地小許耳。

translations.literal: Also, now when we watch stars rising in the east, at first they are only a little above Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Watch stars rise in the east: at first they stand barely above Earth.

sentences.zh: 漸而西行，先經人上，後遂轉西而下焉，不旁旋也。

translations.literal: Gradually they move west, first passing overhead, then turning down to set in the west—they do not wheel sideways.
translations.idiomatic: They drift west, pass overhead, then wheel down to set—never circling sideways.

sentences.zh: 其先在西之星，亦稍下而沒，無北轉者。

translations.literal: Stars first in the west also sink slightly in setting—none turn northward.
translations.idiomatic: Stars in the west likewise sink gradually at setting—none wheel northward.

sentences.zh: 日之出入亦然。

translations.literal: The sun's rising and setting is the same.
translations.idiomatic: The sun rises and sets the same way.

sentences.zh: 若謂天磨石轉者，眾星日月，宜隨天而回，初在於東，次經于南，次到於西，次及於北，而複還於東，不應橫過去也。

translations.literal: If one says Heaven turns like a millstone, the multitude of stars, sun, and moon should wheel with Heaven—first in the east, then passing south, then reaching west, then touching north, and returning east—they should not cross horizontally.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven turned like a millstone, sun, moon, and stars would wheel with it—east, south, west, north, and back—not cut horizontally across the sky.

sentences.zh: 今日出於東，冉冉轉上，及其入西，亦複漸漸稍下，都不繞邊北去。

translations.literal: Now the sun rises in the east, gradually mounting; when it enters the west it also gradually sinks lower—it does not wheel northward along the edge at all.
translations.idiomatic: The sun rises east and mounts gradually; setting west it sinks gradually—never circling north along the rim.

sentences.zh: 了了如此，王生必固謂為不然者，疏矣。

translations.literal: So plainly is this—Master Wang must stubbornly say it is not so; he is far off the mark.
translations.idiomatic: The evidence is plain—Wang Chong's stubborn denial misses the mark.

sentences.zh: 今日徑千里，其中足以當小星之數十也。

translations.literal: Now the sun's diameter is a thousand li—within it there could fit dozens of lesser stars.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's diameter spans a thousand li—room enough for dozens of lesser stars.

sentences.zh: 若日以轉遠之故，但當光曜不能複來照及人耳，宜猶望見其體，不應都失其所在也。

translations.literal: If because the sun turns far its light alone cannot shine back on man, one should still see its body—it should not wholly vanish from its place.
translations.idiomatic: If distance alone hid the sun, its body should still be visible—it should not vanish entirely.

sentences.zh: 日光既盛，其體又大於星。

translations.literal: Sunlight is bright and its body larger than stars.
translations.idiomatic: Sunlight is brilliant and the sun larger than any star.

sentences.zh: 今見極北之星，而不見日之在北者，明其不北行也。

translations.literal: Now we see stars at the far north yet do not see the sun in the north—clearly it does not travel north.
translations.idiomatic: We see polar stars yet never the sun in the north—proof it does not travel north.

sentences.zh: 若日以轉遠之故，不復可見，其比入之間，應當稍小。

translations.literal: If because the sun turns far it can no longer be seen, between its comparison and setting it should appear slightly smaller.
translations.idiomatic: If distance hid the sun, it should shrink slightly between transit and setting.

sentences.zh: 而日方入之時，反乃更大，此非轉遠之徵也。

translations.literal: Yet when the sun is just setting it instead grows larger—this is not a sign of turning far.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at setting the sun grows larger—not a sign of receding distance.

sentences.zh: 王生以火炬喻日，吾亦將借子之矛，以刺子之盾焉。

translations.literal: Master Wang uses the torch to image the sun—I too will borrow your spear to pierce your shield.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong's torch analogy invites the retort: your spear against your own shield.

sentences.zh: 把火之人，去人轉遠，其光轉微，而日月自出至入，不漸小也。

translations.literal: The torch-bearer, the farther from man, the fainter the light—yet sun and moon from rising to setting do not gradually shrink.
translations.idiomatic: A torch-bearer's light fades with distance—yet sun and moon do not shrink from rise to set.

sentences.zh: 王生以火喻之，謬矣。

translations.literal: Master Wang's fire analogy is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong's fire analogy fails.

sentences.zh: 又日之入西方，視之稍稍去，初尚有半，如橫破鏡之狀，須臾淪沒矣。

translations.literal: Also when the sun enters the west, viewed it gradually recedes; at first half remains like a mirror broken horizontally, and in a moment it is swallowed.
translations.idiomatic: At western setting the sun recedes gradually; half remains like a horizontally split mirror, then sinks in an instant.

sentences.zh: 若如王生之言，日轉北去者，其北都沒之頃，宜先如豎破鏡之狀，不應如橫破鏡也。

translations.literal: If as Master Wang says the sun turns northward, at the moment of northern setting it should first appear like a vertically split mirror—not horizontally broken.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun wheeled north as Wang Chong claims, it would vanish like a vertically split mirror—not a horizontal one.

sentences.zh: 如此言之，日入北方，不亦孤孑乎？

translations.literal: Spoken thus, the sun entering the north is also solitary and bereft.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sun setting northward stands alone and implausible.

sentences.zh: 又月之光微，不及日遠矣。

translations.literal: Also the moon's light is faint and far inferior to the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Moonlight is faint, far dimmer than sunlight.

sentences.zh: 月盛之時，雖有重雲蔽之，不見月體，而夕猶朗然，是月光猶從雲中而照外也。

translations.literal: When the moon is full, though heavy clouds cover it and the moon's body is not seen, the evening is still bright—moonlight still shines outward through the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: At full moon, heavy clouds may hide the disk yet evening stays bright—moonlight penetrates the clouds.

sentences.zh: 日若繞西及北者，其光故應如月在雲中之狀，不得夜便大暗也。

translations.literal: If the sun wheeled west and north, its light should be like the moon in clouds—it should not suddenly turn very dark at night.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun circled west and north, its light would diffuse like moonlight in clouds—not plunge the night into darkness.

sentences.zh: 又日入則星月出焉。

translations.literal: Also when the sun sets, stars and moon come out.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun sets, stars and moon appear.

sentences.zh: 明知天以日月分主晝夜，相代而照也。

translations.literal: Clearly Heaven uses sun and moon to divide and govern day and night, alternating in illumination.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly Heaven assigns sun and moon to alternate in governing day and night.

sentences.zh: 若日常出者，不應日亦入而星月出也。

translations.literal: If the sun constantly rose, it should not also set while stars and moon come out.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun always rose, it would not set while stars and moon emerge.

sentences.zh: 又案河、洛之文，皆云水火者，陰陽之餘氣也。

translations.literal: Also examining the texts of the River and Luo, all say fire and water are the surplus qi of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: River and Luo texts call fire and water surplus qi of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 夫言餘氣，則不能生日月可知也，顧當言日精生火者可耳。

translations.literal: Speaking of surplus qi, they clearly cannot generate sun and moon—one should rather say the sun's essence generates fire.
translations.idiomatic: As surplus qi they cannot generate sun and moon—rather the sun's essence generates fire.

sentences.zh: 若水火是日月所生，則亦何得盡如日月之圓乎？

translations.literal: If fire and water were generated by sun and moon, how could they all be round like sun and moon?
translations.idiomatic: If sun and moon generated fire and water, why would both be round like sun and moon?

sentences.zh: 今火出於陽燧，陽燧圓而火不圓也。

translations.literal: Now fire comes from the yang mirror—the yang mirror is round yet fire is not round.
translations.idiomatic: Fire from the yang mirror: the mirror is round, the flame is not.

sentences.zh: 水出於方諸，方諸方而水不方也。

translations.literal: Water comes from the square vessel—the square vessel is square yet water is not square.
translations.idiomatic: Water from the square vessel: the vessel is square, the water is not.

sentences.zh: 又陽燧可以取火於日，而無取日於火之理，此則日精之生火明矣。

translations.literal: Also the yang mirror can take fire from the sun, yet there is no principle of taking the sun from fire—this makes clear the sun's essence generates fire.
translations.idiomatic: The yang mirror draws fire from the sun, not the sun from fire—proof the sun's essence begets fire.

sentences.zh: 方諸可以取水於月，無取月于水之道，此則月精之生水了矣。

translations.literal: The square vessel can take water from the moon—there is no way of taking the moon from water—this settles that the moon's essence generates water.
translations.idiomatic: The square vessel draws water from the moon, not the moon from water—proof the moon's essence begets water.

sentences.zh: 王生又云：「遠故視之圓。

translations.literal: Master Wang also said: "Distance makes it appear round."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong also argued: "Distance makes them look round."

sentences.zh: 」若審然者，月初生之時及既虧之後，何以視之不圓乎？

translations.literal: If this were truly so, at the moon's first emergence and after it wanes, why does it not appear round?
translations.idiomatic: If distance alone made things round, why does the crescent moon not look round at first rise or after waning?

sentences.zh: 而日食，或上或下，從側而起，或如鉤至盡。

translations.literal: Yet in solar eclipses it is sometimes above or below, rising from the side, or like a hook until complete.
translations.idiomatic: Solar eclipses show the sun clipped above or below, or hooked from the side until fully covered.

sentences.zh: 若遠視見圓，不宜見其殘缺左右所起也。

translations.literal: If distant viewing makes it round, one should not see it incomplete with left and right portions rising.
translations.idiomatic: If distance made it round, eclipses should not show partial loss from left or right.

sentences.zh: 此則渾天之體，信而有徵矣。

translations.literal: Thus the body of Spherical Heaven is verified and has evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Spherical Heaven is thus verified by evidence.

sentences.zh: 宋何承天論渾天象體曰：「詳尋前說，因觀渾儀，研求其意，有悟天形正圓，而水居其半，地中高外卑，水周其下。

translations.literal: Song's He Chengtian discussed the form of the spherical model: "Examining the prior doctrine and observing the armillary sphere, I found its meaning: Heaven's form is truly round and water occupies half; Earth is high at the center and low at the edges, with water circling below.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian of Song wrote on the spherical model: "Studying prior doctrine and the armillary sphere, I grasp its meaning: Heaven is truly round, water fills half; Earth rises at center and falls at the rim, water encircling below.

sentences.zh: 言四方者，東曰暘穀，日之所出，西曰濛汜，日之所入。

translations.literal: Speaking of the four directions: east is Yang Valley where the sun rises; west is Meng Si where the sun sets.
translations.idiomatic: The four directions: east is Yang Valley of sunrise; west is Meng Si of sunset.

sentences.zh: 《莊子》又云：'北溟有魚，化而為鳥，將徙于南溟。

translations.literal: The Zhuangzi also says: "In the Northern Sea there is a fish that transforms into a bird and will migrate to the Southern Sea."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi says: "In the Northern Sea a fish becomes a bird and migrates to the Southern Sea."

sentences.zh: '斯亦古之遺記，四方皆水證也。

translations.literal: This too is an ancient preserved record—proof that the four directions are all water.
translations.idiomatic: This ancient record too proves all four directions are water.

sentences.zh: 四方皆水，謂之四海。

translations.literal: All four directions being water is called the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Water on all four sides constitutes the four seas.

sentences.zh: 凡五行相生，水生於金。

translations.literal: Among the five phases, water is generated from metal.
translations.idiomatic: In the five phases, water generates from metal.

sentences.zh: 是故百川發源，皆自山出，由高趣下，歸注於海。

translations.literal: Therefore the hundred streams have their sources—all arising from mountains, running from high to low, pouring into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: All rivers spring from mountains, run downhill, and pour into the sea.

sentences.zh: 日為陽精，光曜炎熾，一夜入水，所經焦竭。

translations.literal: The sun is yang essence; its light blazes fiercely. One night entering water scorches dry what it passes.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is yang essence, fiercely bright. One night's passage through water scorches all it touches.

sentences.zh: 百川歸注，足以相補，故旱不為減，浸不為益。

translations.literal: The hundred streams return and pour in, sufficient to replenish—thus drought does not diminish and flooding does not increase.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers returning to the sea replenish it—drought does not shrink it, floods do not swell it.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「周天三百六十五度、三百四分之七十五。

translations.literal: " It also says: "The circuit of Heaven is three hundred sixty-five and seventy-five four-hundredths degrees."
translations.idiomatic: It also states: "Heaven's full circuit is three hundred sixty-five and seventy-five quarter-degrees."

sentences.zh: 天常西轉，一日一夜，過周一度。

translations.literal: It also says: "The circuit of Heaven is three hundred sixty-five and seventy-five four-hundredths degrees.
translations.idiomatic: It also states: "Heaven's circuit is three hundred sixty-five and seventy-five quarter-degrees.

sentences.zh: 南北二極，相去一百一十六度、三百四分度之六十五強，即天經也。

translations.literal: Heaven constantly turns west; one day and night pass one degree of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven turns constantly westward; one day-night cycle advances one degree.

sentences.zh: 黃道袤帶赤道，春分交於奎七度，秋分交於軫十五度，冬至斗十四度半強，夏至井十六度半。

translations.literal: The two poles north and south are one hundred sixteen and sixty-five four-hundredths strong degrees apart—this is Heaven's longitude. The Yellow Path girdles the equator; at spring equinox it crosses at Kui 7 degrees, at autumn equinox at Zhen 15 degrees; at winter solstice at Dipper 14 and a half strong degrees, at summer solstice at Well 16 and a half.
translations.idiomatic: North and south poles stand one hundred sixteen and sixty-five quarter-degrees apart—Heaven's axis. The Yellow Path belts the equator: spring equinox at Kui 7°, autumn at Zhen 15°, winter solstice at Dipper 14.5°, summer at Well 16.5°.

sentences.zh: 從北極扶天而南五十五度強，則居天四維之中，最高處也，即天頂也。

translations.literal: From the North Pole supporting Heaven southward fifty-five and a half strong degrees, it occupies the center of Heaven's four dimensions—the highest point, Heaven's zenith.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-five and a half degrees south from the North Pole marks Heaven's zenith—the highest point at the center of the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 其下則地中也。

translations.literal: Below it is Earth's center.
translations.idiomatic: Below lies Earth's center.

sentences.zh: 」自外與王蕃大同。

translations.literal: Beyond this it largely agrees with Wang Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this it largely matches Wang Fan.

sentences.zh: 王蕃《渾天說》，具于《晉史》。

translations.literal: Wang Fan's Spherical Heaven Discourse is fully recorded in the Jin History.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan's Spherical Heaven Discourse appears in the Jin History.

sentences.zh: 舊說渾天者，以日月星辰，不問春秋冬夏，晝夜晨昏，上下去地中皆同，無遠近。

translations.literal: The old doctrine of Spherical Heaven holds that sun, moon, and stars, regardless of spring, summer, autumn, winter, day, night, dawn, or dusk, are the same above and below Earth's center—no near or far.
translations.idiomatic: Old Spherical Heaven doctrine holds sun, moon, and stars stay equidistant from Earth's center in all seasons and hours—no variation in distance.

sentences.zh: 《列子》曰：「孔子東遊，見兩小兒鬭。

translations.literal: The Liezi says: "Confucius traveled east and saw two small boys disputing.
translations.idiomatic: The Liezi says: "Confucius traveling east saw two boys arguing.

sentences.zh: 問其故，一小兒曰：'我以日始出去人近，而日中時遠也。

translations.literal: He asked the reason. One boy said: "I think when the sun first rises it is near man, and at midday it is far."
translations.idiomatic: One said: "The sun at dawn is near; at noon it is far."

sentences.zh: '一小兒曰：'我以為日初出遠，而日中時近也。

translations.literal: The other boy said: "I think when the sun first rises it is far, and at midday it is near."
translations.idiomatic: The other said: "At dawn it is far; at noon it is near."

sentences.zh: '言初出近者曰：'日初出，大如車蓋，及其日中，裁如盤蓋。

translations.literal: The one who said near at first rising said: "When the sun first rises it is large as a chariot canopy; at midday it is only like a plate cover.
translations.idiomatic: The "near at dawn" boy said: "At sunrise the sun is chariot-canopy large; at noon only plate-sized.

sentences.zh: 此不為遠者小，近者大乎？

translations.literal: Is this not distant things small and near things large?"
translations.idiomatic: Are not distant things small and near things large?"

sentences.zh: ' 言日初出遠者曰：'日初出時，滄滄涼涼，及其中時，熱如探湯。

translations.literal: The one who said far at first rising said: "When the sun first rises it is cool and clear; at midday it is hot as dipping in boiling water.
translations.idiomatic: The "far at dawn" boy said: "At sunrise it is cool; at noon hot as boiling water.

sentences.zh: 此不為近者熱，遠者涼乎？

translations.literal: Is this not near things hot and distant things cool?"
translations.idiomatic: Are not near things hot and far things cool?"

sentences.zh: 桓譚《新論》云：「漢長水校尉平陵關子陽，以為日之去人，上方遠而四傍近。

translations.literal: Huan Tan's New Discourses says: "Han's Colonel of the Chang River Guan Ziyang of Pingling held that the sun's distance from man is far above and near at the four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Tan's New Discourses records Guan Ziyang of Pingling: "The sun is far overhead and near at the sides.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: How is this known?
translations.idiomatic: How know this?

sentences.zh: 星宿昏時出東方，其間甚疏，相離丈餘。

translations.literal: When lodges appear at dusk in the east, the intervals between them are very sparse, separated by more than one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk eastern stars stand widely spaced—over a zhang apart.

sentences.zh: 及夜半在上方，視之甚數，相離一二尺。

translations.literal: At midnight overhead they appear very dense, separated by one or two chi.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight overhead they crowd together—one or two chi apart.

sentences.zh: 以准度望之，逾益明白，故知天上之遠於傍也。

translations.literal: Measuring by standard degrees, the farther one looks the clearer—thus one knows Heaven above is far from the sides.
translations.idiomatic: By degree measure, overhead stars appear denser—proving Heaven is farther above than at the sides.

sentences.zh: 日為天陽，火為地陽。

translations.literal: The sun is Heaven's yang; fire is Earth's yang.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is Heaven's yang; fire is Earth's yang.

sentences.zh: 地陽上升，天陽下降。

translations.literal: Earth's yang rises; Heaven's yang descends.
translations.idiomatic: Earth's yang rises upward; Heaven's yang descends.

sentences.zh: 今置火於地，從傍與上，診其熱，遠近殊不同焉。

translations.literal: Now place fire on Earth—from the side and from above, examine its heat—the near and far differ greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Place fire on Earth and test heat from the side versus overhead—the difference is great.

sentences.zh: 日中正在上，覆蓋人，人當天陽之沖，故熱于始出時。

translations.literal: At midday the sun is directly overhead, covering man—man is at Heaven's yang's impact, hence hotter than at first rising.
translations.idiomatic: At noon the sun stands directly overhead—yang strikes full force, hence hotter than at dawn.

sentences.zh: 又新從太陰中來，故複涼於其西在桑榆間也。

translations.literal: Also newly coming from within the lunar shade, hence also cooler when west among mulberry and elm.
translations.idiomatic: Also newly emerging from lunar shadow, hence cooler when west among mulberry and elm.

sentences.zh: 桓君山曰：子陽之言，豈其然乎？

translations.literal: Master Huan Tan said: Are Ziyang's words really so?
translations.idiomatic: Huan Tan asked: Can Ziyang's theory be correct?

sentences.zh: 張衡《靈臺》曰：「日之薄地，暗其明也。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng's Ling Tai says: "When the sun nears Earth it dims its brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's Ling Tai says: "Near Earth the sun dims its brilliance.

sentences.zh: 由暗視明，明無所屈，是以望之若大。

translations.literal: Viewing brightness from darkness, brightness has nothing to bend—thus it appears large.
translations.idiomatic: Seen from darkness, brightness shows unobstructed—hence it looks large.

sentences.zh: 方其中，天地同明，明還自奪，故望之若小。

translations.literal: At the center, Heaven and Earth share equal brightness; brightness returns and steals from itself—thus it appears small.
translations.idiomatic: At zenith Heaven and Earth share equal light; brightness cancels itself—hence it looks small.

sentences.zh: 火當夜而揚光，在晝則不明也。

translations.literal: Fire at night spreads light; in daytime it is not bright.
translations.idiomatic: Fire shines at night; by day it is invisible.

sentences.zh: 月之於夜，與日同而差微。

translations.literal: The moon at night is like the sun but slightly less.
translations.idiomatic: The moon at night resembles the sun but dimmer.

sentences.zh: 晉著作郎陽平束皙，字廣微，以為傍方與上方等。

translations.literal: Jin Secretariat Compiler Yang Ping Shu Xi, styled Guangwei, held that the sides and overhead are equal.
translations.idiomatic: Jin compiler Shu Xi of Yangping held side and overhead equal in distance.

sentences.zh: 傍視則天體存於側，故日出時視日大也。

translations.literal: Viewing sideways, Heaven's body is stored at the side—hence the sun appears large at rising.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed sideways Heaven's body lies to the side—hence the sun looks large at rising.

sentences.zh: 日無小大，而所存者有伸厭。

translations.literal: The sun has no small or large—it is what is stored that has compression and extension.
translations.idiomatic: The sun has no intrinsic size—what varies is compression and extension of its image.

sentences.zh: 厭而形小，伸而體大，蓋其理也。

translations.literal: Compressed the form is small; extended the body is large—this is the principle.
translations.idiomatic: Compressed it looks small; extended it looks large—such is the principle.

sentences.zh: 又日始出時色白者，雖大不甚，始出時色赤者，其大則甚，此終以人目之惑，無遠近也。

translations.literal: Also when the sun first rises white, though large it is not very so; when first rising red, it is very large—this ultimately is confusion of the human eye, not distance.
translations.idiomatic: A white dawn sun looks large but not greatly so; a red dawn sun looks very large—all eye illusion, not distance.

sentences.zh: 且夫置器廣庭，則函牛之鼎如釜，堂崇十仞，則八尺之人猶短，物有陵之，非形異也。

translations.literal: Moreover, set a vessel in a broad courtyard and an ox cauldron looks like a pot; raise a hall ten ren and an eight-chi man still looks short—things have what towers over them; the form is not different.
translations.idiomatic: In a broad courtyard an ox cauldron looks like a pot; in a ten-ren hall an eight-chi man looks short—context alters appearance, not the thing itself.

sentences.zh: 夫物有惑心，形有亂目，誠非斷疑定理之主。

translations.literal: Things confuse the heart; forms confuse the eye—they are truly not masters for resolving doubt and fixing principle.
translations.idiomatic: Things confuse the mind and forms confuse the eye—they cannot settle definitive principle.

sentences.zh: 故仰遊雲以觀月，月常動而雲不移；

translations.literal: Thus looking up through traveling clouds to view the moon, the moon constantly moves while clouds do not shift;
translations.idiomatic: Watch the moon through moving clouds—the moon moves, clouds do not;

sentences.zh: 乘船以涉水，水去而船不徙矣。

translations.literal: board a boat to cross water—the water recedes while the boat does not move.
translations.idiomatic: board a boat—the water flows past while the boat stays still.

sentences.zh: 姜岌云：「余以為子陽言天陽下降，日下熱，束皙言天體存於目，則日大，頗近之矣。

translations.literal: Jiang Kui said: "I hold that Ziyang's saying Heaven's yang descends makes the sun hot below, and Shu Xi's saying Heaven's body is stored in the eye makes the sun large—both are quite close.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Kui wrote: "Ziyang's descending yang explains midday heat; Shu Xi's stored-in-the-eye explains dawn size—both near the mark.

sentences.zh: 渾天之體，圓周之徑，詳之於天度，驗之於晷影，而紛然之說，由人目也。

translations.literal: The body of Spherical Heaven, the diameter of the circuit—investigating by heavenly degrees and verifying by gnomon shadows—the tangled theories arise from the human eye.
translations.idiomatic: Spherical Heaven's body and circuit—investigated by degrees, verified by shadows—the tangled theories stem from human sight.

sentences.zh: 參伐初出，在旁則其間疏，在上則其間數。

translations.literal: When Shen and Wei first rise, at the side the intervals are sparse; overhead they are dense.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and Wei at first rising stand sparse at the horizon, dense overhead.

sentences.zh: 以渾檢之，度則均也。

translations.literal: Checking by the sphere, the degrees are equal.
translations.idiomatic: On the sphere their degrees are equal.

sentences.zh: 旁之與上，理無有殊也。

translations.literal: At the side and overhead there is no difference in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Side and overhead differ in appearance, not principle.

sentences.zh: 夫日者純陽之精也，光明外曜，以眩人目，故人視日如小。

translations.literal: The sun is pure yang essence; its light shines outward and dazzles the human eye—thus people see the sun as small.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is pure yang; outward radiance dazzles the eye—hence it looks small.

sentences.zh: 及其初出，地有遊氣，以厭日光，不眩人目，即日赤而大也。

translations.literal: At first rising, earthly wandering vapors compress the sunlight so it does not dazzle the eye—the sun is red and large.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn earthly vapors filter sunlight, sparing the eye—the sun looks red and large.

sentences.zh: 無游氣則色白，大不甚矣。

translations.literal: Without wandering vapors the color is white and not very large.
