translations.idiomatic: Without vapors it looks white and not greatly large.

sentences.zh: 地氣不及天，故一日之中，晨夕日色赤，而中時日色白。

translations.literal: Earthly qi does not reach Heaven—thus within one day at dawn and dusk the sun's color is red, while at midday it is white.
translations.idiomatic: Earthly qi does not reach Heaven—hence red sun at dawn and dusk, white at noon.

sentences.zh: 地氣上升，濛濛四合，與天連者，雖中時亦赤矣。

translations.literal: When earthly qi rises, hazy on all four sides and joining Heaven, even at midday it is also red.
translations.idiomatic: When earthly qi rises in haze joining Heaven, even noon shows red.

sentences.zh: 日與火相類，火則體赤而炎黃，日赤宜矣。

translations.literal: The sun resembles fire; fire has a red body and blazing yellow—the sun's redness is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The sun resembles fire; fire is red and blazing yellow—the sun's redness fits.

sentences.zh: 然日色赤者，猶火無炎也。

translations.literal: Yet when the sun's color is red, it is like fire without flame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a red sun is like fire without flame.

sentences.zh: 光衰失常，則為異矣。

translations.literal: When light wanes and norm is lost, this becomes an anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Fading light breaking norm signals anomaly.

sentences.zh: 梁奉朝請祖暅曰：

translations.literal: Liang Court Gentleman Zu Geng said:
translations.idiomatic: Liang court gentleman Zu Geng wrote:

sentences.zh: 自古論天者多矣，而群氏糾紛，至相非毀。

translations.literal: Since antiquity many have theorized about Heaven, yet schools dispute and even revile one another.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity many theorized Heaven, yet schools quarreled and reviled each other.

sentences.zh: 竊覽同異，稽之典經，仰觀辰極，傍矚四維，睹日月之升降，察五星之見伏，校之以儀象，覆之以晷漏，則渾天之理，信而有徵。

translations.literal: I have examined agreements and differences, checked against canonical texts, looked up at the pole, glanced at the four dimensions, observed sun and moon's ascent and descent, inspected the five planets' appearance and hiding, compared with instruments, covered with gnomon and clepsydra—then Spherical Heaven's principle is verified and has evidence.
translations.idiomatic: I compared schools against the classics, observed pole, quarters, sun, moon, and planets, tested with instruments, gnomon, and clepsydra—Spherical Heaven stands verified.

sentences.zh: 輒遺眾說，附渾儀云。

translations.literal: I leave aside the multitude of theories and append this to the armillary sphere.
translations.idiomatic: I set aside rival theories and append this to the armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 《考靈曜》先儒求得天地相去十七萬八千五百里，以晷影驗之，失於過多。

translations.literal: The Kao Ling Yao of earlier scholars obtained that Heaven and Earth are one hundred seventy-eight thousand five hundred li apart—verified by gnomon shadow, it errs by being too much.
translations.idiomatic: Kao Ling Yao placed Heaven and Earth one hundred seventy-eight thousand five hundred li apart—gnomon tests prove this too great.

sentences.zh: 既不顯求之術，而虛設其數，蓋誇誕之辭，宜非聖人之旨也。

translations.literal: Since the method of seeking it is not shown and numbers are set empty, it is boastful speech—not the sage's intent.
translations.idiomatic: With no shown method and empty numbers, it is boastful—not the sages' intent.

sentences.zh: 學者多固其說而未之革，豈不知尋其理歟，抑未能求其數故也？

translations.literal: Scholars mostly hold to the doctrine without reform—is it that they do not know how to seek its principle, or cannot seek its numbers?
translations.idiomatic: Scholars cling to unreformed doctrine—unable to seek principle, or unable to seek numbers?

sentences.zh: 王蕃所考，校之前說，不啻減半。

translations.literal: Wang Fan's investigation, compared with prior doctrine, reduces it by more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan's reckoning cuts prior estimates by more than half.

sentences.zh: 雖非揆格所知，而求之以理，誠未能遙趣其實，蓋近密乎？

translations.literal: Though not what calipers can know, seeking by principle it truly cannot reach the reality remotely—it is nearly close, is it not?
translations.idiomatic: Though calipers cannot reach it, by principle it approaches reality more closely.

sentences.zh: 輒因王蕃天高數，以求冬至、春分日高及南戴日下去地中數。

translations.literal: I therefore take Wang Fan's number for Heaven's height to seek the sun's height at winter solstice and spring equinox and the number of the sun's nadir south of the cap at those times.
translations.idiomatic: Using Wang Fan's Heaven height I derive solstice and equinox sun heights and southern nadir distances.

sentences.zh: 法，令表高八尺與冬至影長一丈三尺，各自乘，並而開方除之為法。

translations.literal: Method: let the gnomon height be eight chi and winter solstice shadow one zhang three chi; multiply each, add, extract root, and divide as method.
translations.idiomatic: Method: gnomon eight chi, winter solstice shadow one zhang three chi; multiply, add, extract root for divisor.

sentences.zh: 天高乘表高為實，實如法，得四萬二千六百五十八裡有奇，即冬至日高也。

translations.literal: Heaven height times gnomon height is dividend; dividend divided by method yields forty-two thousand six hundred fifty-eight li odd—the winter solstice sun height.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven height × gnomon height ÷ divisor = forty-two thousand six hundred fifty-eight li odd—winter solstice sun height.

sentences.zh: 以天高乘冬至影長為實，實如法，得六萬九千三百二十裡有奇，即冬至南戴日下去地中數也。

translations.literal: Heaven height times winter solstice shadow is dividend; dividend divided by method yields sixty-nine thousand three hundred twenty li odd—the winter solstice southern cap nadir below Earth's center.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven height × winter solstice shadow ÷ divisor = sixty-nine thousand three hundred twenty li odd—winter solstice southern nadir.

sentences.zh: 求春秋分數法，令表高及春秋分影長五尺三寸九分，各自乘，並而開方除之為法。

translations.literal: Method for spring and autumn equinox: let gnomon height and equinox shadow five chi three cun nine fen; multiply each, add, extract root as method.
translations.idiomatic: Equinox method: gnomon height and shadow five chi three cun nine fen; same procedure.

sentences.zh: 因冬至日高實，而以法除之，得六萬七千五百二裡有奇，即春秋分日高也。

translations.literal: Using winter solstice sun height dividend divided by method yields sixty-seven thousand five hundred two li odd—the spring and autumn equinox sun height.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice sun height dividend ÷ method = sixty-seven thousand five hundred two li odd—equinox sun height.

sentences.zh: 以天高乘春秋分影長實，實如法而一，得四萬五千四百七十九裡有奇，即春秋分南戴日下去地中數也。

translations.literal: Heaven height times equinox shadow dividend divided by method yields forty-five thousand four hundred seventy-nine li odd—the spring and autumn equinox southern cap nadir below Earth's center.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven height × equinox shadow ÷ method = forty-five thousand four hundred seventy-nine li odd—equinox southern nadir.

sentences.zh: 南戴日下，所謂丹穴也。

translations.literal: Below the southern cap is what is called the Cinnabar Cave.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the southern cap lies the Cinnabar Cave.

sentences.zh: 推北極裡數法，夜于地中表南，傅地遙望北辰紐星之末，令與表端參合。

translations.literal: Method for deriving North Pole li: at night south of the gnomon at Earth's center, sight along the ground to the end of the Pivot star at the North Pole, aligning with the gnomon top.
translations.idiomatic: North Pole method: at night south of the central gnomon, sight the Pivot star's end aligned with the gnomon top.

sentences.zh: 以人目去表數及表高各自乘，並而開方除之為法。

translations.literal: Eye distance from gnomon and gnomon height—multiply each, add, extract root as method.
translations.idiomatic: Eye-to-gnomon distance and gnomon height: multiply, add, root for divisor.

sentences.zh: 天高乘表高數為實，實如法而一，即北辰紐星高地數也。

translations.literal: Heaven height times gnomon height is dividend; dividend divided by method yields the Pivot star's height at the North Pole.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven height × gnomon height ÷ method = Pivot star height at North Pole.

sentences.zh: 天高乘人目去表為實，實如法，即去北戴極下之數也。

translations.literal: Heaven height times eye distance from gnomon is dividend; dividend divided by method yields the distance below the northern cap at the Pole.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven height × eye distance ÷ method = distance below northern cap.

sentences.zh: 北戴斗極為空桐。

translations.literal: The northern cap at the Dipper's pole is Kongtong.
translations.idiomatic: The northern cap at the Dipper pole is Kongtong.

sentences.zh: 日去赤道表裡二十四度，遠寒近暑而中和。

translations.literal: The sun is twenty-four degrees inside and outside the equator—far brings cold, near brings heat, and between is temperate.
translations.idiomatic: The sun stands twenty-four degrees inside or outside the equator—far means cold, near means heat, between is temperate.

sentences.zh: 二分之日，去天頂三十六度。

translations.literal: On equinox days the sun is thirty-six degrees from Heaven's zenith.
translations.idiomatic: At equinox the sun stands thirty-six degrees from Heaven's zenith.

sentences.zh: 日去地中，四時同度，而有寒暑者，地氣上騰，天氣下降，故遠日下而寒，近日下而暑，非有遠近也。

translations.literal: The sun's distance from Earth's center is the same in all four seasons, yet there is cold and heat because earthly qi rises and heavenly qi descends—far from the sun below brings cold, near the sun below brings heat—not because of distance.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's distance from Earth's center is constant through seasons; cold and heat come from earthly qi rising and heavenly qi descending—not from varying distance.

sentences.zh: 猶火居上，雖遠而炎，在傍，雖近而微。

translations.literal: Like fire placed above—though far it burns hot; at the side, though near it is faint.
translations.idiomatic: Fire overhead burns hot though far; at the side it fades though near.

sentences.zh: 視日在傍而大，居上而小者，仰矚為難，平觀為易也。

translations.literal: That the sun viewed at the side appears large and overhead small is because looking up is hard and looking level is easy.
translations.idiomatic: The sun looks larger at the side and smaller overhead because upward sight is difficult, level sight easy.

sentences.zh: 由視有夷險，非遠近之效也。

translations.literal: Because viewing has easy and difficult aspects, it is not an effect of distance.
translations.idiomatic: Viewing angle, not distance, causes the apparent size difference.

sentences.zh: 今懸珠於百仞之上，或置之於百仞之前，從而觀之，則大小殊矣。

translations.literal: Now suspend a pearl a hundred ren above, or place it a hundred ren in front—viewing from there, the sizes differ greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Suspend a pearl a hundred ren overhead or a hundred ren ahead—viewed from either spot, its size looks very different.

sentences.zh: 先儒弗斯取驗，虛繁翰墨，夷途頓轡，雄辭析辯，不亦迂哉！

translations.literal: Earlier scholars did not take this for verification, vainly multiplying ink—halting the chariot on level ground, eloquent words analyzing and debating—is this not roundabout!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars never tested this, wasting pages in debate—is that not pointless?

sentences.zh: 今大寒在冬至後二氣者，寒積而未消也。

translations.literal: Now great cold falls two qi after the winter solstice because cold accumulates and has not yet dissipated.
translations.idiomatic: Great cold comes two qi after winter solstice because cold accumulates before it fades.

sentences.zh: 大暑在夏至後二氣者，暑積而未歇也。

translations.literal: Great heat falls two qi after the summer solstice because heat accumulates and has not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Great heat comes two qi after summer solstice because heat accumulates before it breaks.

sentences.zh: 寒暑均和，乃在春秋分後二氣者，寒暑積而未平也。

translations.literal: When cold and heat are evenly tempered, it is two qi after the spring and autumn equinoxes—cold and heat accumulate and are not yet balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Even temperance falls two qi after the equinoxes, when accumulated cold and heat have not yet balanced.

sentences.zh: 譬之火始入室，而未甚溫，弗事加薪，久而逾熾。

translations.literal: It is like fire just entering a room—not yet very warm; without adding fuel, in time it burns more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Like fire entering a room: not warm at first, yet without new fuel it grows fiercer with time.

sentences.zh: 既已遷之，猶有餘熱也。

translations.literal: Even after it has moved elsewhere, residual heat remains.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the fire moves on, heat lingers.

sentences.zh: ○渾天儀

translations.literal: The Armillary Sphere
translations.idiomatic: The Armillary Sphere

sentences.zh: 案《虞書》：「舜在〔璣玉衡，以齊七政，」則《考靈曜》所謂觀玉儀之遊，昏明主時，乃命中星者也。

translations.literal: Examining the Documents of Yu: "Shun was at the ji-yu heng to align the seven regulators"—then what the Kao Ling Yao calls observing the jade instrument's motion and dusk and dawn governing the hours is ordering the central stars.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu Documents say Shun used the ji-yu heng to align the seven regulators—what Kao Ling Yao calls observing the jade instrument's motion to govern dusk and dawn means ordering the central stars.

sentences.zh: 〔璣中而星未中為急，急則日過其度，月不及其宿。

translations.literal: When the ji is centered but stars are not centered, this is urgent—urgent means the sun passes its degree and the moon does not reach its lodge.
translations.idiomatic: When the ji is centered but stars are not, this is urgent: the sun overshoots its degree and the moon misses its lodge.

sentences.zh: 〔璣未中而星中為舒，舒則日不及其度，月過其宿。

translations.literal: When the ji is not centered but stars are centered, this is relaxed—relaxed means the sun does not reach its degree and the moon passes its lodge.
translations.idiomatic: When the ji is off but stars are centered, this is relaxed: the sun falls short and the moon overshoots its lodge.

sentences.zh: 〔璣中而星中為調，調則風雨時，庶草蕃蕪，而五穀登，萬事康也。

translations.literal: When the ji is centered and stars are centered, this is balanced—balanced means wind and rain come in season, grasses flourish, the five grains ripen, and all affairs prosper.
translations.idiomatic: When both ji and stars are centered, all is balanced: seasons hold, crops flourish, and affairs prosper.

sentences.zh: 所言〔璣者，謂渾天儀也。

translations.literal: The ji spoken of means the armillary sphere.
translations.idiomatic: The ji mentioned here is the armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 故《春秋文耀鉤》云：「唐堯即位，羲、和立渾儀。

translations.literal: Thus the Chunqiu Wen Yao Gou says: "When Tang Yao took the throne, Xi and He established the armillary instrument."
translations.idiomatic: Chunqiu Wen Yao Gou says: "When Yao took the throne, Xi and He set up the armillary instrument."

sentences.zh: 」而先儒或因星官書，北斗第二星名旋，第三星名璣，第五星名玉衡，仍七政之言，即以為北斗七星。

translations.literal: Yet earlier scholars, because star-office books name the Northern Dipper's second star Xuan, third star Ji, and fifth star Yu Heng, still speaking of the seven regulators, took these for the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Some scholars, noting the Dipper's second star Xuan, third Ji, and fifth Yu Heng in star catalogues, mistook them for the seven regulators.

sentences.zh: 載筆之官，莫之或辨。

translations.literal: Recording officials none could distinguish this.
translations.idiomatic: Historiographers failed to distinguish this.

sentences.zh: 史遷、班固，猶且致疑。

translations.literal: Even Sima Qian and Ban Gu still expressed doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Even Sima Qian and Ban Gu doubted it.

sentences.zh: 馬季長創謂璣衡為渾天儀。

translations.literal: Ma Rong first proposed that ji-heng meant the armillary sphere.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong first identified ji-heng as the armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄亦云；

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan also said:
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan likewise wrote:

sentences.zh: 「其轉運者為璣，其持正者為衡，皆以玉為之。

translations.literal: "What turns and moves is the ji; what holds and fixes is the heng—both made of jade.
translations.idiomatic: "The rotating part is the ji, the fixed part the heng—both of jade.

sentences.zh: 七政者，日月五星也。

translations.literal: The seven regulators are sun, moon, and the five planets.
translations.idiomatic: The seven regulators are sun, moon, and five planets.

sentences.zh: 以璣衡視其行度，以觀天意也。

translations.literal: Using ji-heng to view their motion in degrees is to observe Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Ji-heng measures their degrees to read Heaven's intent."

sentences.zh: 」故王蕃云：「渾天儀者，羲、和之舊器，積代相傳，謂之璣衡。

translations.literal: Thus Wang Fan said: "The armillary sphere is the old instrument of Xi and He, transmitted through generations and called ji-heng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan said: "The armillary sphere is Xi and He's ancient instrument, transmitted as ji-heng.

sentences.zh: 其為用也，以察三光，以分宿度者也。

translations.literal: In use it inspects the three luminaries and divides lodge degrees.
translations.idiomatic: It inspects the three luminaries and divides lodge degrees.

sentences.zh: 又有渾天象者，以著天體，以布星辰。

translations.literal: There is also the spherical model, which displays Heaven's body and arrays the stars.
translations.idiomatic: The spherical model displays Heaven's body and arrays stars.

sentences.zh: 而渾象之法，地當在天中，其勢不便，故反觀其形，地為外匡，于已解者，無異在內。

translations.literal: In the spherical model's method Earth should be at Heaven's center—its form is inconvenient, so one reverses the view: Earth as outer frame—for those who understand, no different from being inside.
translations.idiomatic: The spherical model ideally places Earth at center; impractically one reverses the view with Earth as outer frame—equivalent for those who grasp it.

sentences.zh: 詭狀殊體，而合於理，可謂奇巧。

translations.literal: Strange in form yet sound in principle—it may be called ingeniously clever.
translations.idiomatic: Odd in form yet sound in principle—ingeniously clever.

sentences.zh: 然斯二者，以考于天，蓋密矣。

translations.literal: Yet these two, tested against Heaven, are quite precise.
translations.idiomatic: Both, tested against Heaven, prove precise.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「古舊渾象，以二分為一度，周七尺三寸半分。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The ancient spherical model used two fen to one degree, circumference seven chi three cun and a half fen.
translations.idiomatic: "The old spherical model used two fen per degree, circumference seven chi three cun and a half.

sentences.zh: 而莫知何代所造。

translations.literal: No one knows what age made it.
translations.idiomatic: Its age is unknown.

sentences.zh: 」今案虞喜云：「落下閎為漢孝武帝於地中轉渾天，定時節，作《泰初曆》。

translations.literal: Now examining Yu Xi's statement: "Luo Xiahong made Emperor Wu of Han turn the spherical Heaven at Earth's center to fix seasonal nodes and compose the Taichu Calendar."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi records Luo Xiahong turning spherical Heaven at Earth's center for Emperor Wu, fixing seasons and composing the Taichu Calendar.

sentences.zh: 」或其所制也。

translations.literal: Perhaps he made it.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps he made this instrument.

sentences.zh: 漢孝和帝時，太史揆候，皆以赤道儀，與天度頗有進退。

translations.literal: In Emperor He of Han's time, astrological observers all used the equatorial instrument, which differed somewhat from heavenly degrees in advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Emperor He, observers used equatorial instruments that diverged slightly from true degrees.

sentences.zh: 以問典星待詔姚崇等，皆曰《星圖》有規法，日月實從黃道。

translations.literal: They asked Palace Astronomer Yao Chong and others, who all said the Star Chart had regulated methods and sun and moon truly follow the Yellow Path.
translations.idiomatic: Asked, Yao Chong and others replied the Star Chart prescribed methods and sun and moon truly follow the Yellow Path.

sentences.zh: 官無其器。

translations.literal: The office had no such instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau lacked such an instrument.

sentences.zh: 至永元十五年，詔左中郎將賈逵乃始造太史黃道銅儀。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yongyuan, the emperor ordered Left Palace General Jia Kui to first cast the Grand Astrologer's Yellow Path bronze instrument.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan 15, Emperor He ordered Jia Kui to cast the Grand Astrologer's Yellow Path bronze instrument.

sentences.zh: 至桓帝延熹七年，太史令張衡更以銅制，以四分為一度，周天一丈四尺六寸一分。

translations.literal: In Emperor Huan's Yanxi seventh year, Grand Astrologer Zhang Heng recast it in bronze, four fen to one degree, circuit one zhang four chi six cun one fen.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 7, Zhang Heng recast it in bronze at four fen per degree, circumference one zhang four chi six cun one fen.

sentences.zh: 亦於密室中以漏水轉之，令司之者，閉戶而唱之，以告靈臺之觀天者。

translations.literal: Also in a sealed chamber turned by flowing water; the attendant closed the door and announced to observers at the Spirit Platform.
translations.idiomatic: In a sealed chamber, water-driven, an attendant closed the door and announced to Spirit Platform observers.

sentences.zh: 〔璣所加，某星始見，某星已中，某星今沒，皆如合符。

translations.literal: Where the ji pointed, a certain star first appeared, a certain star was now centered, a certain star now set—all matching tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Where the ji pointed—star rising, culminating, setting—all matched tallies.

sentences.zh: 蕃以古制局小，以布星辰，相去稠概，不得了察。

translations.literal: Fan held the ancient form too small for arraying stars—the intervals too dense for clear inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan found the ancient form too cramped to array stars clearly.

sentences.zh: 張衡所作，又複傷大，難可轉移。

translations.literal: What Zhang Heng made was again too large—hard to move.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's version was too large to move easily.

sentences.zh: 蕃今所作，以三分為一度，週一丈九寸五分、四分分之三。

translations.literal: What Fan now made uses three fen to one degree, circumference one zhang nine cun five fen and three-quarters of a quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's version used three fen per degree, circumference one zhang nine cun five fen and three quarter-fifths.

sentences.zh: 長古法三尺六寸五分、四分分之一，減衡法亦三尺六寸五分、四分分之一。

translations.literal: Three chi six cun five fen and a quarter longer than the ancient method; three chi six cun five fen and a quarter shorter than Heng's method.
translations.idiomatic: Three chi six cun five fen and a quarter longer than the ancient form; the same amount shorter than Heng's.

sentences.zh: 渾天儀法，黃赤道各廣一度有半。

translations.literal: Armillary sphere method: Yellow and red paths each one and a half degrees wide.
translations.idiomatic: By armillary method, Yellow and red paths each span one and a half degrees.

sentences.zh: 故今所作渾象，黃赤道各廣四分半，相去七寸二分。

translations.literal: Thus the spherical model now made has Yellow and red paths each four and a half fen wide, seven cun two fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's spherical model made each path four and a half fen wide, seven cun two fen apart.

sentences.zh: 又云「黃赤二道，相共交錯，其間相去二十四度。

translations.literal: It also says "Yellow and red two paths cross each other, twenty-four degrees apart between them.
translations.idiomatic: "Yellow and red paths cross, twenty-four degrees apart.

sentences.zh: 以兩儀準之，二道俱三百六十五度有奇。

translations.literal: Measured by the two principles, both paths total three hundred sixty-five degrees odd.
translations.idiomatic: By both principles each path totals three hundred sixty-five degrees odd.

sentences.zh: 又赤道見者，常一百八十二度半強。

translations.literal: Also of the equator visible, constantly one hundred eighty-two and a half strong degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The visible equator spans one hundred eighty-two and a half strong degrees.

sentences.zh: 又南北考之，天見者亦一百八十二度半強。

translations.literal: Also measured north and south, Heaven visible is also one hundred eighty-two and a half strong degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Measured north and south, visible Heaven also spans one hundred eighty-two and a half strong degrees.

sentences.zh: 是以知天之體圓如彈丸，南北極相去一百八十二度半強也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows Heaven's body is round like a pellet; north and south poles are one hundred eighty-two and a half strong degrees apart.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Heaven is round as a pellet; the poles stand one hundred eighty-two and a half strong degrees apart.

sentences.zh: 而陸績所作渾象，形如鳥卵，以施二道，不得如法。

translations.literal: Lu Ji's spherical model is shaped like a bird's egg with two paths applied—it cannot follow the method.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's egg-shaped model with two paths cannot follow proper method.

sentences.zh: 若使二道同規，則其間相去不得滿二十四度。

translations.literal: If both paths share one circle, the interval between them cannot fill twenty-four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: If both paths shared one circle, their separation could not reach twenty-four degrees.

sentences.zh: 若令相去二十四度，則黃道當長於赤道。

translations.literal: If set twenty-four degrees apart, the Yellow Path must be longer than the equator.
translations.idiomatic: Set twenty-four degrees apart, the Yellow Path would exceed the equator.

sentences.zh: 又兩極相去，不翅八十二度半強。

translations.literal: Also the two poles apart are not merely eighty-two and a half strong degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Also pole separation falls short of eighty-two and a half strong degrees.

sentences.zh: 案績說云：'天東西徑三十五萬七千里，直徑亦然。

translations.literal: Examining Ji's statement: "Heaven's east-west diameter three hundred fifty-seven thousand li, north-south diameter likewise."
translations.idiomatic: Ji wrote: "Heaven's east-west diameter is three hundred fifty-seven thousand li; north-south likewise."

sentences.zh: '則績意亦以天為正圓也。

translations.literal: Then Ji also held Heaven perfectly round.
translations.idiomatic: Ji too held Heaven perfectly round.

sentences.zh: 器與言謬，頗為乖僻。

translations.literal: Instrument and words contradict—quite perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Instrument and doctrine contradict—quite mistaken.

sentences.zh: 」然則渾天儀者，其制有機有衡。

translations.literal: Thus the armillary sphere has mechanism and crossbars.
translations.idiomatic: The armillary sphere combines mechanism and crossbars.

sentences.zh: 既動靜兼狀，以效二儀之情，又周旋衡管，用考三光之分。

translations.literal: Both moving and static aspects image the two principles; revolving cross-tubes examine the three luminaries' divisions.
translations.idiomatic: It images both principles in motion and rest and uses revolving tubes to measure the three luminaries.

sentences.zh: 所以揆正宿度，准步盈虛，求古之遺法也。

translations.literal: Therefore it rectifies lodge degrees and steps through surplus and deficit—seeking the ancient transmitted method.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it rectifies lodge degrees and tracks surplus and deficit—the ancient transmitted method.

sentences.zh: 則先儒所言圓規徑八尺，漢候臺銅儀，蔡邕所欲寢伏其下者是也。

translations.literal: What earlier scholars called the round compass eight chi in diameter, the Han observatory bronze instrument, is what Cai Yong wished to lie beneath.
translations.idiomatic: The eight-chi round compass and Han observatory bronze instrument are what Cai Yong wished to study beneath.

sentences.zh: 梁華林重雲殿前所置銅儀，其制則有雙環規相並，間相去三寸許，正豎當子午。

translations.literal: The bronze instrument placed before Chongyun Hall at Hualin in Liang had paired ring compasses side by side, about three cun apart, upright at meridian.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Chongyun Hall bronze instrument had paired rings three cun apart, upright on the meridian.

sentences.zh: 其子午之間，應南北極之衡，各合而為孔，以象南北樞。

translations.literal: Between meridian points corresponding to north-south polar axis, each joined as a hole imaging north-south pivots.
translations.idiomatic: Meridian holes imaged the north-south pivots.

sentences.zh: 植楗於前後以屬焉。

translations.literal: Tenons planted front and rear attached to them.
translations.idiomatic: Tenons front and rear attached to them.

sentences.zh: 又有單橫規，高下正當渾之半。

translations.literal: Also a single transverse compass, high and low exactly at the sphere's half.
translations.idiomatic: A single transverse ring sat at the sphere's midpoint.

sentences.zh: 皆周市分為度數；

translations.literal: All circled and divided into degrees;
translations.idiomatic: All were circled and marked in degrees;

sentences.zh: 署以維辰之位，以象地。

translations.literal: marked with lodge positions to image Earth.
translations.idiomatic: marked with lodge positions to image Earth.

sentences.zh: 又有單規，斜帶南北之中，與春秋二分之日道相應。

translations.literal: Also a single compass slanting through north-south center, corresponding to the spring and autumn equinox sun path.
translations.idiomatic: A slanting ring through north-south center matched the equinox sun path.

sentences.zh: 亦周匝分為度數，而署以維辰，並相連者。

translations.literal: Also circled and divided into degrees, marked with lodges, all linked together.
translations.idiomatic: Also circled, divided, and marked with lodges, all linked.

sentences.zh: 屬楗植而不動。

translations.literal: Attached to fixed tenons without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed to immobile tenons.

sentences.zh: 其裡又有雙規相並，如外雙規。

translations.literal: Inside were also paired compasses side by side, like the outer pair.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, paired rings like the outer pair.

sentences.zh: 內徑八尺，週二丈四尺，而屬雙軸。

translations.literal: Inner diameter eight chi, circumference two zhang four chi, attached to paired axles.
translations.idiomatic: Inner diameter eight chi, circumference two zhang four chi, on paired axles.

sentences.zh: 軸兩頭出規外各二寸許，合兩為一。

translations.literal: Axle ends projected two cun beyond the compass, joining into one.
translations.idiomatic: Axle ends projected two cun and joined as one.

sentences.zh: 內有孔，圓徑二寸許，南頭入地下，注於外雙規南樞孔中，以象南極。

translations.literal: Inner hole two cun diameter; south end entered Earth, set in outer south pivot hole imaging the South Pole.
translations.idiomatic: A two-cun hole: south end entered Earth at the outer south pivot, imaging the South Pole.

sentences.zh: 北頭出地上，入於外雙規北樞孔中，以象北極。

translations.literal: North end rose above Earth into outer north pivot hole imaging the North Pole.
translations.idiomatic: North end rose into the outer north pivot, imaging the North Pole.

sentences.zh: 其運動得東西轉，以象天行。

translations.literal: Its motion could turn east-west to image Heaven's motion.
translations.idiomatic: It turned east-west to image Heaven's motion.

sentences.zh: 其雙軸之間，則置衡，長八尺，通中有孔，圓徑一寸。

translations.literal: Between the paired axles a crossbar eight chi long was set, pierced by a one-cun round hole.
translations.idiomatic: Between axles an eight-chi crossbar with a one-cun hole was set.

sentences.zh: 當衡之半，兩邊有關，各注著雙軸。

translations.literal: At the crossbar's half, hinges on both sides attached to the paired axles.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-crossbar hinges attached to both axles.

sentences.zh: 衡即隨天象東西轉運，又自於雙軸間得南北低仰。

translations.literal: The crossbar turned east-west with the sky and also tilted north-south between the axles.
translations.idiomatic: The crossbar turned with the sky and tilted north-south between axles.

sentences.zh: 所以准驗辰曆，分考次度，其於揆測，唯所欲為之者也。

translations.literal: Thus it verified the calendar, divided and examined degrees—for observation, whatever one wished.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it verified the calendar and measured degrees as desired.

sentences.zh: 檢其鐫題，是偽劉曜光初六年，史官丞南陽孔挺所造，則古之渾儀之法者也。

translations.literal: Checking its inscription: falsely dated Liu Yao Guangchu 6, made by Astrological Officer Assistant Kong Ting of Nanyang—the ancient armillary method.
translations.idiomatic: Its inscription falsely dated it Liu Yao Guangchu 6 by Astrological Assistant Kong Ting of Nanyang—the ancient armillary method.

sentences.zh: 而宋御史中丞何承天及太中大夫徐爰，各著《宋史》，咸以為即張衡所造。

translations.literal: Song Censor-in-Chief He Chengtian and Grand Counselor Xu Ai each wrote the Song History, both holding it was what Zhang Heng made.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian and Xu Ai both wrote it was Zhang Heng's work.

sentences.zh: 其儀略舉天狀，而不綴經星七曜。

translations.literal: Its instrument briefly showed Heaven's form but did not array fixed stars and seven luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: It showed Heaven's form but omitted fixed stars and seven luminaries.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉喪亂，沉沒西戎。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin turmoil sank it in the Western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei-Jin chaos sank it in the Western Rong.

sentences.zh: 義熙十四年，宋高祖定咸陽得之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yixi, Song Gaozu recovered it when settling Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 14, Song Gaozu recovered it at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 梁尚書沈約著《宋史》，亦云然，皆失之遠矣。

translations.literal: Liang Minister Shen Yue's Song History also says so—all far off the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue's Song History agrees—all mistaken.

sentences.zh: 後魏道武天興初，命太史令晁崇修渾儀，以觀星象。

translations.literal: Later Wei Emperor Daowu in Tianxing初 ordered Grand Astrologer Chao Chong to repair the armillary sphere to observe stars.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Daowu in Tianxing初 ordered Chao Chong to repair the armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 十有餘載，至明元永興四年壬子，詔造太史候部鐵儀，以為渾天法，考〔璣之正。

translations.literal: After more than ten years, in Mingyuan Yongxing 4 renchen, an edict cast the Astrological Bureau iron instrument as spherical Heaven method to verify ji correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later, Yongxing 4 renchen, an edict cast the iron Astrological Bureau instrument as spherical Heaven method.

sentences.zh: 其銘曰；

translations.literal: Its inscription reads:
translations.idiomatic: Its inscription reads:

sentences.zh: 「於皇大代，配天比祚。

translations.literal: "In the august Great Dynasty, matching Heaven and comparing fortune.
translations.idiomatic: "In the august Great Dynasty, matching Heaven and fortune.

sentences.zh: 赫赫明明，聲烈遐布。

translations.literal: Brilliant and bright, fame spreading afar.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant and bright, fame spreading afar.

sentences.zh: 爰造茲器，考正宿度。

translations.literal: Thus making this instrument, verifying lodge degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Thus making this instrument to verify lodge degrees.

sentences.zh: 貽法後葉，永垂典故。

translations.literal: Leaving method for later generations, eternally transmitting the canonical example."
translations.idiomatic: Leaving method for posterity, eternally transmitting the canonical example."

sentences.zh: 」其制並以銅鐵，唯志星度以銀錯之。

translations.literal: Its form all copper and iron; only star degrees marked in silver inlay.
translations.idiomatic: Copper and iron throughout; star degrees inlaid in silver.

sentences.zh: 南北柱曲抱雙規，東西柱直立，下有十字水準，以植四柱。

translations.literal: North-south pillars curved embracing paired compasses; east-west pillars upright; below a cross water level to plant the four pillars.
translations.idiomatic: Curved north-south pillars embraced paired rings; east-west pillars stood upright on a cross water level.

sentences.zh: 十字之上，以龜負雙規。

translations.literal: On the cross, a tortoise bore the paired compasses.
translations.idiomatic: A tortoise on the cross bore the paired rings.

sentences.zh: 其餘皆與劉曜儀大同。

translations.literal: The rest largely matches Liu Yao's instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The rest largely matches Liu Yao's instrument.

sentences.zh: 即今太史候臺所用也。

translations.literal: This is what the Grand Astrologer's observatory platform uses today.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the observatory platform uses today.

sentences.zh: ○渾天象

translations.literal: The Spherical Model
translations.idiomatic: The Spherical Model

sentences.zh: 渾天象者，其制有機而無衡，梁末秘府有，以木為之。

translations.literal: The spherical model has mechanism but no crossbars; Liang's secret repository had one made of wood.
translations.idiomatic: The spherical model has mechanism but no crossbars; Liang's secret repository held a wooden one.

sentences.zh: 其圓如丸，其大數圍。

translations.literal: Its form is round like a pellet, its size several arm-spans in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: Round as a pellet, several arm-spans around.

sentences.zh: 南北兩頭有軸。

translations.literal: North and south ends have axles.
translations.idiomatic: Axles project from north and south ends.

sentences.zh: 遍體布二十八宿、三家星、黃赤二道及天漢等。

translations.literal: The whole body arrays the twenty-eight lodges, three schools' stars, Yellow and red two paths, and the Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: Its surface bears the twenty-eight lodges, three schools' stars, both paths, and the Milky Way.

sentences.zh: 別為橫規環，以匡其外。

translations.literal: Separately a transverse ring compass girds the outside.
translations.idiomatic: A transverse ring girds the exterior.

sentences.zh: 高下管之，以象地。

translations.literal: High and low tubes control it to image Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Tubes above and below control it to image Earth.

sentences.zh: 南軸頭入地，注于南植，以象南極。

translations.literal: The south axle end enters Earth, set in the south pillar, imaging the South Pole.
translations.idiomatic: The south axle enters Earth at the south pillar, imaging the South Pole.

sentences.zh: 北軸頭出於地上，注於北植，以象北極。

translations.literal: The north axle end rises above Earth, set in the north pillar, imaging the North Pole.
translations.idiomatic: The north axle rises at the north pillar, imaging the North Pole.

sentences.zh: 正東西運轉。

translations.literal: It turns due east-west.
translations.idiomatic: It rotates east-west.

sentences.zh: 昏明中星，既其應度，分至氣節，亦驗，在不差而已。

translations.literal: Stars centered at dusk and dawn match their degrees; solstices, equinoxes, and seasonal qi are also verified—without error.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk and dawn centered stars match their degrees; solstices, equinoxes, and seasonal nodes verify without error.

sentences.zh: 不如渾儀，別有衡管，測揆日月，分步星度者也。

translations.literal: Unlike the armillary sphere, it lacks separate cross-tubes for measuring sun and moon and stepping star degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Unlike the armillary sphere, it lacks cross-tubes for measuring sun, moon, and star degrees.

sentences.zh: 吳太史令陳卓云：「先賢制木為儀，名曰渾天。

translations.literal: Wu Grand Astrologer Chen Zhuo said: "Earlier sages made wood into an instrument called Spherical Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhuo of Wu said: "Ancient sages made a wooden instrument called Spherical Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」即此之謂耶？

translations.literal: Is this what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: Is this what he meant?

sentences.zh: 由斯而言，儀象二器，遠不相涉。

translations.literal: From this speaking, the two instruments sphere and model are far from involving each other.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the armillary sphere and spherical model are distinct instruments.

sentences.zh: 則張衡所造，蓋亦止在渾象七曜，而何承天莫辨儀象之異，亦為乖失。

translations.literal: Then what Zhang Heng made was probably only the seven luminaries on the spherical model—yet He Chengtian did not distinguish sphere from model; this too is error.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng likely made only the spherical model's seven luminaries—He Chengtian's failure to distinguish the instruments was also an error.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝以元嘉十三年詔太史更造渾儀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song in Yuanjia 13 ordered the Grand Astrologer to recast the armillary sphere.
translations.idiomatic: Song Emperor Wen in Yuanjia 13 ordered a new armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 太史令錢樂之依案舊說，采效儀象，鑄銅為之。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Qian Lezhi followed old doctrine, adopting sphere and model methods, casting it in bronze.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Qian Lezhi cast bronze following old sphere and model methods.

sentences.zh: 五分為一度，徑六尺八分少，週一丈八尺二寸六分少。

translations.literal: Five fen to one degree; diameter six chi eight fen odd, circumference one zhang eight chi two cun six fen odd.
translations.idiomatic: Five fen per degree; diameter six chi eight fen odd, circumference one zhang eight chi two cun six fen odd.

sentences.zh: 地在天內，不動。

translations.literal: Earth inside Heaven, unmoving.
translations.idiomatic: Earth rests inside Heaven, unmoving.

sentences.zh: 立黃赤二道之規，南北二極之規，布列二十八宿、北斗極星。

translations.literal: Yellow and red path compasses and north-south pole compasses erected; twenty-eight lodges and Northern Dipper pole stars arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Compasses for both paths and both poles; twenty-eight lodges and pole stars arrayed.

sentences.zh: 置日月五星于黃道上。

translations.literal: Sun, moon, and five planets placed on the Yellow Path.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and five planets set on the Yellow Path.

sentences.zh: 為之杠軸，以象天運。

translations.literal: Axles made for it to image Heaven's motion.
translations.idiomatic: Axles image Heaven's motion.

sentences.zh: 昏明中星，與天相符。

translations.literal: Stars centered at dusk and dawn match Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk and dawn stars match Heaven.

sentences.zh: 梁末，置於文德殿前。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, placed before Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At Liang's end it stood before Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 至如斯制，以為渾儀，儀則內闕衡管。

translations.literal: Made thus, as armillary sphere it lacks inner cross-tubes.
translations.idiomatic: As an armillary sphere it lacked inner cross-tubes.

sentences.zh: 以為渾象，而地不在外。

translations.literal: As spherical model, Earth is not outside.
translations.idiomatic: As a spherical model, Earth was not placed outside.

sentences.zh: 是參兩法，別為一體。

translations.literal: Combining two methods, it became a separate whole.
translations.idiomatic: It combined two methods into one hybrid instrument.

sentences.zh: 就器用而求，猶渾象之流，外內天地之狀，不失其位也。

translations.literal: Judging by use, it remains of the spherical model type—the inner-outer form of Heaven and Earth not losing position.
translations.idiomatic: In use it remained a spherical model—Heaven and Earth's inner-outer relation preserved.

sentences.zh: 吳時又有葛衡，明達天官，能為機巧。

translations.literal: In Wu there was also Ge Heng, skilled in celestial offices and ingenious in mechanism.
translations.idiomatic: Wu also had Ge Heng, expert in astronomy and ingenious in mechanism.

sentences.zh: 改作渾天，使地居於天中。

translations.literal: He remade Spherical Heaven with Earth at Heaven's center.
translations.idiomatic: He remade Spherical Heaven with Earth at center.

sentences.zh: 以機動之，天動而地止，以上應晷度，則樂之之所放述也。

translations.literal: Turned by mechanism—Heaven moves and Earth stops—to correspond above with gnomon degrees; this is what Lezhi described.
translations.idiomatic: Mechanism turned Heaven while Earth stayed still, matching gnomon degrees—what Lezhi described.

sentences.zh: 到元嘉十七年，又作小渾天，二分為一度，徑二尺二寸，週六尺六寸。

translations.literal: By Yuanjia 17 he also made a small Spherical Heaven, two fen to one degree, diameter two chi two cun, circumference six chi six cun.
translations.idiomatic: By Yuanjia 17 he made a small sphere at two fen per degree, diameter two chi two cun.

sentences.zh: 安二十八宿中外官星備足。

translations.literal: Twenty-eight lodges and inner and outer official stars fully installed.
translations.idiomatic: All twenty-eight lodges and inner and outer official stars were installed.

sentences.zh: 以白青黃等三色珠為三家星。

translations.literal: White, green, and yellow beads marked the three schools' stars.
translations.idiomatic: White, green, and yellow beads distinguished the three schools.

sentences.zh: 其日月五星，悉居黃道。

translations.literal: Sun, moon, and five planets all on the Yellow Path.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and five planets all rode the Yellow Path.

sentences.zh: 亦象天運，而地在其中。

translations.literal: Also imaging Heaven's motion with Earth within.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's motion was imaged with Earth inside.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉所造儀象器，開皇九年平陳後，併入長安。

translations.literal: The Yuanjia instrument made in Liu Song, after pacifying Chen in Kaihuang 9, was brought together to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song's Yuanjia instrument entered Chang'an after Chen was pacified in Kaihuang 9.

sentences.zh: 大業初，移於東都觀象殿。

translations.literal: At the start of Daye it was moved to the Observational Hall at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Daye's start it moved to the Eastern Capital's Observational Hall.

sentences.zh: ○蓋圖

translations.literal: The Canopy Chart
translations.idiomatic: The Canopy Chart

sentences.zh: 晉侍中劉智云：「顓頊造渾儀，黃帝為蓋天。

translations.literal: Jin Palace Attendant Liu Zhi said: "Zhuanxu made the armillary sphere; the Yellow Emperor made Canopy Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi of Jin said: "Zhuanxu made the armillary sphere; the Yellow Emperor made Canopy Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」然此二器，皆古之所制，但傳說義者，失其用耳。

translations.literal: Yet both instruments are anciently made—only those transmitting the meaning lost their use.
translations.idiomatic: Both are ancient instruments—later transmitters lost their proper use.

sentences.zh: 昔者聖王正曆明時，作圓蓋以圓列宿。

translations.literal: Formerly the sage king rectified the calendar and clarified the seasons, making a round canopy to array the lodges in a circle.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sage kings rectified the calendar and made a round canopy chart to array the lodges.

sentences.zh: 極在其中，回之以觀天象。

translations.literal: The pole within, turning it to observe celestial phenomena.
translations.idiomatic: The pole stood within; turning the chart observed the sky.

sentences.zh: 分三百六十五度、四分度之一，以定日數。

translations.literal: Divided three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter degrees to fix day numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred sixty-five and a quarter degrees fixed the day count.

sentences.zh: 日行于星紀，轉回右行，故圓規之，以為日行道。

translations.literal: The sun travels in Star Record, turning back moving right—thus circled with a compass as the sun's path.
translations.idiomatic: The sun travels the Star Record path—circled with a compass as its road.

sentences.zh: 欲明其四時所在，故於春也，則以青為道；

translations.literal: To show where the four seasons lie, in spring the path is marked green;
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal paths were color-coded: green for spring;

sentences.zh: 于夏也，則以赤為道；

translations.literal: in summer, red;
translations.idiomatic: red for summer;

sentences.zh: 于秋也，則以白為道；

translations.literal: in autumn, white;
translations.idiomatic: white for autumn;

sentences.zh: 于冬也，則以黑為道。

translations.literal: in winter, black.
translations.idiomatic: black for winter.

sentences.zh: 四季之末，各十八日，則以黃為道。

translations.literal: At each season's end, eighteen days each, yellow marks the path.
translations.idiomatic: The last eighteen days of each season were marked yellow.

sentences.zh: 蓋圖已定，仰觀雖明，而未可正昏明，分晝夜，故作渾儀，以象天體。

translations.literal: Once the canopy chart was fixed, looking up was clear, yet one could not fix dusk and dawn or divide day and night—thus the armillary sphere was made to image Heaven's body.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy chart clarified the sky but could not fix dusk, dawn, or day-night division—hence the armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 今案自開皇已後，天下一統，靈臺以後魏鐵渾天儀，測七曜盈縮，以蓋圖列星坐，分黃赤二道距二十八宿分度，而莫有更為渾象者矣。

translations.literal: Now examining from Kaihuang onward, the realm unified—the Spirit Platform used Northern Wei's iron armillary sphere to measure the seven luminaries' surplus and deficit, the canopy chart to array star seats, dividing Yellow and red two paths and twenty-eight lodge degrees—and none made a new spherical model.
translations.idiomatic: From Kaihuang onward the realm was unified: the Spirit Platform used Northern Wei's iron armillary sphere for the seven luminaries and the canopy chart for star positions—no new spherical model was made.

sentences.zh: 仁壽四年，河間劉焯造《皇極曆》，上啓於東宮。

translations.literal: In Renshou 4, Liu Zhuo of Hejian made the Huangji Calendar and presented it to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou 4, Liu Zhuo of Hejian presented the Huangji Calendar to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 論渾天云：

translations.literal: On Spherical Heaven:
translations.idiomatic: On Spherical Heaven:

sentences.zh: 璿璣玉衡，正天之器，帝王欽若，世傳其象。

translations.literal: Xuanji-yuheng—the instrument rectifying Heaven; emperors reverently conform; generations transmit its form.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanji-yuheng rectifies Heaven; emperors reverently conform; generations transmit its form.

sentences.zh: 漢之孝武，詳考律曆，糾落下閎、鮮于妄人等，共所營定。

translations.literal: Han's Emperor Wu carefully examined pitch pipes and calendar, correcting Luo Xiahong, Xianyu Wangren, and others who jointly established it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu corrected Luo Xiahong, Xianyu Wangren, and others who jointly established the system.

sentences.zh: 逮于張衡，又尋述作，亦其體制，不異閎等。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhang Heng, he again pursued composition—its system no different from Hong and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng continued the tradition in the same system.

sentences.zh: 雖閎制莫存，而衡造有器。

translations.literal: Though Hong's form does not survive, Heng's casting has an instrument.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's form is lost, but Heng's instrument survives.

sentences.zh: 至吳時，陸績、王蕃，並要修鑄。

translations.literal: In Wu times, Lu Ji and Wang Fan both intended to recast.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Lu Ji and Wang Fan both recast instruments.

sentences.zh: 績小有異，蕃乃事同。

translations.literal: Ji differed slightly; Fan's work was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Ji differed slightly; Fan matched the standard.

sentences.zh: 宋有錢樂之，魏初晁崇等，總用銅鐵，小大有殊，規域經模，不異蕃造。

translations.literal: Song had Qian Lezhi; early Wei had Chao Chong and others—all used copper and iron, large and small differing, yet compass scope and warp pattern not differing from Fan's making.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Qian Lezhi and early Wei's Chao Chong used copper and iron in varied sizes but followed Fan's pattern.

sentences.zh: 觀蔡邕《月令章句》，鄭玄注《考靈曜》，勢同衡法，迄今不改。

translations.literal: Examining Cai Yong's Monthly Ordinance Commentary and Zheng Xuan's Kao Ling Yao commentary, the tendency matches Heng's method—unchanged to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong and Zheng Xuan follow Heng's method—unchanged to this day.

sentences.zh: 焯以愚管，留情推測，見其數制，莫不違爽。

translations.literal: Zhuo with limited insight applied himself to inference—seeing its numbers and system, none did not violate and miss.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo examined the system and found every measure in error.

sentences.zh: 失之千里，差若毫釐，大象一乖，余何可驗。

translations.literal: Missing by a thousand li, differing by hairs—once the great image is wrong, what else can be verified?
translations.idiomatic: Miss by a thousand li over hairsbreadth—once the great image fails, nothing verifies.

sentences.zh: 況赤黃均度，月無出入，至所恆定，氣不別衡。

translations.literal: Moreover red and yellow equal in degrees, the moon without entering and exiting, solstice points fixed, qi not distinguishing crossbars.
translations.idiomatic: Red and yellow paths equal in degrees; the moon never enters or exits; solstice points fixed; crossbars fail to distinguish qi.

sentences.zh: 分刻本差，輪回守故。

translations.literal: Clepsydra marks originally wrong, wheels returning to the old.
translations.idiomatic: Clepsydra marks were wrong; wheels merely preserved the old errors.

sentences.zh: 其為疏謬，不可複言。

translations.literal: Its looseness and error cannot be spoken again.
translations.idiomatic: The errors are beyond recounting.

sentences.zh: 亦既由理不明，致使異家間出。

translations.literal: Also because principle was unclear, different schools arose among men.
translations.idiomatic: Unclear principle spawned rival schools.

sentences.zh: 蓋及宣夜，三說並驅，平、昕、安、穹，四天騰沸。

translations.literal: Canopy and Overnight, three theories driving together; Ping, Xin, An, Qiong—four Heavens boiling.
translations.idiomatic: Canopy, Overnight, and Spherical Heaven competed; Ping, Xin, An, and Qiong theories proliferated.

sentences.zh: 至當不二，理唯一揆，豈容天體，七種殊說？

translations.literal: What should be singular and not dual, principle having one standard—how can Heaven's body have seven different theories?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven should have one standard—how can seven theories coexist?

sentences.zh: 又影漏去極，就渾可推，百骸共體，本非異物。

translations.literal: Also shadow, clepsydra, and distance from the pole can be derived from the sphere—one body sharing all parts, originally not different things.
translations.idiomatic: Shadow, clepsydra, and polar distance derive from one sphere—one body, not separate things.

sentences.zh: 此真已驗，彼偽自彰，豈朗日未暉，爝火不息，理有而闕，詎不可悲者也？

translations.literal: The true already verified, the false self-revealed—can bright sun not shine while torch fire does not cease? Principle exists yet is lacking—is this not lamentable?
translations.idiomatic: Truth verified, falsehood exposed—must bright sun wait for torches? To have principle yet lack it is lamentable.

sentences.zh: 昔蔡邕自朔方上書曰：「以八尺之儀，度知天地之象，古有其器，而無其書。

translations.literal: Formerly Cai Yong from Shuofang submitted a memorial: "With an eight-chi instrument, measure and know Heaven and Earth's image—anciently there was the instrument but no book.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong from Shuofang wrote: "An eight-chi instrument can measure Heaven and Earth's image—the instrument existed but no book."

sentences.zh: 常欲寢伏儀下，案度成數，而為立說。

translations.literal: I always wished to lie beneath the instrument, arrange degrees into numbers, and establish doctrine."
translations.idiomatic: He wished to lie beneath it, derive the numbers, and write doctrine."

sentences.zh: 」邕以負罪朔裔，書奏不許。

translations.literal: Yong, bearing guilt in the northern frontier, memorial not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's memorial was denied because he was exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 邕若蒙許，亦必不能。

translations.literal: Even if Yong had been permitted, he surely could not have done it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if permitted, he could not have succeeded.

sentences.zh: 邕才不逾張衡，衡本豈有遺思也？

translations.literal: Yong's talent did not exceed Zhang Heng—did Heng originally have leftover thought?
translations.idiomatic: Yong's talent did not exceed Zhang Heng—did Heng leave the problem unfinished?

sentences.zh: 則有器無書，觀不能悟。

translations.literal: Then having instrument without book, observation cannot enlighten.
translations.idiomatic: Instrument without book—observation cannot enlighten.

sentences.zh: 焯今立術，改正舊渾。

translations.literal: Zhuo now establishes method, correcting the old sphere.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo now establishes method to correct the old sphere.

sentences.zh: 又以二至之影，定去極晷漏，並天地高遠，星辰運周，所宗有本，皆有其率。

translations.literal: Also using solstice shadows to fix distance from pole, gnomon clepsydra, together with Heaven and Earth's height and distance, stars' circuit—all honored have root, all have their rates.
translations.idiomatic: Using solstice shadows he fixes polar distance, gnomon clepsydra, Heaven-Earth height, and stellar circuit—all with proper rates.

sentences.zh: 祛今賢之巨惑，稽往哲之群疑，豁若雲披，朗如霧散。

translations.literal: Removing today's worthies' great confusion, examining past sages' crowd of doubts—open as clouds part, clear as mist disperses.
translations.idiomatic: He clears today's confusion and past sages' doubts—as clouds part and mist clears.

sentences.zh: 為之錯綜，數卷已成，待得影差，謹更起送。

translations.literal: Composing it in several scrolls already complete—awaiting shadow difference, respectfully to send again.
translations.idiomatic: Several scrolls are complete; he awaits shadow measurements to send them.

sentences.zh: 又云：「《周官》夏至日影，尺有五寸。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Zhou Offices' summer solstice shadow is one chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted: "Zhou Offices give summer solstice shadow as one chi five cun.

sentences.zh: 張衡、鄭玄、王番、陸績先儒等，皆以為影千里差一寸。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng, Zheng Xuan, Wang Fan, Lu Ji and earlier scholars all held shadow differs one cun per thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng, Zheng Xuan, Wang Fan, and Lu Ji held shadow differs one cun per thousand li.

sentences.zh: 言南戴日下萬五千里，表影正同，天高乃異。

translations.literal: Saying south of the cap at the sun's nadir ten thousand five thousand li, gnomon shadows exactly match, yet Heaven's height differs.
translations.idiomatic: They said ten thousand five thousand li south of the cap shadows match yet Heaven's height differs.

sentences.zh: 考之演算法，必為不可。

translations.literal: Examining calculation methods, this must be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation proves this impossible.

sentences.zh: 寸差千里，亦無典說，明為意斷，事不可依。

translations.literal: One cun difference per thousand li has no canonical doctrine—clearly arbitrary judgment, the matter cannot be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: One cun per thousand li lacks canonical support—it is arbitrary.

sentences.zh: 今交、愛之州，表北無影，計無萬里，南過戴日。

translations.literal: Now Jiao and Ai provinces—north of the gnomon no shadow, calculating not ten thousand li, yet south past the cap.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao and Ai provinces show no shadow north of the gnomon—not ten thousand li yet south of the cap.

sentences.zh: 是千里一寸，非其實差。

translations.literal: Thus one cun per thousand li is not the actual difference.
translations.idiomatic: One cun per thousand li is not the true rate.

sentences.zh: 焯今說渾，以道為率，道裡不定，得差乃審。

translations.literal: Zhuo now explains the sphere using the path as rate—path li unfixed, obtaining difference then verifies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo uses the path as rate—fixed li unknown until difference is measured.

sentences.zh: 既大聖之年，升平之日，厘改群謬，斯正其時。

translations.literal: Since it is the great sage's year and ascending peace's day, correcting crowd errors—this is the right time.
translations.idiomatic: In an age of sage rule and ascending peace, correcting errors is timely.

sentences.zh: 請一水工並解算術士，取河南、北平地之所，可量數百里，南北使正。

translations.literal: I request one waterworks craftsman and one mathematician, taking level ground north and south of the Yellow River measurable for several hundred li, aligned north-south.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a surveyor and mathematician on level ground north and south of the Yellow River for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 審時以漏，平地以繩，隨氣至分，同日度影。

translations.literal: Fix time by clepsydra, level ground by cord, following qi to the minute, same day measuring shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Fix time by clepsydra, level by cord, measure shadows on the same day.

sentences.zh: 得其差率，裡即可知。

translations.literal: Obtain the difference rate and li can be known.
translations.idiomatic: From the difference rate, li can be known.

sentences.zh: 則天地無所匿其形，辰象無所逃其數，超前顯聖，效象除疑。

translations.literal: Then Heaven and Earth cannot hide their form, stars cannot escape their numbers—surpassing the past, displaying the image, removing doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Then Heaven and Earth cannot hide their form and stars cannot escape their numbers.

sentences.zh: 請勿以人廢言。

translations.literal: Please do not reject words because of the man."
translations.idiomatic: Do not reject the proposal because of the proposer."

sentences.zh: 」不用。

translations.literal: Not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: It was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 至大業三年，敕諸郡測影，而焯尋卒，事遂寢廢。

translations.literal: By Daye 3, an edict ordered all commanderies to measure shadows—but Zhuo soon died and the matter was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye 3 an edict ordered shadow measurement—but Zhuo died and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: ○地中

translations.literal: Earth's Center
translations.idiomatic: Earth's Center

sentences.zh: 《周禮·大司徒職》：「以土圭之法，測土深，正日景，以求地中。

translations.literal: Rites of Zhou, Grand Steward's Duties: "By the earth-tablet method, measure earth's depth, rectify the sun's shadow, to seek Earth's center."
translations.idiomatic: Rites of Zhou, Grand Steward: "By the earth-tablet method, measure depth and rectify the sun's shadow to find Earth's center."

sentences.zh: 」此則渾天之正說，立儀象之大本。

translations.literal: This is Spherical Heaven's correct doctrine, establishing instruments and models' great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: This is Spherical Heaven's correct doctrine—the foundation of instruments and models.

sentences.zh: 故云：「日南則景短多暑，日北則景長多寒，日東則景夕多風，日西則景朝多陰。

translations.literal: Thus it says: "When the sun is south, shadow is short and heat abundant; when north, shadow long and cold abundant; when east, shadow at evening and wind abundant; when west, shadow at morning and yin abundant.
translations.idiomatic: It says: "Sun south—short shadow, much heat; north—long shadow, much cold; east—evening shadow, much wind; west—morning shadow, much yin.

sentences.zh: 日至之景，尺有五寸，謂之地中。

translations.literal: At solstice the shadow is one chi five cun—this is called Earth's center.
translations.idiomatic: Solstice shadow one chi five cun marks Earth's center.

sentences.zh: 天地之所合也。

translations.literal: Where Heaven and Earth meet.
translations.idiomatic: Where Heaven and Earth converge.

sentences.zh: 四時之所交也，風雨之所會也，陰陽之所和也。

translations.literal: Where the four seasons cross, where wind and rain gather, where yin and yang harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Where seasons cross, wind and rain gather, and yin and yang harmonize.

sentences.zh: 然則百物阜安，乃建王國焉。

translations.literal: Then the hundred things flourish in peace—and the royal state is established.
translations.idiomatic: Then all things flourish and the royal state is founded.

sentences.zh: 」又《考工記·匠人》：「建國，水地以縣。

translations.literal: " Also Records of the Craftsman, Artisan: "Establishing the state, level the ground with plumb line.
translations.idiomatic: Records of the Craftsman: "Establishing the state, level ground with a plumb line.

sentences.zh: 置Ｓ以縣，眡以景。

translations.literal: Set the gnomon with plumb line, view by shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Set the gnomon plumb and read its shadow.

sentences.zh: 為規，識日出之景與日入之景。

translations.literal: Make a compass, mark sunrise shadow and sunset shadow.
translations.idiomatic: With a compass mark sunrise and sunset shadows.

sentences.zh: 晝參諸日中之景，夜考之極星，以正朝夕。

translations.literal: By day refer to midday shadow; by night examine the pole star—to rectify morning and evening."
translations.idiomatic: By day use midday shadow; by night the pole star—to fix morning and evening."

sentences.zh: 」案土圭正影，經文闕略，先儒解說，又非明審。

translations.literal: Examining earth-tablet shadow rectification, the classic text is deficient; earlier scholars' explanations are also not clear and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Classic texts on the earth-tablet method are incomplete; earlier explanations are unclear.

sentences.zh: 祖暅錯綜經注，以推地中。

translations.literal: Zu Geng synthesized classic and commentary to derive Earth's center.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Geng synthesized classics and commentaries to find Earth's center.

sentences.zh: 其法曰：「先驗昏旦，定刻漏，分辰次。

translations.literal: His method says: "First verify dusk and dawn, fix clepsydra marks, divide chronogram positions.
translations.idiomatic: His method: "First fix dusk and dawn and clepsydra marks, dividing chronogram positions.

sentences.zh: 乃立儀錶于准平之地，名曰南表。

translations.literal: Then erect an instrument on level ground called the south gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: Erect an instrument on level ground—the south gnomon.

sentences.zh: 漏刻上水，居日之中，更立一表于南表影末，名曰中表。

translations.literal: Clepsydra rising, at the sun's center erect another gnomon at the south gnomon's shadow tip called the center gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: At solar noon erect a center gnomon at the south gnomon's shadow tip.

sentences.zh: 夜依中表，以望北極樞，而立北表，令參相直。

translations.literal: At night by the center gnomon sight the North Pole Pivot and erect the north gnomon, making all three align.
translations.idiomatic: At night sight the North Pole Pivot from the center gnomon and erect the north gnomon aligned.

sentences.zh: 三表皆以懸准定，乃觀。

translations.literal: All three gnomons fixed by plumb line—then observe.
translations.idiomatic: All three fixed plumb—then observe.

sentences.zh: 三表直者，其立表之地，即當子午之正。

translations.literal: When three gnomons align straight, the gnomon site is on true meridian.
translations.idiomatic: Straight alignment marks true meridian.

sentences.zh: 三表曲者，地偏僻。

translations.literal: When three gnomons bend, the ground is off-center.
translations.idiomatic: Bent alignment means off-center ground.

sentences.zh: 每觀中表，以知所偏。

translations.literal: Each time observing the center gnomon to know the deviation.
translations.idiomatic: Observe the center gnomon to detect deviation.

sentences.zh: 中表在西，則立表處在地中之西，當更向東求地中。

translations.literal: Center gnomon west—the site is west of Earth's center; seek center eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Center gnomon west—site is west of center; move east.

sentences.zh: 若中表在東，則立表處在地中之東也，當更向西求地中。

translations.literal: If center gnomon east—the site is east of Earth's center; seek center westward.
translations.idiomatic: Center gnomon east—site is east of center; move west.

sentences.zh: 取三表直者，為地中之正。

translations.literal: Take where three gnomons align straight as true Earth's center.
translations.idiomatic: True center is where all three align straight.

sentences.zh: 又以春秋二分之日，旦始出東方半體，乃立表於中表之東，名曰東表。

translations.literal: Also on spring and autumn equinox days, when the sun first shows half its body in the east, erect a gnomon east of the center gnomon called the east gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: At equinox, when half the sun shows in the east, erect an east gnomon east of center.

sentences.zh: 令東表與日及中表參相直。

translations.literal: Make east gnomon, sun, and center gnomon align.
translations.idiomatic: Align east gnomon, sun, and center gnomon.

sentences.zh: 視日之夕，日入西方半體，又立表於中表之西，名曰西表。

translations.literal: At evening when half the sun sets west, erect a gnomon west of center called the west gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: At evening half-sunset, erect a west gnomon west of center.

sentences.zh: 亦從中表西望西表及日，參相直。

translations.literal: Also from center gnomon sight west to west gnomon and sun, all aligned.
translations.idiomatic: From center, align west gnomon and setting sun.

sentences.zh: 乃觀三表直者，即地南北之中也。

translations.literal: When three gnomons align straight, this is true north-south center.
translations.idiomatic: Straight three gnomons mark true north-south center.

sentences.zh: 若中表差近南，則所測之地在卯酉之南。

translations.literal: If center gnomon deviates south, the measured ground is south of mao-you.
translations.idiomatic: Center gnomon south of line—site is south of mao-you.

sentences.zh: 中表差在北，則所測之地在卯酉之北。

translations.literal: Center gnomon deviates north—the measured ground is north of mao-you.
translations.idiomatic: Center gnomon north—site is north of mao-you.

sentences.zh: 進退南北，求三表直正東西者，則其地處中，居卯酉之正也。

translations.literal: Adjusting north-south, seeking three gnomons straight east-west, the ground is centered on true mao-you."
translations.idiomatic: Adjust north-south until east-west gnomons align—the site sits on true mao-you."

sentences.zh: ○晷影

translations.literal: Gnomon Shadows
translations.idiomatic: Gnomon Shadows

sentences.zh: 昔者周公測晷影于陽城，以參考曆紀。

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou measured gnomon shadow at Yangcheng to consult and verify calendar reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou measured gnomon shadows at Yangcheng to verify the calendar.

sentences.zh: 其于《周禮》，在《大司徒之職》：「以土圭之法，測土深，正日景，以求地中。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, in the Grand Steward's Duties: "By the earth-tablet method, measure earth's depth, rectify the sun's shadow, to seek Earth's center.
translations.idiomatic: Rites of Zhou, Grand Steward: "By the earth-tablet method rectify the sun's shadow to find Earth's center.

sentences.zh: 日至之景，尺有五寸，則天地之所合，四時之所交。

translations.literal: At solstice the shadow is one chi five cun—then Heaven and Earth meet, the four seasons cross.
translations.idiomatic: Solstice shadow one chi five cun—Heaven and Earth meet and seasons cross.

sentences.zh: 百物阜安，乃建王國。

translations.literal: The hundred things flourish in peace—and the royal state is established."
translations.idiomatic: All things flourish and the royal state is founded."

sentences.zh: 」然則日為陽精，玄象之著然者也。

translations.literal: Thus the sun is yang essence—the dark image's manifest brightness.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is yang essence—the manifest brightness of the dark image.

sentences.zh: 生靈因之動息，寒暑由其遞代。

translations.literal: Living creatures thereby move and rest; cold and heat alternate by it.
translations.idiomatic: Living creatures move and rest by it; cold and heat alternate.

sentences.zh: 觀陰陽之升降，揆天地之高遠，正位辨方，定時考閏，莫近於茲也。

translations.literal: Observing yin and yang's ascent and descent, measuring Heaven and Earth's height and distance, rectifying position and distinguishing direction, fixing time and examining intercalation—nothing is nearer than this.
translations.idiomatic: Observing yin-yang motion, measuring Heaven-Earth distance, fixing position and time—nothing serves better.

sentences.zh: 古法簡略，旨趣難究，術家考測，互有異同。

translations.literal: Ancient methods are brief and obscure, hard to investigate; technicians' measurements differ mutually.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient methods are brief and obscure; technicians disagree.

sentences.zh: 先儒皆云：「夏至立八尺表于陽城，其影與土圭等。

translations.literal: Earlier scholars all say: "At summer solstice erect an eight-chi gnomon at Yangcheng; its shadow equals the earth tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars say: "At summer solstice an eight-chi gnomon at Yangcheng matches the earth tablet."

sentences.zh: 」案《尚書考靈曜》稱：「日永，景尺五寸；

translations.literal: Examining Documents Kao Ling Yao: "Long day, shadow one chi five cun;
translations.idiomatic: Documents Kao Ling Yao: "Long day—shadow one chi five cun;

sentences.zh: 日短，景尺三寸。

translations.literal: short day, shadow one chi three cun."
translations.idiomatic: short day—shadow one chi three cun."

sentences.zh: 」《易通卦驗》曰：「冬至之日，樹八尺之表，日中視其晷景長短，以占和否。

translations.literal: Changes Tong Gua Yan says: "On the winter solstice day, plant an eight-chi gnomon; at midday view its gnomon shadow length to read harmony or disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Changes Tong Gua Yan: "On winter solstice plant an eight-chi gnomon; at midday read shadow length for harmony or disorder."

sentences.zh: 夏至景一尺四寸八分，冬至一丈三尺。

translations.literal: Summer solstice shadow one chi four cun eight fen; winter solstice one zhang three chi.
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice shadow one chi four cun eight fen; winter solstice one zhang three chi.

sentences.zh: 」《周髀》云：「成周土中，夏至景一尺六寸，冬至景一丈三尺五寸。

translations.literal: Zhou Bi says: "At Chengzhou Earth's center, summer solstice shadow one chi six cun, winter solstice one zhang three chi five cun."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bi: "At Chengzhou center, summer solstice one chi six cun, winter solstice one zhang three chi five cun."

sentences.zh: 」劉向《鴻範傳》曰：「夏至景長一尺五寸八分，冬至一丈三尺一寸四分，春秋二分，景七尺三寸六分。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's Hong Fan Commentary: "Summer solstice shadow one chi five cun eight fen, winter solstice one zhang three chi one cun four fen, spring and autumn equinox shadow seven chi three cun six fen."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang: "Summer solstice one chi five cun eight fen, winter solstice one zhang three chi one cun four fen, equinox seven chi three cun six fen."

sentences.zh: 」後漢《四分曆》、魏《景初曆》、宋《元嘉曆》、《大明》祖沖之曆，皆與《考靈曜》同。

translations.literal: Later Han Four Parts Calendar, Wei Jingchu Calendar, Song Yuanjia Calendar, and Liu Song Zu Chongzhi's Daming Calendar all match Kao Ling Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han Four Parts, Wei Jingchu, Song Yuanjia, and Zu Chongzhi's Daming calendars all match Kao Ling Yao.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏及宋，所都皆別，四家曆法，候影則齊。

translations.literal: Han, Wei, and Song capitals all differed—yet four calendars' shadow observation aligned.
translations.idiomatic: Han, Wei, and Song had different capitals yet shadow measures aligned.

sentences.zh: 且緯候所陳，恐難依據。

translations.literal: Moreover apocryphal observations presented—feared hard to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Apocryphal observations are hard to rely on.

sentences.zh: 劉向二分之影，直以率推，非因表候定其長短。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's equinox shadows were directly derived by rate—not fixed by gnomon observation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's equinox shadows were calculated, not measured.

sentences.zh: 然尋晷影尺丈，雖有大較，或地域不改，而分寸參差，或南北殊方，而長短維一。

translations.literal: Yet seeking gnomon shadow chi and zhang, though there is broad comparison—either the region unchanged yet fen and cun differ, or north and south different regions yet length uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Shadow measures vary by region even when texts give single values.

sentences.zh: 蓋術士未能精驗，馮占所以致乖。

translations.literal: Probably technicians could not verify precisely—relying on divination thus leads to discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Technicians failed to verify precisely; divination led to error.

sentences.zh: 今刪其繁雜，附於此云。

translations.literal: Now deleting the redundant, appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Redundant material is deleted here.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，祖暅造八尺銅表，其下與圭相連。

translations.literal: In Liang Tianjian, Zu Geng made an eight-chi bronze gnomon, its base joined to the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Tianjian, Zu Geng made an eight-chi bronze gnomon joined to its tablet.

sentences.zh: 圭上為溝，置水，以取平正。

translations.literal: On the tablet a channel with water to obtain level correctness.
translations.idiomatic: A water channel on the tablet ensured level.

sentences.zh: 揆測日晷，求其盈縮。

translations.literal: Measure the sun's gnomon, seeking surplus and deficit.
translations.idiomatic: He measured solar gnomon shadows for surplus and deficit.

sentences.zh: 至大同十年，太史令虞廣刂又用九尺表格江左之影。

translations.literal: By Datong 10, Grand Astrologer Yu Guangce also used a nine-chi gnomon to measure Jiangzuo shadows.
translations.idiomatic: By Datong 10, Grand Astrologer Yu Guangce used a nine-chi gnomon for Jiangzuo shadows.

sentences.zh: 夏至一尺三寸二分，冬至一丈三尺七分，立夏、立秋二尺四寸五分，春分、秋分五尺三寸九分。

translations.literal: Summer solstice one chi three cun two fen, winter solstice one zhang three chi seven fen, Lixia and Liqiu two chi four cun five fen, spring and autumn equinox five chi three cun nine fen.
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice one chi three cun two fen, winter solstice one zhang three chi seven fen, Lixia and Liqiu two chi four cun five fen, equinox five chi three cun nine fen.

sentences.zh: 陳氏一代，唯用梁法。

translations.literal: The Chen house for one generation used only Liang method.
translations.idiomatic: Chen used only Liang methods.

sentences.zh: 齊神武以洛陽舊器並徙鄴中，以暨文宣受終，竟未考驗。

translations.literal: Northern Qi Shenwu moved Luoyang's old instruments to Ye—yet when Wenxuan ended, never verified.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi Shenwu moved Luoyang instruments to Ye but never verified them under Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 至武平七年，訖幹景禮始薦劉孝孫、張孟賓等於後主。

translations.literal: By Wuping 7, Gan Jingli finally recommended Liu Xiaosun and Zhang Mengbin to the Later Lord.
translations.idiomatic: By Wuping 7, Gan Jingli recommended Liu Xiaosun and Zhang Mengbin.

sentences.zh: 劉、張建表測影，以考分至之氣。

translations.literal: Liu and Zhang erected gnomons measuring shadow to examine solstice qi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu and Zhang erected gnomons to test solstice qi.

sentences.zh: 草創未就，仍遇朝亡。

translations.literal: Draft not finished—they met the dynasty's fall.
translations.idiomatic: The project was unfinished when the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 周自天和以來，言曆者紛紛複出。

translations.literal: From Zhou Tianhe onward, calendar speakers proliferated again.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhou Tianhe onward calendar debates proliferated.

sentences.zh: 亦驗二至之影，以考曆之精粗。

translations.literal: Also verifying solstice shadows to examine calendar precision.
translations.idiomatic: Solstice shadows tested calendar precision.

sentences.zh: 及高祖踐極之後，大議造曆。

translations.literal: After Gaozu took the throne, great debate on making calendar.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's accession, debate on calendar reform ensued.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄兼明揆測，言日長之瑞。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan understood measurement, speaking of the auspicious omen of lengthening days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan cited lengthening days as an auspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 有詔司存，而莫能考決。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices—yet none could examine and decide.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were ordered to decide—none could.

sentences.zh: 至開皇十九年，袁充為太史令，欲成胄玄舊事，複表曰：「隋興已後，日景漸長。

translations.literal: By Kaihuang 19, Yuan Chong as Grand Astrologer wished to complete Zhouxuan's old matter, again memorializing: "Since Sui's rise, sun shadows gradually lengthen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 19, Yuan Chong memorialized: "Since Sui's rise, sun shadows gradually lengthened.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年冬至之影，長一丈二尺七寸二分，自爾漸短。

translations.literal: Kaihuang 1 winter solstice shadow one zhang two chi seven cun two fen—from then gradually shorter.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 1 winter solstice shadow one zhang two chi seven cun two fen—then gradually shorter.

sentences.zh: 至十七年冬至影，一丈二尺六寸三分。

translations.literal: By year 17 winter solstice shadow one zhang two chi six cun three fen.
translations.idiomatic: Year 17 winter solstice one zhang two chi six cun three fen.

sentences.zh: 四年冬至，在洛陽測影，長一丈二尺八寸八分。

translations.literal: Year 4 winter solstice, measured at Luoyang, shadow one zhang two chi eight cun eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: Year 4 winter solstice at Luoyang: one zhang two chi eight cun eight fen.

sentences.zh: 二年夏至影，一尺四寸八分，自爾漸短。

translations.literal: Year 2 summer solstice shadow one chi four cun eight fen—from then gradually shorter.
translations.idiomatic: Year 2 summer solstice one chi four cun eight fen—then shorter.

sentences.zh: 至十六年夏至影，一尺四寸五分。

translations.literal: By year 16 summer solstice shadow one chi four cun five fen.
translations.idiomatic: Year 16 summer solstice one chi four cun five fen.

sentences.zh: 其十八年冬至，陰雲不測。

translations.literal: Year 18 winter solstice—clouds prevented measurement.
translations.idiomatic: Year 18 winter solstice—clouds blocked measurement.

sentences.zh: 元年、十七年、十八年夏至，亦陰雲不測。

translations.literal: Years 1, 17, and 18 summer solstice—also clouds prevented measurement.
translations.idiomatic: Years 1, 17, and 18 summer solstice—also unmeasured due to clouds.

sentences.zh: 《周官》以土圭之法正日影，日至之影，尺有五寸。

translations.literal: Zhou Offices use earth-tablet method to rectify sun shadow; solstice shadow one chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Offices rectify sun shadow; solstice shadow one chi five cun.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：'冬至之景，一丈三尺。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "Winter solstice shadow one zhang three chi."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan: "Winter solstice shadow one zhang three chi."

sentences.zh: '今十六年夏至之影，短於舊五分，十七年冬至之影，短於舊三寸七分。

translations.literal: Now year 16 summer solstice shadow five fen shorter than old; year 17 winter solstice three cun seven fen shorter than old.
translations.idiomatic: Year 16 summer solstice five fen shorter; year 17 winter solstice three cun seven fen shorter.

sentences.zh: 日去極近，則影短而日長；

translations.literal: Sun far from pole—shadow short and day long;
translations.idiomatic: Far from pole—short shadow, long day;

sentences.zh: 去極遠，則影長而日短。

translations.literal: far from pole—shadow long and day short.
translations.idiomatic: near pole—long shadow, short day.

sentences.zh: 行內道則去極近，行外道則去極遠。

translations.literal: Traveling inner path then far from pole near; traveling outer path then far from pole distant.
translations.idiomatic: Inner path—near pole; outer path—far from pole.

sentences.zh: 《堯典》云：'日短星昴，以正仲冬。

translations.literal: Documents of Yao: "Short day, star Pleiades centered—to rectify mid-winter."
translations.idiomatic: Documents of Yao: "Short day, Pleiades centered—mid-winter."

sentences.zh: '據昴星昏中，則知堯時仲冬，日在須女十度。

translations.literal: According to Pleiades centered at dusk, then know at Yao's mid-winter the sun was at Maiden 10 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Pleiades at dusk implies Yao's mid-winter sun at Maiden 10°.

sentences.zh: 以歷數推之，開皇以來冬至，日在斗十一度，與唐堯之代，去極俱近。

translations.literal: By calendar reckoning, since Kaihuang winter solstice sun at Dipper 11 degrees—with Tang Yao's age, distance from pole both near.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kaihuang winter solstice sun at Dipper 11°—like Yao's era, both near the pole.

sentences.zh: 謹案《元命包》云：'日月出內道，〔璣得其常，天帝崇靈，聖王初功。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining Yuan Ming Bao: "Sun and moon exit inner path, ji obtains its norm, Heavenly Emperor exalts numinous spirit, sage king's first achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ming Bao: "Sun and moon on inner path, ji holds norm, Heaven exalts the sage's first achievement."
