sentences.zh: '京房《別對》曰：'太平日行上道，升平日行次道，霸代日行下道。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Separate Responses: "Great peace sun travels upper path, ascending peace middle path, hegemonic age lower path."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang: "Great peace—upper path; ascending peace—middle; hegemonic age—lower."

sentences.zh: '伏惟大隋啓運，上感乾元，影短日長，振古稀有。

translations.literal: Considering Great Sui's opening fortune, above moved by Qian yuan, shadow short day long—rare since antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Great Sui opened fortune under Qian yuan—short shadow, long day, rare since antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」是時廢庶人勇，晉王廣初為太子，充奏此事，深合時宜。

translations.literal: At this time Deposed Heir Yong, Prince of Jin Guang newly made crown prince—Chong's memorial deeply fit the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Yong, new crown prince Guang—Chong's memorial suited the moment.

sentences.zh: 上臨朝謂百官曰：「景長之慶，天之祐也。

translations.literal: The emperor at court told officials: "Shadow lengthening's celebration is Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told officials: "Lengthening shadows are Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 今太子新立，當須改元，宜取日長之意，以為年號。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince newly established—must change era name; should take long day's meaning as reign title."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is new—we should take long days as the era name."

sentences.zh: 」由是改開皇二十一年為仁壽元年。

translations.literal: Thus Kaihuang 21 became Renshou 1.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 21 became Renshou 1.

sentences.zh: 此後百工作役，並加程課，以日長故也。

translations.literal: After this all public works and corvée added schedule intensity—because days were long.
translations.idiomatic: Public works intensified—because days were supposedly longer.

sentences.zh: 皇太子率百官詣闕陳賀。

translations.literal: The crown prince led officials to the palace to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince led officials in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 案日徐疾盈縮無常，充等以為祥瑞，大為議者所貶。

translations.literal: Examining sun's slow, fast, surplus, and deficit as irregular—Chong and others took it as auspicious omen, greatly criticized by debaters.
translations.idiomatic: Sun motion is irregular—critics condemned Chong's omen reading.

sentences.zh: 又《考靈曜》、《周髀》張衡《靈憲》及鄭玄注《周官》，並云：「日影於地，千里而差一寸。

translations.literal: Also Kao Ling Yao, Zhou Bi, Zhang Heng's Ling Xian, and Zheng Xuan's Zhou Offices commentary all say: "Sun shadow on Earth differs one cun per thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: Kao Ling Yao, Zhou Bi, Ling Xian, and Zheng Xuan all say shadow differs one cun per thousand li.

sentences.zh: 」案宋元嘉十九年壬午，使使往交州測影。

translations.literal: Examining Liu Song Yuanjia 19 renwu, envoys sent to Jiao Province to measure shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 19 renwu envoys measured shadows at Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 夏至之日，影出表南三寸二分。

translations.literal: On summer solstice day, shadow extended three cun two fen south of the gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice shadow extended three cun two fen south of the gnomon.

sentences.zh: 何承天遙取陽城，云夏至一尺五寸。

translations.literal: He Chengtian remotely took Yangcheng, saying summer solstice one chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian used Yangcheng's summer solstice one chi five cun remotely.

sentences.zh: 計陽城去交州，路當萬里，而影實差一尺八寸二分。

translations.literal: Calculating Yangcheng to Jiao Province, the road should be ten thousand li, yet shadow actually differed one chi eight cun two fen.
translations.idiomatic: Yangcheng to Jiao Province should be ten thousand li by road, yet shadows differed by one chi eight cun two fen.

sentences.zh: 是六百里而差一寸也。

translations.literal: Thus six hundred li per cun difference.
translations.idiomatic: That is one cun difference per six hundred li.

sentences.zh: 又當梁大同中，二至所測，以八尺表率取之，夏至當一尺一寸七分強。

translations.literal: Also in Liang Datong, solstice measurements with eight-chi gnomon standard gave summer solstice about one chi one cun seven fen strong.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Datong solstice measures with an eight-chi gnomon gave summer solstice about one chi one cun seven fen strong.

sentences.zh: 後魏信都芳注《周髀四術》，稱永平元年戊子，當梁天監之七年，見洛陽測影，又見公孫崇集諸朝士，共觀秘書影。

translations.literal: Northern Wei Xin Du Fang's commentary on Zhou Bi Four Methods says Yongping 1 wuzi, corresponding to Liang Tianjian 7, saw Luoyang shadow measurement; also saw Gongsun Chong gather court gentlemen viewing Secretariat shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Du Fang noted that in Yongping 1 (Liang Tianjian 7) Luoyang shadows were measured and Gongsun Chong gathered officials to view Secretariat shadows.

sentences.zh: 同是夏至日，其中影皆長一尺五寸八分。

translations.literal: Same summer solstice day—all midday shadows one chi five cun eight fen long.
translations.idiomatic: On the same summer solstice all midday shadows measured one chi five cun eight fen.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，金陵去洛，南北略當千里，而影差四寸。

translations.literal: From this inferring, Jinling to Luoyang north-south roughly one thousand li, yet shadow differed four cun.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling to Luoyang is roughly one thousand li north-south, yet shadows differed four cun.

sentences.zh: 則二百五十裡而影差一寸也。

translations.literal: Then two hundred fifty li per cun difference.
translations.idiomatic: That yields one cun per two hundred fifty li.

sentences.zh: 況人路迂回，山川登降，方於鳥道，所校彌多，則千里之言，未足依也。

translations.literal: Moreover human roads wind, mountains rise and fall—compared with bird flight, correction is greater; thus the thousand-li saying cannot be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: Human roads wind and terrain varies—unlike bird flight—so the thousand-li rule cannot be relied on.

sentences.zh: 其揆測參差如此，故備論之。

translations.literal: Measurement discrepancies are thus—therefore fully discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Measurements diverge thus—hence this full discussion.

sentences.zh: ○漏刻

translations.literal: Clepsydra Marks
translations.idiomatic: Clepsydra Marks

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝創觀漏水，制器取則，以分晝夜。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor first observed dripping water, made instruments taking norms, to divide day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor first observed dripping water and made instruments to divide day and night.

sentences.zh: 其後因以命官，《周禮》挈壺氏則其職也。

translations.literal: Afterward offices were named accordingly—Rites of Zhou's Pitcher Bearer is that duty.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were named accordingly—the Rites of Zhou Pitcher Bearer held this duty.

sentences.zh: 其法，總以百刻，分於晝夜。

translations.literal: Its method totals one hundred marks divided between day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The method totals one hundred marks between day and night.

sentences.zh: 冬至晝漏四十刻，夜漏六十刻。

translations.literal: Winter solstice day clepsydra forty marks, night sixty marks.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice: forty day marks, sixty night marks.

sentences.zh: 夏至晝漏六十刻，夜漏四十刻。

translations.literal: Summer solstice day clepsydra sixty marks, night forty marks.
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice: sixty day marks, forty night marks.

sentences.zh: 春秋二分，晝夜各五十刻。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn equinox—day and night each fifty marks.
translations.idiomatic: Equinoxes: fifty marks each for day and night.

sentences.zh: 日未出前二刻半而明，既沒後二刻半乃昏。

translations.literal: Two and a half marks before sun not yet risen it is light; two and a half marks after setting then dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Light begins two and a half marks before sunrise; dusk two and a half marks after sunset.

sentences.zh: 減夜五刻，以益晝漏，謂之昏旦。

translations.literal: Subtract five night marks to add to day clepsydra—called dusk and dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Five night marks transfer to day clepsydra—dusk and dawn allowance.

sentences.zh: 漏刻皆隨氣增損。

translations.literal: Clepsydra marks all increase and decrease with qi.
translations.idiomatic: Clepsydra marks adjust with seasonal qi.

sentences.zh: 冬夏二至之間，晝夜長短，凡差二十刻。

translations.literal: Between winter and summer solstices, day-night length differs twenty marks total.
translations.idiomatic: Between solstices day and night length differs twenty marks.

sentences.zh: 每差一刻為一箭。

translations.literal: Each one-mark difference is one arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Each one-mark change equals one arrow.

sentences.zh: 冬至互起其首，凡有四十一箭。

translations.literal: Winter solstice alternately starting the head—in all forty-one arrows.
translations.idiomatic: From winter solstice forty-one arrows alternate.

sentences.zh: 晝有朝，有禺，有中，有晡，有夕。

translations.literal: Day has court, yu, center, bu, evening.
translations.idiomatic: Day periods: court, yu, center, bu, evening.

sentences.zh: 夜有甲、乙、丙、丁、戊。

translations.literal: Night has jia, yi, bing, ding, wu.
translations.idiomatic: Night watches: jia, yi, bing, ding, wu.

sentences.zh: 昏旦有星中。

translations.literal: Dusk and dawn have centered stars.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk and dawn have centered stars.

sentences.zh: 每箭各有其數，皆所以分時代守，更其作役。

translations.literal: Each arrow has its number—all to divide eras, guard time, and change labor.
translations.idiomatic: Each arrow has its count to divide eras, guard time, and schedule labor.

sentences.zh: 漢興，張蒼因循古制，猶多疏闊。

translations.literal: Han risen, Zhang Cang followed ancient system—still much loose and wide.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Zhang Cang followed ancient practice but left much loose.

sentences.zh: 及孝武考定星曆，下漏以追天度，亦未能盡其理。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu examined stars and calendar, lowered clepsydra to chase heavenly degrees—also could not exhaust principle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu lowered clepsydra to match heavenly degrees—yet principle was not fully grasped.

sentences.zh: 劉向《鴻範傳》記武帝時所用法云：「冬夏二至之間，一百八十餘日，晝夜差二十刻。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's Hong Fan Commentary records Wu's method: "Between winter and summer solstices, one hundred eighty-odd days, day-night differs twenty marks."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang records Wu's method: between solstices one hundred eighty-odd days differ twenty marks in day-night length.

sentences.zh: 」大率二至之後，九日而增損一刻焉。

translations.literal: " Generally after solstices, every nine days increase or decrease one mark.
translations.idiomatic: Generally one mark changes every nine days after a solstice.

sentences.zh: 至哀帝時，又改用晝夜一百二十刻，尋亦寢廢。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ai's time, again changed to day-night one hundred twenty marks—soon also abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai tried one hundred twenty marks—soon abandoned.

sentences.zh: 至王莽竊位，又遵行之。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang usurped, again followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang followed it again.

sentences.zh: 光武之初，亦以百刻九日加減法，編於《甲令》，為《常符漏品》。

translations.literal: Early Guangwu also used hundred-mark nine-day adjustment, compiled in Edict A as Constant Talisman Clepsydra Categories.
translations.idiomatic: Early Guangwu used hundred marks with nine-day adjustment in Edict A.

sentences.zh: 至和帝永元十四年，霍融上言：「官曆率九日增減一刻，不與天相應。

translations.literal: By Emperor He Yongyuan 14, Huo Rong submitted: "Official calendar uniformly nine days per mark change—not corresponding with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Huo Rong in Yongyuan 14: official calendar's nine-day mark change does not match Heaven.

sentences.zh: 或時差至二刻半，不如夏曆漏刻，隨日南北為長短。

translations.literal: Sometimes difference reaches two and a half marks—inferior to Xia calendar clepsydra following sun north-south for length.
translations.idiomatic: Error reached two and a half marks—inferior to Xia calendar clepsydra following solar latitude.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔用夏曆漏刻。

translations.literal: " Then edict used Xia calendar clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted Xia calendar clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 依日行黃道去極，每差二度四分，為增減一刻。

translations.literal: Following sun's Yellow Path distance from pole, every two degrees four fen difference is one mark increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Each two degrees four fen of solar polar distance changes clepsydra one mark.

sentences.zh: 凡用四十八箭，終於魏、晉，相傳不改。

translations.literal: In all forty-eight arrows used—through Wei and Jin transmitted unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-eight arrows were used through Wei and Jin unchanged.

sentences.zh: 宋何承天以月蝕所在，當日之衡，考驗日宿，知移舊六度。

translations.literal: Song He Chengtian from lunar eclipse location at day's balance, verifying sun's lodge, knew old shift of six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian found the sun's lodge shifted six degrees from eclipse data.

sentences.zh: 冬至之日，其影極長，測量晷度，知冬至移舊四日。

translations.literal: Winter solstice day its shadow extremely long—measuring gnomon degrees, knew winter solstice shifted old four days.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice shadow measurement showed a four-day shift.

sentences.zh: 前代諸漏，春分晝長，秋分晝短，差過半刻。

translations.literal: Prior generations' clepsydra—spring equinox day long, autumn equinox day short, difference over half a mark.
translations.idiomatic: Older clepsydra made spring days too long and autumn days too short by over half a mark.

sentences.zh: 皆由氣日不正，所以而然。

translations.literal: All because qi days not correct—whence this.
translations.idiomatic: All because seasonal days were incorrect.

sentences.zh: 遂議造漏法。

translations.literal: Then proposed making clepsydra method.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed a new clepsydra method.

sentences.zh: 春秋二分，昏旦晝夜漏各五十五刻。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn equinox dusk-dawn day-night clepsydra each fifty-five marks.
translations.idiomatic: Equinox dusk-dawn clepsydra: fifty-five marks each for day and night.

sentences.zh: 齊及梁初，因循不改。

translations.literal: Qi and early Liang followed unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and early Liang followed unchanged.

sentences.zh: 至天監六年，武帝以晝夜百刻，分配十二辰，辰得八刻，仍有餘分。

translations.literal: By Tianjian 6, Emperor Wu because day-night hundred marks divided among twelve chronograms, each chronogram eight marks with remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian 6: hundred marks divided among twelve chronograms left remainders.

sentences.zh: 乃以晝夜為九十六刻，一辰有全刻八焉。

translations.literal: Then made day-night ninety-six marks—one chronogram exactly eight full marks.
translations.idiomatic: Day-night became ninety-six marks—eight full marks per chronogram.

sentences.zh: 至大同十年，又改用一百八刻。

translations.literal: By Datong 10, again changed to one hundred eight marks.
translations.idiomatic: Datong 10 changed to one hundred eight marks.

sentences.zh: 依《尚書考靈曜》晝夜三十六頃之數，因而三之。

translations.literal: Following Documents Kao Ling Yao day-night thirty-six qing count, then trebled.
translations.idiomatic: Following Kao Ling Yao's thirty-six qing count, trebled.

sentences.zh: 冬至晝漏四十八刻，夜漏六十刻。

translations.literal: Winter solstice day clepsydra forty-eight marks, night sixty marks.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice: forty-eight day, sixty night marks.

sentences.zh: 夏至晝漏七十刻，夜漏三十八刻。

translations.literal: Summer solstice day clepsydra seventy marks, night thirty-eight marks.
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice: seventy day, thirty-eight night marks.

sentences.zh: 春秋二分，晝漏六十刻，夜漏四十八刻。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn equinox day clepsydra sixty marks, night forty-eight marks.
translations.idiomatic: Equinox: sixty day, forty-eight night marks.

sentences.zh: 昏旦之數各三刻。

translations.literal: Dusk and dawn each three marks.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk and dawn: three marks each.

sentences.zh: 先令祖暅為《漏經》，皆依渾天黃道日行去極遠近，為用箭日率。

translations.literal: First ordered Zu Geng's Clepsydra Classic—all following spherical Heaven Yellow Path sun daily polar distance for arrow-day rates.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Geng's Clepsydra Classic used solar polar distance for arrow rates.

sentences.zh: 陳文帝天嘉中，亦命舍人硃史造漏，依古百刻為法。

translations.literal: Chen Emperor Wen Tianjia ordered Gentleman Zhu Shi to make clepsydra, following ancient hundred-mark method.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wendi ordered Zhu Shi to make clepsydra by the ancient hundred-mark method.

sentences.zh: 周、齊因循魏漏。

translations.literal: Zhou and Qi followed Wei clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Qi followed Wei clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋、梁大同，並以百刻分於晝夜。

translations.literal: Jin, Song, Liang Datong all divided hundred marks between day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, Song, and Liang Datong used hundred marks between day and night.

sentences.zh: 隋初，用周朝尹公正、馬顯所造《漏經》。

translations.literal: Early Sui used Zhou Yin Gongzheng and Ma Xian's Clepsydra Classic.
translations.idiomatic: Early Sui used Yin Gongzheng and Ma Xian's Clepsydra Classic.

sentences.zh: 至開皇十四年，鄜州司馬袁充上晷影漏刻。

translations.literal: By Kaihuang 14, Fuzhou Marshal Yuan Chong submitted gnomon shadow clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 14: Yuan Chong submitted gnomon and clepsydra reforms.

sentences.zh: 充以短影平儀，均布十二辰，立表，隨日影所指辰刻，以驗漏水之節。

translations.literal: Chong used short-shadow level instrument, evenly distributing twelve chronograms, erecting gnomon—following day shadow's indicated chronogram mark to verify clepsydra nodes.
translations.idiomatic: Chong used a level instrument and gnomon shadows to verify clepsydra nodes by chronogram.

sentences.zh: 十二辰刻，互有多少，時正前後，刻亦不同。

translations.literal: Twelve chronogram marks mutually more or less; time before and after center, marks also differ.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve chronogram marks varied; marks differed before and after true center.

sentences.zh: 其二至二分用箭辰刻之法，今列之云。

translations.literal: The solstice and equinox arrow-chronogram mark method—now listed:
translations.idiomatic: Solstice and equinox arrow-chronogram methods are listed below:

sentences.zh: 冬至：日出辰正，入申正，晝四十刻，夜六十刻。

translations.literal: Winter solstice: sun rises chen centered, sets shen centered; day forty marks, night sixty marks.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice: sunrise at chen center, sunset at shen center; forty day, sixty night marks.

sentences.zh: 子、醜、亥各二刻，寅、戌各六刻，卯、酉各十三刻，辰、申各十四刻，巳、未各十刻，午八刻。

translations.literal: Zi, chou, hai each two marks; yin, xu each six; mao, you each thirteen; chen, shen each fourteen; si, wei each ten; wu eight marks.
translations.idiomatic: Zi, chou, hai two marks each; yin, xu six; mao, you thirteen; chen, shen fourteen; si, wei ten; wu eight.

sentences.zh: 右十四日改箭。

translations.literal: Right—fourteen days change arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Arrow changes every fourteen days.

sentences.zh: 春秋二分：日出卯正，入酉正，晝五十刻，夜五十刻。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn equinox: sun rises mao centered, sets you centered; day fifty marks, night fifty marks.
translations.idiomatic: Equinox: sunrise mao center, sunset you center; fifty day, fifty night marks.

sentences.zh: 子四刻，醜、亥七刻，寅、戌九刻，卯、酉十四刻，辰、申九刻，巳、未七刻，午四刻。

translations.literal: Zi four marks; chou, hai seven; yin, xu nine; mao, you fourteen; chen, shen nine; si, wei seven; wu four marks.
translations.idiomatic: Zi four; chou, hai seven; yin, xu nine; mao, you fourteen; chen, shen nine; si, wei seven; wu four.

sentences.zh: 右五日改箭。

translations.literal: Right—five days change arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Arrow changes every five days.

sentences.zh: 夏至：日出寅正，入戌正，晝六十刻，夜四十刻。

translations.literal: Summer solstice: sun rises yin centered, sets xu centered; day sixty marks, night forty marks.
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice: sunrise yin center, sunset xu center; sixty day, forty night marks.

sentences.zh: 子八刻，醜、亥十刻，寅、戌十四刻，卯、酉十三刻，辰、申六刻，巳、未二刻，午二刻。

translations.literal: Zi eight marks; chou, hai ten; yin, xu fourteen; mao, you thirteen; chen, shen six; si, wei two; wu two marks.
translations.idiomatic: Zi eight; chou, hai ten; yin, xu fourteen; mao, you thirteen; chen, shen six; si, wei two; wu two.

sentences.zh: 右一十九日，加減一刻，改箭。

translations.literal: Right—nineteen days, add or subtract one mark, change arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Every nineteen days adjust one mark and change arrow.

sentences.zh: 袁充素不曉渾天黃道去極之數，苟役私智，變改舊章，其於施用，未為精密。

translations.literal: Yuan Chong never understood spherical Heaven Yellow Path polar distance numbers—forcing private wit, altering old statutes—in application not precise.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chong did not understand polar distance; his private alterations were imprecise.

sentences.zh: 開皇十七年，張胄玄用後魏渾天鐵儀，測知春秋二分，日出卯酉之北，不正當中。

translations.literal: Kaihuang 17, Zhang Zhouxuan used Northern Wei iron armillary sphere, measured knowing spring and autumn equinox sun rises north of mao-you—not directly centered.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 17: Zhang Zhouxuan found equinox sunrise north of mao-you, not centered.

sentences.zh: 與何承天所測頗同，皆日出卯三刻五十五分，入酉四刻二十五分。

translations.literal: Matching He Chengtian's measurement—both sun rise mao three marks fifty-five fen, set you four marks twenty-five fen.
translations.idiomatic: Matching He Chengtian: sunrise mao 3 marks 55 fen, sunset you 4 marks 25 fen.

sentences.zh: 晝漏五十刻十一分，夜漏四十九刻四十分，晝夜差六十分刻之四十。

translations.literal: Day clepsydra fifty marks eleven fen, night forty-nine marks forty fen—day-night difference sixty forty-hundredths marks.
translations.idiomatic: Day fifty marks eleven fen, night forty-nine forty—difference sixty forty-hundredths marks.

sentences.zh: 仁壽四年，劉焯上《皇極曆》，有日行遲疾，推二十四氣，皆有盈縮定日。

translations.literal: Renshou 4, Liu Zhuo submitted Huangji Calendar with sun's slow and fast motion, deriving twenty-four qi—all with surplus and deficit fixed days.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou 4: Liu Zhuo's Huangji Calendar derived twenty-four qi with surplus and deficit days.

sentences.zh: 春秋分定日，去冬至各八十八日有奇，去夏至各九十三日有奇。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn equinox fixed days—eighty-eight days odd from winter solstice, ninety-three days odd from summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Equinox fixed days: eighty-eight odd from winter solstice, ninety-three odd from summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 二分定日，晝夜各五十刻。

translations.literal: Equinox fixed days—day and night each fifty marks.
translations.idiomatic: Equinox fixed days: fifty marks day and night.

sentences.zh: 又依渾天黃道，驗知冬至夜漏五十九刻、一百分刻之八十六，晝漏四十刻一十四分，夏至晝漏五十九刻八十六分，夜漏四十刻一十四分。

translations.literal: Also verifying by spherical Heaven Yellow Path—knowing winter solstice night clepsydra fifty-nine marks eighty-six hundredths, day forty marks fourteen fen; summer solstice day fifty-nine eighty-six, night forty fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: By Yellow Path: winter solstice night fifty-nine marks 86 hundredths, day forty fourteen; summer reversed.

sentences.zh: 冬夏二至之間，晝夜差一十九刻、一百分刻之七十二。

translations.literal: Between winter and summer solstices, day-night difference nineteen marks seventy-two hundredths.
translations.idiomatic: Between solstices day-night differs nineteen marks seventy-two hundredths.

sentences.zh: 胄玄及焯漏刻，並不施用。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan and Zhuo clepsydra—neither applied.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Zhouxuan nor Zhuo's clepsydra was adopted.

sentences.zh: 然其法制，皆著在曆術，推驗加時，最為詳審。

translations.literal: Yet their methods and systems are recorded in calendar arts—verifying and adding time, most detailed and examined.
translations.idiomatic: Their methods remain in calendar texts—the most detailed for time verification.

sentences.zh: 大業初，耿詢作古欹器，以漏水注之，獻於煬帝。

translations.literal: Daye start, Geng Xun made ancient tilt vessel, water-filled, presented to Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At Daye's start Geng Xun made an ancient tilt vessel for Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，因令與宇文愷依後魏道士李蘭所修道家上法稱漏制，造稱水漏器，以充行從。

translations.literal: Emperor approved—ordered with Yuwen Kai following Northern Wei Daoist Li Lan's Daoist upper-method scale clepsydra, making scale water clepsydra for travel retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered Yuwen Kai to make traveling scale clepsydra after Li Lan's method.

sentences.zh: 又作候影分箭上水方器，置於東都乾陽殿前鼓下司辰。

translations.literal: Also made shadow-dividing arrow upper-water square vessel, placed at Eastern Capital Qianyang Hall before drums for timekeeping.
translations.idiomatic: Also a shadow-dividing water vessel at Qianyang Hall for timekeeping.

sentences.zh: 又作馬上漏刻，以從行辨時刻。

translations.literal: Also made horse-mounted clepsydra for travel time distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Also a horse-mounted clepsydra for travel.

sentences.zh: 揆日晷，下漏刻，此二者，測天地正儀象之本也。

translations.literal: Measuring sun gnomon, lowering clepsydra marks—these two are measuring Heaven and Earth's correct instruments and models' root.
translations.idiomatic: Gnomon and clepsydra are the roots of correct celestial measurement.

sentences.zh: 晷漏沿革，今古大殊，故列其差，以補前闕。

translations.literal: Gnomon clepsydra evolution ancient and modern greatly differs—thus listing differences to supplement prior gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Gnomon and clepsydra evolved greatly—differences are listed to fill prior gaps.

sentences.zh: ○經星中宮

translations.literal: Fixed Stars: Inner Palace
translations.idiomatic: Fixed Stars: Inner Palace

sentences.zh: 北極五星，鉤陳六星，皆在紫宮中。

translations.literal: The five stars of the North Pole and the six stars of Goutchen are all within the Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The five North Pole stars and six Goutchen stars all lie within the Purple Palace.

sentences.zh: 北極，辰也。

translations.literal: The North Pole is the celestial pivot (chen).
translations.idiomatic: The North Pole is the celestial pivot.

sentences.zh: 其紐星，天之樞也。

translations.literal: Its pivot star is the pivot of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Its pivot star is Heaven's pivot.

sentences.zh: 天運無窮，三光迭耀，而極星不移。

translations.literal: Heaven's motion is endless; sun, moon, and stars shine in succession, yet the pole star does not move.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven turns without end as the three luminaries pass in turn, yet the pole star holds its place.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「居其所而眾星共之。

translations.literal: Hence it is said: "Remaining in its place, all stars revolve around it."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "It dwells in its place while all stars attend it."

sentences.zh: 」賈逵、張衡、蔡邕、王蕃、陸績，皆以北極紐星為樞，是不動處也。

translations.literal: " Jia Kui, Zhang Heng, Cai Yong, Wang Fan, and Lu Ji all took the North Pole pivot star as the pivot—the unmoving point.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui, Zhang Heng, Cai Yong, Wang Fan, and Lu Ji all held the North Pole pivot star to be the fixed pivot.

sentences.zh: 祖暅以儀准候不動處，在紐星之末，猶一度有餘。

translations.literal: Zu Geng, using instruments to observe the unmoving point, found it at the end of the pivot star, still more than one degree off.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Geng measured the unmoving point with instruments and placed it beyond the pivot star by more than one degree.

sentences.zh: 北極大星，太一之座也。

translations.literal: The great star of the North Pole is the seat of the Supreme One.
translations.idiomatic: The North Pole's great star is the throne of the Supreme One.

sentences.zh: 第一星主月，太子也。

translations.literal: The first star governs the moon and represents the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The first star governs the moon; it is the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 第二星主日，帝王也。

translations.literal: The second star governs the sun and represents the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The second star governs the sun; it is the emperor.

sentences.zh: 第三星主五星，庶子也。

translations.literal: The third star governs the five planets and represents the secondary son.
translations.idiomatic: The third star governs the five planets; it is the secondary son.

sentences.zh: 所謂第二星者，最赤明者也。

translations.literal: What is called the second star is the brightest and reddest.
translations.idiomatic: The so-called second star is the brightest red star.

sentences.zh: 北極五星，最為尊也。

translations.literal: Among the five North Pole stars, it is the most honored.
translations.idiomatic: The five North Pole stars are the most exalted.

sentences.zh: 中星不明，主不用事。

translations.literal: If the central star is dim, the ruler does not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the central star is unclear, the sovereign neglects governance.

sentences.zh: 右星不明，太子憂。

translations.literal: If the right star is dim, the Heir Apparent is troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When the right star fades, the Heir Apparent faces worry.

sentences.zh: 鉤陳，後宮也，太帝之正妃也，太帝之坐也。

translations.literal: Goutchen is the inner palace, the Great Emperor's principal consort, and the Great Emperor's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Goutchen represents the inner palace—the Great Emperor's chief consort and throne.

sentences.zh: 北四星曰女御宮，八十一御妻之象也。

translations.literal: The four northern stars are called the Palace of Female Attendants, imaging eighty-one imperial consorts.
translations.idiomatic: The four northern stars form the Palace of Female Attendants, symbolizing eighty-one consorts.

sentences.zh: 鉤陳口中一星，曰天皇太帝。

translations.literal: One star within Goutchen's mouth is called the Celestial August Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: A star in Goutchen's mouth is the Celestial August Emperor.

sentences.zh: 其神曰耀魄寶，主御群靈，秉萬神圖。

translations.literal: Its deity is called Yaopobao; it governs all spirits and holds the chart of myriad deities.
translations.idiomatic: Its god Yaopobao governs the host of spirits and bears the map of ten thousand gods.

sentences.zh: 抱極樞四星曰四輔，所以輔佐北極，而出度授政也。

translations.literal: Four stars embracing the pole pivot are called the Four Assistants, aiding the North Pole in issuing degrees and bestowing governance.
translations.idiomatic: Four stars encircling the pole pivot are the Four Assistants, helping the North Pole measure degrees and grant rule.

sentences.zh: 太帝上九星曰華蓋，蓋所以覆蔽太帝之坐也。

translations.literal: Nine stars above the Great Emperor are called the Canopy, covering and sheltering the Great Emperor's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Nine stars above the Great Emperor form the Canopy, shielding his throne.

sentences.zh: 又九星直曰杠。

translations.literal: Nine stars extending straight are called the Pole (gang).
translations.idiomatic: Nine stars in a line are the Pole—the canopy's handle.

sentences.zh: 蓋下五星曰五帝內坐，設敘順，帝所居也。

translations.literal: Five stars beneath the Canopy are called the Inner Seats of the Five Emperors, ordering where emperors dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Five stars under the Canopy are the Inner Seats of the Five Emperors, marking the imperial residence in proper order.

sentences.zh: 客犯紫宮中坐，大臣犯主。

translations.literal: If a guest star invades the central seat of the Purple Palace, ministers challenge the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star striking the Purple Palace's central seat means ministers rebel against the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 華蓋杠旁六星曰六甲，可以分陰陽而紀節候，故在帝旁，所以布政教而授人時也。

translations.literal: Six stars beside Canopy and Pole are called the Six Jia, dividing yin and yang and marking seasons; beside the emperor they spread governance and grant the people their seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Six stars by the Canopy Pole are the Six Jia, marking yin-yang and seasonal nodes to teach governance and set the calendar.

sentences.zh: 極東一星曰柱下史，主記過。

translations.literal: One star east of the pole is called the Historian beneath the Column; it records faults.
translations.idiomatic: East of the pole is the Historian beneath the Column, recording transgressions.

sentences.zh: 古者有左右史，此之象也。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were left and right historians—this is their image.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient courts had left and right historians; these stars mirror them.

sentences.zh: 柱史北一星曰女史，婦人之微者，主傳漏。

translations.literal: One star north of the Column Historian is called the Female Historian, a minor woman official governing the transmission of clepsydra marks.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Column Historian is the Female Historian, a minor female officer in charge of timekeeping.

sentences.zh: 故漢有侍史。

translations.literal: Hence the Han had attendant historians.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Han dynasty maintained attendant historians.

sentences.zh: 傳舍九星在華蓋上，近河，賓客之館，主胡人入中國。

translations.literal: Nine Transfer Lodging stars lie above the Canopy near the river—the guest house governing northern tribes entering China.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Transfer Lodging stars above the Canopy by the river mark the guest lodge for tribes entering China.

sentences.zh: 客星守之，備奸使，亦曰胡兵起。

translations.literal: If a guest star lodges there, guard against treacherous envoys; it also means northern armies rise.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star lingers there, prepare for spies—and northern armies may rise.

sentences.zh: 傳舍南河中五星曰造父，御官也，一曰司馬，或曰伯樂。

translations.literal: Five stars in the river south of Transfer Lodging are called Zaofu, eunuch officials; also called Sima, or sometimes Bo Le.
translations.idiomatic: Five stars south in the river are Zaofu, overseers of the imperial stud—also Sima or Bo Le.

sentences.zh: 星亡，馬大貴。

translations.literal: If a star disappears, horses become greatly prized.
translations.idiomatic: When the star vanishes, horses fetch high prices.

sentences.zh: 西河中九星如鉤狀，曰鉤星，伸則地動。

translations.literal: Nine stars in the western river form a hook shape, called Hook Star; when stretched straight, the earth quakes.
translations.idiomatic: Nine hook-shaped stars in the western river are Hook Star; if they straighten, the earth trembles.

sentences.zh: 天一一星，在紫宮門右星南，天帝之神也，主戰鬭，知人吉凶者也。

translations.literal: Heaven One, one star south of the right gate star of the Purple Palace, is the god of the Celestial Emperor, governing battle and knowing human fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven One lies south of the Purple Palace gate; the Celestial Emperor's god presides over war and reads human fates.

sentences.zh: 太一一星，在天一南，相近，亦天帝神也，主使十六神，知風雨水旱，兵革饑饉，疾疫災害所生之國也。

translations.literal: Supreme One, one star south of Heaven One and near it, is also the Celestial Emperor's god, commanding sixteen spirits and knowing which lands suffer wind, rain, flood, drought, war, famine, plague, and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme One, close south of Heaven One, commands sixteen spirits and reveals which countries face storms, drought, war, famine, and plague.

sentences.zh: 紫宮垣十五星，其西蕃七，東蕃八，在北斗北。

translations.literal: The Purple Palace ramparts are fifteen stars—seven in the western bastion and eight in the eastern—north of the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen rampart stars of the Purple Palace, seven west and eight east, lie north of the Northern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 一曰紫微，太帝之坐也，天子之常居也，主命，主度也。

translations.literal: Also called Purple Subtlety—the Great Emperor's seat, the Son of Heaven's regular residence; it governs fate and degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Also Purple Subtlety: the Great Emperor's throne and the Son of Heaven's dwelling, governing mandate and celestial degrees.

sentences.zh: 一曰長垣，一曰天營，一曰旗星，為蕃衛，備蕃臣也。

translations.literal: Also called Long Rampart, Celestial Camp, and Banner Stars; they are bastion guards, preparing frontier ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Also Long Rampart, Celestial Camp, and Banner Stars—bastion guards for frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 宮闕兵起，旗星直，天子出，自將宮中兵。

translations.literal: When palace troops rise, if Banner Stars stand straight, the Son of Heaven goes out and personally leads the palace armies.
translations.idiomatic: When palace armies mobilize and Banner Stars align straight, the Son of Heaven leads the palace troops himself.

sentences.zh: 東垣下五星曰天柱，建政教，懸圖法之所也。

translations.literal: Five stars beneath the eastern rampart are called the Heavenly Pillar, where governance and law charts are displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Five stars under the eastern wall are the Heavenly Pillar, displaying governance and legal charts.

sentences.zh: 常以朔望日懸禁令於天柱，以示百司。

translations.literal: On new and full moon days proclamations are hung on the Heavenly Pillar to show all offices.
translations.idiomatic: At new and full moons edicts are posted on the Heavenly Pillar for all departments.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》以正歲之月，懸法象魏，此之類也。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou says that in the first month of the year laws are hung at the symbolic watchtower—this is of that kind.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou hangs laws at the symbolic tower in the first month—this follows that practice.

sentences.zh: 門內東南維五星曰尚書，主納言，夙夜諮謀，龍作納言，此之象也。

translations.literal: Five stars at the inner southeast corner are called the Imperial Secretariat, governing memorials; night and day consulting—"Dragon rises as memorial officer" images this.
translations.idiomatic: Five stars at the inner southeast are the Imperial Secretariat, receiving memorials and advising day and night.

sentences.zh: 尚書西二星曰陰德、陽德，主周急振無。

translations.literal: Two stars west of the Secretariat are called Yin Virtue and Yang Virtue; they govern urgent relief and aid to the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Secretariat are Yin Virtue and Yang Virtue, overseeing emergency relief.

sentences.zh: 宮門左星內二星曰大理，主平刑斷獄也。

translations.literal: Two stars within the left gate star are called the Grand Judge, governing fair punishment and trials.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the left gate are the Grand Judge stars, adjudicating punishment and lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 門外六星曰天床，主寢舍，解息燕休。

translations.literal: Six stars outside the gate are called the Celestial Bed, governing sleeping quarters, rest, and leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Six stars outside the gate are the Celestial Bed, governing rest and repose.

sentences.zh: 西南角外二星曰內廚，主六宮之飲食，主後夫人與太子宴飲。

translations.literal: Two stars outside the southwest corner are called the Inner Kitchen, governing food of the six palaces and feasts of the empress and Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the southwest corner, the Inner Kitchen oversees palace food and royal feasts.

sentences.zh: 東北維外六星曰天廚，主盛饌。

translations.literal: Six stars outside the northeast corner are called the Celestial Kitchen, storing prepared dishes.
translations.idiomatic: Six stars beyond the northeast corner are the Celestial Kitchen, holding banquet fare.

sentences.zh: 北斗七星，輔一星在太微北，七政之樞機，陰陽之元本也，故運乎天中，而臨制四方，以建四時而均五行也。

translations.literal: The Northern Dipper is seven stars; an Assistant Star lies north of the Supreme Palace—the pivot mechanism of the seven regulators and root of yin and yang; it turns at Heaven's center, overseeing the four quarters, establishing seasons and balancing the five phases.
translations.idiomatic: Seven stars of the Northern Dipper, with an Assistant north of the Supreme Palace, pivot the seven regulators and yin-yang, turning at Heaven's center to rule the four quarters and seasons.

sentences.zh: 魁四星為〔璣，杓三星為玉衡。

translations.literal: The four stars of the bowl are Ji; the three stars of the handle are Jade Balance.
translations.idiomatic: The bowl's four stars are Ji; the handle's three are Jade Balance.

sentences.zh: 又象號令之主，又為帝車，取乎運動之義也。

translations.literal: It also images the master of commands, and also the imperial chariot—taking the meaning of motion.
translations.idiomatic: It also represents the commander of edicts and the imperial chariot—in motion.

sentences.zh: 又魁第一星曰天樞，二曰璇，三曰璣，四曰權，五曰玉衡，六曰開陽，七曰搖光。

translations.literal: The first star of the bowl is called Celestial Pivot; second Xuan; third Ji; fourth Quan; fifth Jade Balance; sixth Kaiyang; seventh Yaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: The bowl stars are Celestial Pivot, Xuan, Ji, Quan; the handle stars Jade Balance, Kaiyang, Yaoguang.

sentences.zh: 一至四為魁，五至七為杓。

translations.literal: The first through fourth form the bowl; the fifth through seventh form the handle.
translations.idiomatic: Stars one to four are the bowl; five to seven the handle.

sentences.zh: 樞為天，璇為地，璣為人，權為時，玉衡為音，開陽為律，搖光為星。

translations.literal: Pivot is Heaven, Xuan is Earth, Ji is the human, Quan is time, Jade Balance is pitch, Kaiyang is measure, Yaoguang is the stars.
translations.idiomatic: Pivot stands for Heaven, Xuan for Earth, Ji for humanity, Quan for season, Jade Balance for pitch, Kaiyang for measure, Yaoguang for stars.

sentences.zh: 石氏云：「第一曰正星，主陽德，天子之象也。

translations.literal: Master Shi says: "The first is called the Correct Star; it governs yang virtue and images the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Master Shi says: "The first is the Correct Star, governing yang virtue—the Son of Heaven's image."

sentences.zh: 二曰法星，主陰刑，女主之位也。

translations.literal: The second is the Law Star; it governs yin punishment and is the empress's position.
translations.idiomatic: The second is the Law Star, governing yin punishment—the empress's seat.

sentences.zh: 三曰令星，主禍害也。

translations.literal: The third is the Command Star; it governs calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The third is the Command Star, governing disaster.

sentences.zh: 四曰伐星，主天理，伐無道。

translations.literal: The fourth is the Punitive Star; it governs Heaven's principle and punishes the lawless.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth is the Punitive Star, upholding Heaven's justice against the lawless.

sentences.zh: 五曰殺星，主中央，助四旁，殺有罪。

translations.literal: The fifth is the Killing Star; it governs the center, assists the four sides, and kills the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth is the Killing Star, at the center aiding the four quarters to execute the guilty.

sentences.zh: 六曰危星，主天倉五穀。

translations.literal: The sixth is the Danger Star; it governs Heaven's granary of the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth is the Danger Star, governing Heaven's storehouse of grain.

sentences.zh: 七曰部星，亦曰應星，主兵。

translations.literal: The seventh is the Department Star, also called the Responding Star; it governs war.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh is the Department or Responding Star, governing warfare.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「一主天，二主地，三主火，四主水，五主土，六主木，七主金。

translations.literal: " It also says: "The first governs Heaven, the second Earth, the third Fire, the fourth Water, the fifth Earth, the sixth Wood, the seventh Metal."
translations.idiomatic: It also states: "The first governs Heaven, the second Earth, the third Fire, the fourth Water, the fifth Earth, the sixth Wood, the seventh Metal."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「一主秦，二主楚，三主樑，四主吳，五主趙，六主燕，七主齊。

translations.literal: " It also says: "The first governs Qin, the second Chu, the third Liang, the fourth Wu, the fifth Zhao, the sixth Yan, the seventh Qi."
translations.idiomatic: It also states: "The first governs Qin, the second Chu, the third Liang, the fourth Wu, the fifth Zhao, the sixth Yan, the seventh Qi."

sentences.zh: 魁中四星，為貴人之牢，曰天理也。

translations.literal: The four stars within the bowl are the nobleman's prison, called Heavenly Principle.
translations.idiomatic: Four stars in the bowl form the nobles' prison—the Heavenly Principle.

sentences.zh: 輔星傅乎開陽，所以佐斗成功也。

translations.literal: The Assistant Star adjoins Kaiyang to help the Dipper succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The Assistant Star lies by Kaiyang, aiding the Dipper's success.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「主危正，矯不平。

translations.literal: " It also says: "It governs danger and correction, rectifying imbalance."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "It governs danger and correction, straightening what is crooked."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「丞相之象也。

translations.literal: " It also says: "It is the image of the Chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "It images the Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 」七政星明，其國昌。

translations.literal: When the seven regulator stars are bright, the state flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: Bright seven regulator stars mean a flourishing realm.

sentences.zh: 不明，國殃。

translations.literal: When dim, the state suffers disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When they fade, the state faces calamity.

sentences.zh: 斗旁欲多星則安，斗中少星則人恐上，天下多訟法者。

translations.literal: Many stars beside the Dipper mean peace; few stars within mean people fear the ruler and lawsuits multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Many companion stars bring peace; few within the Dipper mean popular fear and many lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 無星二十日。

translations.literal: Twenty days without stars.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days with no stars visible.

sentences.zh: 有輔星明而斗不明，臣強主弱。

translations.literal: If the Assistant is bright and the Dipper dim, ministers are strong and the ruler weak.
translations.idiomatic: A bright Assistant with a dim Dipper means strong ministers and a weak ruler.

sentences.zh: 半明輔不明，主強臣弱也。

translations.literal: If half bright and the Assistant dim, the ruler is strong and ministers weak.
translations.idiomatic: Half brightness with a dim Assistant means a strong ruler and weak ministers.

sentences.zh: 杓南三星及魁第一星，皆曰三公，宣德化，調七政，和陰陽之官也。

translations.literal: The three stars south of the handle and the first star of the bowl are all called the Three Dukes—officials who spread virtue, regulate the seven regulators, and harmonize yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: The handle's southern three stars and the bowl's first star are the Three Dukes, spreading virtue and harmonizing yin-yang.

sentences.zh: 文昌六星，在北斗魁前，天之六府也，主集計天道。

translations.literal: Literary Glory is six stars before the Northern Dipper bowl—Heaven's six treasuries, tallying Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Six Literary Glory stars before the Dipper bowl are Heaven's six treasuries, accounting Heaven's order.

sentences.zh: 一曰上將，大將建威武。

translations.literal: The first is the supreme general—the great general establishing martial awe.
translations.idiomatic: First: the supreme general, the great commander establishing martial majesty.

sentences.zh: 二曰次將，尚書正左右。

translations.literal: The second is the deputy general—the Secretariat correcting left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Second: the deputy general, the Secretariat correcting left and right.

sentences.zh: 三曰貴相，太常理文緒。

translations.literal: The third is the honored minister—the Grand Steward managing literary threads.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the honored minister, the Grand Steward overseeing documents.

sentences.zh: 四曰司祿、司中，司隸賞功進。

translations.literal: The fourth is Director of Emolument and Director of the Center; Director of Inspection rewards merit and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: Directors of Emolument and the Center; the Inspector rewards achievement.

sentences.zh: 五曰司命、司怪，太史主滅咎。

translations.literal: The fifth is Director of Fate and Director of Omens; the Grand Historian extinguishes blame.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: Directors of Fate and Omens; the Grand Historian removes fault.

sentences.zh: 六曰司寇，大理佐理寶。

translations.literal: The sixth is Director of Punishment; the Grand Judge assists in managing treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: Director of Punishment; the Grand Judge aids in managing treasures.

sentences.zh: 所謂一者，起北斗魁前，近內階者也。

translations.literal: What is called the first rises before the Northern Dipper bowl, near the Inner Steps.
translations.idiomatic: The first begins before the Dipper bowl, near the Inner Steps.

sentences.zh: 明潤，大小齊，天瑞臻。

translations.literal: Bright and lustrous, sizes even—Heaven's auspice arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When bright, moist, and evenly sized, Heaven sends auspicious signs.

sentences.zh: 文昌北六星曰內階，天皇之陛也。

translations.literal: Six stars north of Literary Glory are called the Inner Steps—the stairway of the Celestial Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Six stars north of Literary Glory are the Inner Steps, the Celestial Sovereign's stair.

sentences.zh: 相一星在北斗南。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Star is south of the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor Star lies south of the Northern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 相者總領百司而掌邦教，以佐帝王，安邦國，集眾事也。

translations.literal: The chancellor oversees all offices and governs state instruction, assisting the emperor, stabilizing the realm, and gathering all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor Star represents one who leads all offices, teaches the state, aids the emperor, and gathers affairs.

sentences.zh: 其明吉。

translations.literal: When bright, auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Brightness brings good fortune.

sentences.zh: 太陽守一星，在相西，大將大臣之象也，主戒不虞，設武備也。

translations.literal: Taiyang Shou, one star west of the Chancellor, images great generals and high ministers; it governs guarding against the unexpected and establishing military readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyang Shou west of the Chancellor images great commanders, guarding against surprise and keeping arms ready.

sentences.zh: 非其常，兵起。

translations.literal: When not as usual, war rises.
translations.idiomatic: When abnormal, armies mobilize.

sentences.zh: 西北四星曰勢。

translations.literal: Four stars in the northwest are called Power.
translations.idiomatic: Four northwestern stars are Power.

sentences.zh: 勢，腐刑人也。

translations.literal: Power—corrupt punishers.
translations.idiomatic: Power represents corrupt executioners.

sentences.zh: 天牢六星在北斗魁下，貴人之牢也，主愆過，禁暴淫。

translations.literal: Six Celestial Prison stars lie beneath the Northern Dipper bowl—the nobles' prison; they govern transgressions and restrain violence and licentiousness.
translations.idiomatic: Six Celestial Prison stars under the Dipper bowl imprison nobles, governing faults and restraining violence.

sentences.zh: 太微，天子庭也，五帝之坐也，亦十二諸侯府也。

translations.literal: The Supreme Palace is the Son of Heaven's court, the seats of the Five Emperors, and also the twelve feudal lords' offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Palace is the imperial court, seat of the Five Emperors and twelve feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 其外蕃，九卿也。

translations.literal: Its outer bastion is the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Its outer bastion represents the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 一曰太微為衡。

translations.literal: Also called: the Supreme Palace is the balance.
translations.idiomatic: It is also said the Supreme Palace is the balance.

sentences.zh: 衡，主平也。

translations.literal: The balance governs fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The balance oversees equity.

sentences.zh: 又為天庭，理法平辭，監升授德，列宿受符，諸神考節，舒情稽疑也。

translations.literal: It is also the celestial court—adjudicating law evenly, overseeing promotion and virtue, constellations receiving tokens, deities examining nodes, expressing feelings and investigating doubts.
translations.idiomatic: It is Heaven's court: fair law, promotion of virtue, tokens to stars, gods reviewing seasons, probing doubts.

sentences.zh: 南蕃中二星間曰端門。

translations.literal: Between the two central stars of the southern bastion is the Central Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The southern bastion's two central stars form the Central Gate.

sentences.zh: 東曰左執法，廷尉之象也。

translations.literal: East is the Left Enforcer—the image of the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: To the east is the Left Enforcer, imaging the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 西曰右執法，御史大夫之象也。

translations.literal: West is the Right Enforcer—the image of the Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: To the west is the Right Enforcer, imaging the Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 執法，所以舉刺凶奸者也。

translations.literal: The enforcers expose and impeach villains.
translations.idiomatic: Enforcers impeach the wicked.

sentences.zh: 左執法之東，左掖門也。

translations.literal: East of the Left Enforcer is the Left Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Left Enforcer lies the Left Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 右執法之西，右掖門也。

translations.literal: West of the Right Enforcer is the Right Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Right Enforcer lies the Right Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 東蕃四星，南第一曰上相，其北東太陽門也。

translations.literal: Four stars of the eastern bastion: the southern first is the chief minister; north of it is the Eastern Sun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern bastion: southern first is chief minister; its north is the Eastern Sun Gate.

sentences.zh: 第二星曰次相，其北中華東門也。

translations.literal: The second star is the deputy minister; north of it is the Central East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Second is deputy minister; north is the Central East Gate.

sentences.zh: 第三星曰次將，其北東太陰門也。

translations.literal: The third star is the deputy general; north of it is the Eastern Moon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Third is deputy general; north is the Eastern Moon Gate.

sentences.zh: 第四星曰上將。

translations.literal: The fourth star is the supreme general.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth is the supreme general.

sentences.zh: 所謂四輔也。

translations.literal: These are called the Four Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: These are the Four Assistants.

sentences.zh: 西蕃四星：南第一星曰上將，其北西太陽門也。

translations.literal: Four stars of the western bastion: the southern first star is the supreme general; north of it is the Western Sun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Western bastion: southern first is supreme general; north is the Western Sun Gate.

sentences.zh: 第二星曰次將，其北中華西門也。

translations.literal: The second star is the deputy general; north of it is the Central West Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Second is deputy general; north is the Central West Gate.

sentences.zh: 第三曰次相，其北西太陰門也。

translations.literal: The third is the deputy minister; north of it is the Western Moon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Third is deputy minister; north is the Western Moon Gate.

sentences.zh: 第四星曰上相。

translations.literal: The fourth star is the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth is the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 亦四輔也。

translations.literal: These are also the Four Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: These too are the Four Assistants.

sentences.zh: 東西蕃有芒及搖動者，諸侯謀天子也。

translations.literal: If the eastern and western bastions show rays or wavering, feudal lords plot against the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Rays or motion in east and west bastions mean lords plot against the throne.

sentences.zh: 執法移則刑罰尤急。

translations.literal: If the enforcers shift, punishments become especially harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Shifting enforcers bring especially harsh punishments.

sentences.zh: 月、五星所犯中坐，成刑。

translations.literal: If the moon or five planets strike the central seat, punishment is executed.
translations.idiomatic: Moon or five planets hitting the central seat bring execution.

sentences.zh: 月、五星入太微軌道，吉。

translations.literal: If the moon or five planets enter the Supreme Palace orbit, auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Moon or five planets entering the Supreme Palace orbit are auspicious.

sentences.zh: 西南角外三星曰明堂，天子布政之宮也。

translations.literal: Three stars outside the southwest corner are called the Bright Hall—the Son of Heaven's palace of promulgating government.
translations.idiomatic: Three stars beyond the southwest corner are the Bright Hall, where the Son of Heaven promulgates policy.

sentences.zh: 明堂西三星曰靈臺，觀臺也。

translations.literal: Three stars west of the Bright Hall are called the Spirit Terrace—the observation tower.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Bright Hall are three Spirit Terrace stars, the observation tower.

sentences.zh: 主觀雲物，察符瑞，候災變也。

translations.literal: It governs observing clouds and phenomena, inspecting auspicious tokens, and watching for disasters and changes.
translations.idiomatic: It oversees cloud signs, auspicious portents, and calamities.

sentences.zh: 左執法東北一星曰謁者，主贊賓客也。

translations.literal: One star northeast of the Left Enforcer is called the Usher; it receives guests.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast of the Left Enforcer is the Usher, receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 謁者東北三星曰三公內坐，朝會之所居也。

translations.literal: Three stars northeast of the Usher are called the Inner Seats of the Three Dukes—where court assembly dwells.
translations.idiomatic: Three stars northeast of the Usher are the Inner Three Dukes' seats for court assembly.

sentences.zh: 三公北三星曰九卿內坐，主治萬事。

translations.literal: Three stars north of the Three Dukes are called the Inner Seats of the Nine Ministers, governing all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Three Dukes are the Inner Nine Ministers, managing all business.

sentences.zh: 九卿西五星曰內五諸侯，內侍天子，不之國者也。

translations.literal: Five stars west of the Nine Ministers are called the Inner Five Feudal Lords—attending the Son of Heaven within and not going to their states.
translations.idiomatic: Five stars west of the Nine Ministers are Inner Feudal Lords who attend court and do not rule abroad.

sentences.zh: 辟雍之禮得，則太微諸侯明。

translations.literal: When the Piyong rites are fulfilled, the Supreme Palace feudal lords shine.
translations.idiomatic: When Piyong rites are correct, the Supreme Palace lords' stars are bright.

sentences.zh: 黃帝坐一星，在太微中，含樞紐之神也。

translations.literal: One star, the Seat of the Yellow Emperor, is within the Supreme Palace—the spirit containing pivot and hub.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Supreme Palace is the Yellow Emperor's Seat, spirit of pivot and hub.

sentences.zh: 天子動得天度，止得地意，從容中道，則太微五帝坐明，坐以光。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven moves attaining Heaven's measure and Earth's intent, at ease on the middle Way, the Five Emperors' seats in the Supreme Palace shine bright.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler attains Heaven's measure and Earth's intent along the middle Way, the Five Emperors' seats blaze bright.

sentences.zh: 黃帝坐不明，人主求賢士以輔法，不然則奪勢。

translations.literal: If the Yellow Emperor's Seat is dim, the ruler seeks worthy men to assist the law; otherwise he loses power.
translations.idiomatic: A dim Yellow Emperor's Seat makes the ruler seek worthy aides—or lose power.

sentences.zh: 又曰太微五坐小弱青黑，天子國亡。

translations.literal: It is also said: if the Supreme Palace's five seats are small, weak, and blackish, the Son of Heaven's state perishes.
translations.idiomatic: If the five Supreme Palace seats are small, weak, and dark, the dynasty falls.

sentences.zh: 四帝坐四星，四星夾黃帝坐。

translations.literal: Four stars of the Four Emperors' Seats flank the Yellow Emperor's Seat.
translations.idiomatic: Four Emperors' Seat stars flank the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 東方星，蒼帝靈威仰之神也。

translations.literal: The eastern star is the god Lingweiyang of the Green Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern star is Green Emperor Lingweiyang.

sentences.zh: 南方星，赤帝熛怒之神也。

translations.literal: The southern star is the god Biaonu of the Red Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The southern star is Red Emperor Biaonu.

sentences.zh: 西方星，白帝招距之神也。

translations.literal: The western star is the god Zhaoju of the White Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The western star is White Emperor Zhaoju.

sentences.zh: 北方星，黑帝葉光紀之神也。

translations.literal: The northern star is the god Yeguangji of the Black Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The northern star is Black Emperor Yeguangji.

sentences.zh: 五帝坐北一星曰太子，帝儲也。

translations.literal: One star north of the Five Emperors' Seats is called the Heir Apparent—the imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Five Emperors' Seats is the Heir Apparent star.

sentences.zh: 太子北一星曰從官，侍臣也。

translations.literal: One star north of the Heir Apparent is called the Attendant Official—attendant ministers.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Heir Apparent is the Attendant Official.

sentences.zh: 帝坐東北一星曰幸臣。

translations.literal: One star northeast of the imperial seat is called the Favored Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast of the throne is the Favored Minister star.

sentences.zh: 屏四星在端門之內，近右執法。

translations.literal: Four Screen stars are within the Central Gate, near the Right Enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Four Screen stars inside the Central Gate screen the court near the Right Enforcer.

sentences.zh: 屏，所以壅蔽帝庭也。

translations.literal: The Screen blocks and shelters the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: The Screen shields the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 執法主刺舉，臣尊敬君上，則星光明潤澤。

translations.literal: The enforcer governs impeachment; when ministers respect the ruler, the stars are bright and lustrous.
translations.idiomatic: Enforcers impeach; when ministers revere the ruler, their stars shine moist and bright.

sentences.zh: 郎位十五星，在帝坐東北，一曰依烏，郎位也。

translations.literal: Fifteen Officer Position stars are northeast of the imperial seat; also called Dependent Crow—the officer positions.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen Officer Position stars northeast of the throne are the attendant corps.

sentences.zh: 周官之元士，漢官之光祿、中散、諫議、議郎、三署郎中，是其職也。

translations.literal: Chief clerks of the Zhou offices; Palace Attendant, Palace Secretary, Remonstrance Counselor, Consultation Gentleman, and Attendants of the Three Bureaus of Han—these are their duties.
translations.idiomatic: They image Zhou chief clerks and Han attendants, counselors, and bureau gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 或曰今之尚書也。

translations.literal: Or it is said: today's Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Some say they represent today's Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 郎位主衛守也。

translations.literal: Officer Positions govern guard and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Officer Positions oversee guard duty.

sentences.zh: 其星明，大臣有劫主。

translations.literal: When their stars are bright, high ministers seize the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Officer Position stars mean ministers seize the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 又曰客犯上。

translations.literal: It is also said: a guest star strikes the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star striking them also menaces the ruler.

sentences.zh: 其星不具，後死，幸臣誅。

translations.literal: If the stars are incomplete, the empress dies and favored ministers are executed.
translations.idiomatic: Incomplete stars mean the empress dies and favorites are executed.

sentences.zh: 客星入之，大臣為亂。

translations.literal: If a guest star enters, high ministers rebel.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star entering brings ministerial rebellion.

sentences.zh: 郎將一星在郎位北，主閱具，所以為武備也。

translations.literal: One Commandant of Attendants star is north of Officer Positions; it reviews equipment—the military readiness.
translations.idiomatic: North of Officer Positions is the Commandant of Attendants, reviewing arms and equipment.

sentences.zh: 武賁一星，在太微西蕃北，下臺南，靜室旄頭之騎官也。

translations.literal: One Elite Guard star is north of the Supreme Palace's western bastion, south of the Lower Terrace—cavalry of the Quiet Chamber and Maotou.
translations.idiomatic: An Elite Guard star north of the western bastion, south of the Lower Terrace, images Maotou cavalry.

sentences.zh: 常陳七星，如畢狀，在帝坐北，天子宿衛武賁之土，以設強毅也。

translations.literal: Constant Array is seven stars shaped like Net, north of the imperial seat—the Son of Heaven's night guard of elite warriors, establishing firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Seven Net-shaped Constant Array stars north of the throne are the emperor's elite night guard.

sentences.zh: 星搖動，天子自出，明則武兵用，微則武兵弱。

translations.literal: When the stars waver, the Son of Heaven goes out himself; when bright, military force is used; when faint, military force weakens.
translations.idiomatic: Wavering stars mean the emperor leads in person; brightness brings war; faintness weakens arms.

sentences.zh: 三台六星，兩兩而居，起文昌，列招搖、太微。

translations.literal: Three Terraces are six stars dwelling in pairs, rising from Literary Glory and arrayed toward Swaying Spear and the Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Six Three Terrace stars in pairs rise from Literary Glory toward Swaying Spear and the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 一曰天柱，三公之位也。

translations.literal: Also called the Heavenly Pillar—the position of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Also the Heavenly Pillar—the Three Dukes' place.

sentences.zh: 在天曰三台，主開德宣符也。

translations.literal: In Heaven called Three Terraces; it governs opening virtue and proclaiming tokens.
translations.idiomatic: In Heaven they are the Three Terraces, opening virtue and proclaiming mandates.

sentences.zh: 西近文昌二星曰上臺，為司命，主壽。

translations.literal: Two stars west near Literary Glory are called the Upper Terrace—Director of Fate, governing longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Two stars west near Literary Glory are the Upper Terrace, Director of Fate for longevity.

sentences.zh: 次二星曰中台，為司中，主宗。

translations.literal: The next two stars are the Middle Terrace—Director of the Center, governing the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Next two are the Middle Terrace, Director of the Center for the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 東二星曰下臺，為司祿，主兵，所以昭德塞違也。

translations.literal: Two stars east are the Lower Terrace—Director of Emolument, governing war—therefore displaying virtue and blocking transgression.
translations.idiomatic: Two eastern stars are the Lower Terrace, Director of Emolument for war—displaying virtue, blocking wrong.

sentences.zh: 又曰三台為天階，太一躡以上下。

translations.literal: It is also said the Three Terraces are the Celestial Stairway; the Supreme One treads up and down.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Terraces are also Heaven's stairway where the Supreme One treads.

sentences.zh: 一曰泰階，上星為天子，下星為女主；

translations.literal: Also called the Grand Stairway: the upper star is the Son of Heaven, the lower the empress;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Stairway's upper star is the Son of Heaven, lower the empress;

sentences.zh: 中階，上星為諸侯三公，下星為卿大夫；

translations.literal: middle stair: upper stars are feudal lords and Three Dukes, lower are ministers and grand masters;
translations.idiomatic: middle stair: upper feudal lords and Three Dukes, lower ministers and grand masters;

sentences.zh: 下階，上星為士，下星為庶人。

translations.literal: lower stair: upper are gentlemen, lower the common people.
translations.idiomatic: lower stair: upper gentlemen, lower commoners.

sentences.zh: 所以和陰陽而理萬物也。

translations.literal: Thus yin and yang are harmonized and the myriad things governed.
translations.idiomatic: They harmonize yin-yang and govern the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 其星有變，各以所主占人。

translations.literal: When their stars change, each is interpreted by what it governs regarding people.
translations.idiomatic: Star changes are read by what each governs among people.

sentences.zh: 君臣和集，如其常度。

translations.literal: When ruler and ministers harmonize according to their usual measure.
translations.idiomatic: When ruler and ministers accord with their proper stations.

sentences.zh: 南四星曰內平，近職執法平罪之官也。

translations.literal: Four southern stars are called Inner Peace—officials of near rank who judge crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Four southern stars are Inner Peace, nearby judges of crime.

sentences.zh: 中台之北一星曰大尊，貴戚也。

translations.literal: One star north of the Middle Terrace is called Great Honored—honored kin.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Middle Terrace is Great Honored, imaging noble kin.

sentences.zh: 下臺南一星曰武賁，衛官也。

translations.literal: One star south of the Lower Terrace is called Elite Guard—guard officials.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Lower Terrace is Elite Guard, guard officers.

sentences.zh: 攝提六星，直斗杓之南，主建時節，伺禨祥。

translations.literal: Sheti is six stars straight south of the Dipper handle, governing establishment of seasonal nodes and watching omens.
translations.idiomatic: Six Sheti stars south of the handle establish seasons and watch omens.

sentences.zh: 攝提為楯，以夾擁帝席也，主九卿。

translations.literal: Sheti is a shield embracing the Imperial Mat, governing the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti shields the Imperial Mat and governs the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 明大，三公恣，客星入之，聖人受制。

translations.literal: When bright and large, the Three Dukes act willfully; if a guest star enters, the sage is constrained.
translations.idiomatic: Great brightness lets the Three Dukes run wild; a guest star entering constrains the sage.

sentences.zh: 西三星曰周鼎，主流亡。

translations.literal: Three western stars are called the Zhou Cauldrons—they govern dynastic fall.
translations.idiomatic: Three western stars are Zhou Cauldrons, governing dynastic collapse.

sentences.zh: 大角一星，在攝提間。

translations.literal: Great Horn is one star between Sheti stars.
translations.idiomatic: Great Horn is one star amid Sheti.

sentences.zh: 大角者，天王座也。

translations.literal: Great Horn is the Heavenly King's throne.
translations.idiomatic: Great Horn is the throne of the Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 又為天棟，正經紀。

translations.literal: It is also the Heavenly Ridgepole, rectifying governance.
translations.idiomatic: It is also Heaven's ridgepole, setting governance straight.

sentences.zh: 北三星曰帝席，主宴獻酬酢。

translations.literal: Three northern stars are called the Imperial Mat, governing feasts and toasts.
translations.idiomatic: Three northern stars are the Imperial Mat for feasts and toasts.

sentences.zh: 梗河三星，在大角北。

translations.literal: Geng River is three stars north of Great Horn.
translations.idiomatic: Three Geng River stars lie north of Great Horn.

sentences.zh: 梗河者，天矛也。

translations.literal: Geng River is the Celestial Spear.
translations.idiomatic: Geng River is the Celestial Spear.

sentences.zh: 一曰天鋒，主胡兵。

translations.literal: Also called the Celestial Point; it governs northern armies.
translations.idiomatic: Also the Celestial Point, governing northern armies.

sentences.zh: 又為喪，故其變動應以兵喪也。

translations.literal: It also governs mourning; thus its changes respond with war and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: It also governs funerals; its changes bring war and mourning.

sentences.zh: 星亡，其國有兵謀。

translations.literal: If a star vanishes, that state has military plotting.
translations.idiomatic: A vanished star means military plotting in that state.

sentences.zh: 招搖一星在其北，一曰矛楯，主胡兵。

translations.literal: Swaying Spear is one star north of it; also called spear and shield; it governs northern armies.
translations.idiomatic: Swaying Spear north of it is spear-and-shield, governing northern armies.

sentences.zh: 占與梗河略相類也。

translations.literal: Its interpretation is broadly similar to Geng River.
translations.idiomatic: Its omens resemble Geng River's.

sentences.zh: 招搖與北斗杓間曰天庫。

translations.literal: Between Swaying Spear and the Dipper handle is called the Celestial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Between Swaying Spear and the handle is the Celestial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 星去其所，則有庫開之祥也。

translations.literal: When stars leave their places, there is the omen of the storehouse opening.
translations.idiomatic: Stars leaving their places mean the storehouse opens—auspicious.

sentences.zh: 招搖欲與棟星、梗河、北斗相應，則胡常來受命於中國。

translations.literal: Swaying Spear should respond with Ridgepole Star, Geng River, and the Northern Dipper—then the Hu regularly receive mandate from China.
translations.idiomatic: When Swaying Spear aligns with Ridgepole, Geng River, and the Dipper, northern tribes accept China's mandate.

sentences.zh: 招搖明而不正，胡不受命。

translations.literal: If Swaying Spear is bright but not upright, the Hu do not receive mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Bright but crooked Swaying Spear means the Hu reject mandate.

sentences.zh: 玄戈二星，在招搖北。

translations.literal: Dark Halberd is two stars north of Swaying Spear.
translations.idiomatic: Two Dark Halberd stars lie north of Swaying Spear.

sentences.zh: 玄戈所主，與招搖同。

translations.literal: What Dark Halberd governs is the same as Swaying Spear.
translations.idiomatic: Dark Halberd's governance matches Swaying Spear.

sentences.zh: 或云主北夷。

translations.literal: Some say it governs northern tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Some say it governs northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 客星守之，胡大敗。

translations.literal: If a guest star lodges there, the Hu suffer great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star lodging there brings great defeat to the Hu.

sentences.zh: 天槍三星，在北斗杓東。

translations.literal: Heavenly Spear is three stars east of the Dipper handle.
translations.idiomatic: Three Heavenly Spear stars lie east of the handle.

sentences.zh: 一曰天鉞，天之武備也。

translations.literal: Also called the Celestial Battle-axe—Heaven's military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: Also the Celestial Battle-axe—Heaven's martial readiness.

sentences.zh: 故在紫宮之左，所以禦難也。

translations.literal: Thus it is left of the Purple Palace to ward off danger.
translations.idiomatic: It stands left of the Purple Palace to repel peril.

sentences.zh: 女床三星，在其北，後宮御也，主女事。

translations.literal: Female Couch is three stars north of it—the inner palace attendants, governing women's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Three Female Couch stars north govern the inner palace and women's affairs.

sentences.zh: 天棓五星，在女床北，天子先驅也，主忿爭與刑罰，藏兵，亦所以禦難也。

translations.literal: Heavenly Club is five stars north of Female Couch—the Son of Heaven's vanguard; it governs strife and punishment, stores troops, and also wards off danger.
translations.idiomatic: Five Heavenly Club stars north of Female Couch are the imperial vanguard, governing strife, punishment, and stored arms.

sentences.zh: 槍棓皆以備非常也。

translations.literal: Spear and club both guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Spear and club both meet emergencies.

sentences.zh: 一星不具，國兵起。

translations.literal: If one star is incomplete, national armies rise.
translations.idiomatic: One missing star raises national armies.

sentences.zh: 東七星曰扶筐，盛桑之器，主勸蠶也。

translations.literal: Seven eastern stars are called Mulberry Basket—the vessel for mulberry, governing encouraging sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Seven eastern Mulberry Basket stars encourage sericulture.

sentences.zh: 七公七星，在招搖東，天之相也，三公之象，主七政。

translations.literal: Seven Lords are seven stars east of Swaying Spear—Heaven's ministers, the image of the Three Dukes, governing the seven regulators.
translations.idiomatic: Seven Lords east of Swaying Spear image the Three Dukes and govern the seven regulators.

sentences.zh: 貫索九星在其前，賤人之牢也。

translations.literal: Girdle Rope is nine stars before it—the prison of base people.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Girdle Rope stars before them imprison base people.

sentences.zh: 一曰連索，一曰運營，一曰天牢，主法律，禁暴強也。

translations.literal: Also called Linked Rope, Moving Camp, and Celestial Prison; it governs law and restrains violence and coercion.
translations.idiomatic: Also Linked Rope, Moving Camp, Celestial Prison—law restraining violence.

sentences.zh: 牢口一星為門，欲其開也。

translations.literal: One star at the prison mouth is the gate—they desire it open.
translations.idiomatic: The prison-mouth star is the gate—they wish it open.

sentences.zh: 九星皆明，天下獄煩。

translations.literal: When all nine stars are bright, prisons across the realm are burdened.
translations.idiomatic: All nine bright means prisons everywhere are overburdened.

sentences.zh: 七星見，小赦；

translations.literal: If seven appear, minor amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: Seven visible brings minor amnesty;

sentences.zh: 五星，大赦。

translations.literal: if five, major amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: five visible brings major amnesty.

sentences.zh: 動則斧钅質用，中空則更元。

translations.literal: If they move, axe and mace are used; if hollow within, the era changes.
translations.idiomatic: Motion brings executions; hollowness within changes the reign era.

sentences.zh: 《漢志》云十五星。

translations.literal: The Han Treatise says fifteen stars.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Treatise records fifteen stars.

sentences.zh: 天紀九星，在貫索東，九卿也。

translations.literal: Celestial Record is nine stars east of Girdle Rope—the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Celestial Record stars east of Girdle Rope are the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 九河主萬事之紀，理怨訟也。

translations.literal: Nine Rivers governs the records of all affairs and adjudicates grievances and lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Rivers records all affairs and settles lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 明則天下多辭訟，亡則政理壞，國紀亂，散絕則地震山崩。

translations.literal: When bright, lawsuits multiply across the realm; when vanished, governance fails and state order collapses; if scattered and broken, earthquakes and mountain collapses.
translations.idiomatic: Brightness brings lawsuits; vanishing ruins order; scattering brings quakes.

sentences.zh: 織女三星，在天紀東端，天女也，主果瓜絲帛珍寶也。

translations.literal: Weaving Maid is three stars at the eastern end of Celestial Record—a celestial woman governing fruits, melons, silk, brocade, and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Three Weaving Maid stars at Celestial Record's east govern produce, silk, and treasures.

sentences.zh: 王者至孝，神祇咸喜，則織女星俱明，天下和平。

translations.literal: When the king is utmost filial and spirits all rejoice, Weaving Maid stars all shine—peace across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ultimate filial piety makes Weaving Maid bright and the realm peaceful.

sentences.zh: 大星怒角，布帛貴。

translations.literal: If the great star shows angry horns, cloth and silk become expensive.
translations.idiomatic: An angry-horned great star makes cloth and silk costly.

sentences.zh: 東足四星曰漸臺，臨水之臺也。

translations.literal: Four stars of the eastern foot are called Gradual Terrace—a waterside terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Four eastern-foot stars are Gradual Terrace by the water.

sentences.zh: 主晷漏律呂之事。

translations.literal: It governs gnomon, clepsydra, and pitch-pipe affairs.
translations.idiomatic: It governs gnomon, clepsydra, and pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 西之五星曰輦道，王者嬉遊之道也，漢輦道通南、北宮象也。

translations.literal: Five western stars are called Imperial Carriage Way—the Son of Heaven's path of pleasure excursions; the Han carriage way connecting south and north palaces images this.
translations.idiomatic: Five western Carriage Way stars are the emperor's pleasure route, imaging Han's north-south palace road.

sentences.zh: 左右角間二星曰平道之官。

translations.literal: Two stars between the left and right Horn stars are called officials of the Level Way.
translations.idiomatic: Two stars between the Horns are Level Way officials.

sentences.zh: 平道西一星曰進賢，主卿相舉逸才。

translations.literal: One star west of Level Way is called Advance the Worthy—it governs ministers recommending outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: West of Level Way is Advance the Worthy, recommending talent.

sentences.zh: 角北二星曰天田。

translations.literal: Two stars north of the Horn are called Celestial Field.
translations.idiomatic: Two stars north of the Horn are Celestial Field.

sentences.zh: 亢北六星曰亢池。

translations.literal: Six stars north of Kang are called Kang Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Six Kang Pool stars lie north of Kang.

sentences.zh: 亢，舟航也；

translations.literal: Kang—boats;
translations.idiomatic: Kang means boats;

sentences.zh: 池，水也。

translations.literal: Pool—water.
translations.idiomatic: Pool means water.

sentences.zh: 主送往迎來。

translations.literal: It governs sending off and welcoming arrivals.
translations.idiomatic: It governs departures and welcomes.

sentences.zh: 氐北一星曰天乳，主甘露。

translations.literal: One star north of Di is called Celestial Milk—it governs sweet dew.
translations.idiomatic: North of Di is Celestial Milk, governing sweet dew.

sentences.zh: 房中道一星曰歲，守之，陰陽平。

translations.literal: One star in the Heart corridor is called Jupiter; if it lodges there, yin and yang are balanced.
translations.idiomatic: A Heart corridor star is Jupiter; lodging there balances yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 房西二星南北列，曰天福，主乘輿之官，若《禮》巾車、公車之政。

translations.literal: Two stars west of Heart, north and south in a row, are called Celestial Blessing—governing chariot offices, like the Rites' Chariot and Public Chariot administrations.
translations.idiomatic: Two stars west of Heart are Celestial Blessing, chariot offices of the Rites.

sentences.zh: 主祠事。

translations.literal: It governs sacrificial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: It governs sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 東咸、西咸各四星，在房、心北，日月五星之道也。

translations.literal: Eastern Salt and Western Salt are four stars each, north of Heart and Fang—the path of sun, moon, and five planets.
translations.idiomatic: Four Eastern and four Western Salt stars north of Heart and Fang mark the luminaries' path.

sentences.zh: 房之戶，所以防淫佚也。

translations.literal: The door of Fang—therefore guarding against licentiousness.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's door guards against licentiousness.

sentences.zh: 星明則吉，暗則凶。

translations.literal: When stars are bright, auspicious; when dim, inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Bright stars are lucky; dim stars unlucky.

sentences.zh: 月、五星犯守之，有陰謀。

translations.literal: If the moon or five planets invade or lodge there, secret plotting occurs.
translations.idiomatic: Moon or five planets striking there bring secret plots.

sentences.zh: 東咸西三星，南北列，曰罰星，主受金贖。
